articles.src: 2024年信阳市息县中考三模
articles.title: Do you ever feel like there’s not enough time in the day?
body: Do you ever feel like there’s not enough time in the day? That time is somehow racing away from you, and it is impossible to fit everything in. But then, you step outside into the countryside and suddenly everything seems slower, more relaxed, like time has somehow changed. It’s not just you — recent research showed nature can control our sense of time.

Richardo Correia, the researcher at the University of Finland, found that being in nature may change how we experience time and perhaps, even give us the sense of time abundance (充裕). Correia compared people’s experiences of time when they performed different types of tasks in cities and natural environments. It showed that people reported a sense of expanded time when they were in nature compared to when they were in cities. For example, a walk through the countryside felt longer than a city walk of the same distance.

It’s not just our sense of time in the moment which appears to be changed by the natural world, and it’s also our sense of the past and future. Earlier research shows that spending time in nature helps to move our focus from the immediate (目前的) moment towards our future needs. So rather than focusing on the stress of the demands (需求) on our time, nature helps us to see the bigger picture. This can help us focus on what’s important so that we meet our long-term goals. This is partly because spending time in nature appears to make us less impulsive (冲动的), enabling us to think more about future benefits instead of wanting immediate ones.

qs.stem: How might you feel when you walk in the countryside?
opts: Time is racing away from you.
There are less hours in the day.
Things seem to go at a slower speed.

ex.ev: But then, you step outside into the countryside and suddenly everything seems slower, more relaxed, like time has somehow changed.
ex.why: 走到乡下，一切好像都变慢、变轻松了。

qs.stem: In what way did Correia carry out the research?

ex.ev: Correia compared people’s experiences of time when they performed different types of tasks in cities and natural environments.
ex.why: 他比较人们在城市和在大自然里做事时对时间的感受——用的是对比的方法。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “expanded” probably mean?

ex.ev: For example, a walk through the countryside felt longer than a city walk of the same distance.
ex.why: 同样的距离，在乡下走感觉更长——expanded 是时间「变多、变长」。

qs.stem: How does nature help with our sense of the future?
opts: By reminding us of the past.

ex.ev: Earlier research shows that spending time in nature helps to move our focus from the immediate (目前的) moment towards our future needs.
ex.why: 大自然把我们的注意力从眼前转到将来的需要上——改变了我们关注的重点。

qs.stem: Which is the best title for the passage?
opts: Where our sense of time has gone.
Why we lose sense of time in nature.
How nature changes our sense of time.

ex.ev: recent research showed nature can control our sense of time.
ex.why: 全文讲大自然怎样改变我们对现在、过去和将来的时间感。

articles.src: 2024年信阳市新县中考三模
articles.title: There are lots of fun-filled ethnic (少数民族的) festivals in our country.
body: There are lots of fun-filled ethnic (少数民族的) festivals in our country. Let’s take a look at some of them.
March Fair of Bai People

The March Fair is the most important festival for the Bai people living in Dali, Yunnan. It starts from the 15th day of the 3rd lunar month and lasts about 7 days. During the festival, people in and around Dali come together for trade. What’s more, they race horses, dance to and sing traditional songs.
Torch Festival of Yi People

In Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan, Yi people celebrate the Torch (火把) Festival. It usually takes place from the 24th to the 26th day of the 6th lunar month every year. As part of the festival, every family needs to light a torch. The idea is that these torches will drive away bad luck. In the center of town, there is always a bonfire (篝火). People of all ages sing and dance around it.
Water Festival of Dai People

The Water Festival is the New Year for the Dai people living in Xishuangbanna, Yunnan. It lasts 3 days in April. During the festival, Dai people wear their festival suits to dance and throw water at each other (they believe it could bring happiness and good luck). The wetter you get, the luckier you will be.
Interested in these Chinese festivals? Go and experience them yourself.

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “it” in Paragraph 3 refer to?

ex.ev: Yi people celebrate the Torch (火把) Festival. It usually takes place from the 24th to the 26th day of the 6th lunar month every year.
ex.why: it 指前一句说的火把节：每年农历六月二十四到二十六。

qs.stem: How long does Torch Festival of Yi People last?

ex.ev: It usually takes place from the 24th to the 26th day of the 6th lunar month every year.
ex.why: 从二十四到二十六日，一共 3 天。

qs.stem: Where can you experience all the three ethnic festivals above?

ex.why: 三月街在云南大理，泼水节在云南西双版纳，火把节在云南、贵州、四川——三个节日都能在云南过。

qs.stem: Which of the following is TRUE according to the text?
opts: The Torch Festival lasts the shortest time.
Bai People often trade and draw in March Fair.
The Water Festival is the New Year for Dai people.
Yi People need to light a torch to see the road clearly.

ex.ev: The Water Festival is the New Year for the Dai people living in Xishuangbanna, Yunnan.
ex.why: 泼水节是傣族的新年。火把节和泼水节都是 3 天；三月街是做买卖，不是画画；火把是为了赶走坏运气。

qs.stem: What does the passage mainly talk about?
opts: Some ethnic clothes in our country.
Some ethnic food in our country.
Some ethnic movies in our country.
Some ethnic festivals in our country.

ex.ev: There are lots of fun-filled ethnic (少数民族的) festivals in our country.
ex.why: 第一句点题：介绍我国几个有趣的少数民族节日。

articles.src: 2024年信阳市新县中考三模
articles.title: These days, we easily feel stressed as we need to do lots of
body: These days, we easily feel stressed as we need to do lots of work every day. It’s important to know how to solve problems and find ways to relax.

We should try organizing our problems from most important to least important as well as most urgent (紧急的) to least urgent. If some problems are both important and urgent, such as studying for a next-day test, do those tasks first. Once those are done, work on things that are important but not urgent, such as preparing for the final exams. From there, we can work on problems that are less important. Organizing our work this way helps a lot in knowing what to do first and not worrying about the rest.

Sometimes we feel stressed because we are not able to complete the task by ourselves. It’s better to ask someone for help. If we stick to doing these tasks ourselves, it can make us more stressed and upset. Open your mouth bravely, and someone must give you a hand.

Still, sometimes we don’t feel relaxed even after organizing our work well. That’s okay. We can try to plan some exercise in our daily life. It doesn’t even have to be a big trip to the gym, although that surely helps. It could be something as small as walking around the neighborhood for 10 minutes. Also, we can try different activities together with our family members or friends.

We can try meditation (冥想). Again, this does not need to be anything special. Just set aside 10to 20 minutes with a timer, sit upright, close your eyes, and focus only on breathing. If other ideas come up, accept that they are there and let them fall away on their own.
By trying these steps, we will go a long way toward feeling relaxed and peaceful when finishing all of the work.

qs.stem: In which order should we organize our tasks? a. Both important and urgent tasks.                 b. Less important tasks. c. Important but not urgent tasks.                  d. Neither important nor urgent tasks.

ex.ev: If some problems are both important and urgent, such as studying for a next-day test, do those tasks first.
ex.why: 先做又重要又紧急的（a），再做重要但不紧急的（c），然后是不太重要的（b），最后是既不重要也不紧急的（d）。

qs.stem: What does Paragraph 3 tell us?
opts: Always complete the tasks by ourselves.
We can tell the truth to other people.
Try to give a helping hand to others.
We should ask for help sometimes.

ex.ev: It’s better to ask someone for help.
ex.why: 第三段讲自己完不成时，最好请别人帮忙。

qs.stem: What does the writer advise us to do to relax in Paragraph 4?
opts: Spend time organizing our work well.
Do the same activity every day.

ex.ev: It could be something as small as walking around the neighborhood for 10 minutes.
ex.why: 不一定要去健身房，在附近走 10 分钟也行——去散散步。

qs.stem: What should we do when other ideas come up during meditation?
opts: Lie down and set a timer.
Open and then close our eyes.

ex.ev: If other ideas come up, accept that they are there and let them fall away on their own.
ex.why: 冥想时有别的念头，就接受它们，让它们自己消失——不去管它们。

qs.stem: Which can be a proper title for the text?
opts: Keys to Keeping a Peaceful Mind

ex.ev: These days, we easily feel stressed as we need to do lots of work every day.
ex.why: 全文讲压力大时怎么办：排好顺序、请人帮忙、锻炼、冥想——应对压力的建议。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店市西平县中考三模
articles.title: You know that it’s important to manage money.
body: You know that it’s important to manage money. However, it’s very easy to waste money-even small buying like school things and snacks quickly adds up. This makes it harder to save up for the things you really want. What’s more, you might run out of money in this way. That’s why you need to learn how to manage your money. Here is a method suggested by experts.
To start, you need to figure out what you need, not just what you want.

Needs are the things that you require in order to live. People often mistake things that they need for things that they want. For example, you need a pair of shoes, but that doesn’t mean you need to buy a pair in the latest fashions. Or you need to eat dinner, but that doesn’t mean you need takeaway pizza-you just want it.

Wants are things that it would be nice to have, but that you can live without. Your wants will change as time passes. As a child, you might want a new bike, but when you get a bit older, you probably want a phone, new clothes, or even a car. It isn’t a good idea to spend all your money on the things you want. Because there's a risk you won't have enough money left to pay for things you need.

After knowing what you need and what you want, it’s important to try “mindful spending”. This means thinking carefully about whether you really need something right now, or whether it would be better to wait or save the money instead. Stop and think before you spend. This helps you get into a good habit of spending. You will make it much easier to manage your money when you grow up.

qs.stem: What does the underlined phrase “figure out” mean in the text?

ex.ev: To start, you need to figure out what you need, not just what you want.
ex.why: 先要弄清楚自己需要什么——figure out 就是「弄清楚、想明白」（make clear）。

qs.stem: How does the writer explain the idea of “what you need” in Paragraph 3?

ex.ev: For example, you need a pair of shoes, but that doesn’t mean you need to buy a pair in the latest fashions.
ex.why: 第三段用鞋子、晚饭两个例子说明什么是「需要」。

qs.stem: How can you try “mindful spending”?
opts: By spending money on the things you like right now.
By spending money after you have a deep thinking.
By waiting for a better time to save money.
By spending the least money and saving money.

ex.ev: This means thinking carefully about whether you really need something right now, or whether it would be better to wait or save the money instead.
ex.why: 「用心消费」就是花钱前认真想一想是不是真的需要。

qs.stem: Who is the text written for?

ex.ev: even small buying like school things and snacks quickly adds up.
ex.why: 文中说买学习用品、零食，还说长大后更容易管钱，是写给学生的。

qs.stem: What is the purpose of this text?
opts: To warn us not to waste money.
To list reasons for saving money.
To give examples of spending money.
To offer a method to manage money.

ex.ev: That’s why you need to learn how to manage your money. Here is a method suggested by experts.
ex.why: 第一段说明目的：介绍专家建议的一种管钱方法。

What do you do with your leftover (剩余的) fruit or vegetables?     16     But if you try to plant some of them, they can grow back for you to eat or enjoy! Here are four ways to grow your own plants.

Let’s start with carrots. Pour water in a plate and soak (浸泡) the carrot tops in it for two weeks. Then, plant the tops in the soil (土壤).     17     Surprisingly, they are great in salads. Or you can simply keep them as a beautiful house plant.

Growing fruit or vegetables may be easier than you think. Have a try and you'll find that it's interesting to grow some green in your life.

articles.src: 2024年信阳市平桥区中考三模
articles.title: We know that having a nice sleep is very important for a person.
body: We know that having a nice sleep is very important for a person. And people of different ages need different temperatures to sleep well. What’s the best temperature for old people to have a good sleep? A group of researchers did a study and found the results were interesting.

The key to sleeping well at night for older people could be how hot or cold their rooms are. Researchers said the best way to get a good night’s sleep was to make sure the bedroom temperature was between 20℃ and 25℃. The researchers are from Harvard University and the Hinda and Arthur Marcus Institute for Aging Research in the USA. They asked 50 people aged 65 and older to wear a sleep monitor for a year and a half. The researchers collected the information from the sleep monitors and found that the quality (质量) of sleep got worse when the room temperature was outside the 20—25℃. They also found that 20℃ was the best temperature. The lead researcher said, “Sleep comes easier and is often deeper and more restful in a cooler environment.”

The research was full of surprising information. It reported that the temperature could influence sleep as much as experiencing pain or drinking alcohol (酒) before bedtime. The researchers found a 5%—10% drop in sleep quality when the temperature was lower than 20℃ or higher than 25℃. They said poor sleep could lead to health problems. These included inability to think clearly, mood swings (情绪波动) and higher levels of stress. Other problems included an increased chance of getting diabetes and cardiovascular disease (糖尿病与心血管疾病). The researchers said people should create “a more comfortable home environment” to sleep well. They also said, “Climate change may influence the sleep quality of older adults.”

qs.stem: How does the writer lead into the topic in Paragraph 1?

ex.ev: What’s the best temperature for old people to have a good sleep?
ex.why: 第一段用一个问题引出话题：老人睡觉的最佳温度是多少？

qs.stem: What do the underlined words “a sleep monitor” mean in the text?

ex.ev: They asked 50 people aged 65 and older to wear a sleep monitor for a year and a half.
ex.why: 睡眠监测器是戴在身上、记录睡眠的设备，A 图是戴在手腕上带屏幕的手环。

qs.stem: What’s the best temperature for a good night’s sleep for the old according to the study?

ex.ev: They also found that 20℃ was the best temperature.
ex.why: 研究发现 20℃ 是最好的温度。

qs.stem: What did the researchers suggest?
opts: People should try to change the climate.
People should drink alcohol before bedtime.
People should stay in a cold environment all the time.
People should make their homes comfortable to sleep well.

ex.ev: The researchers said people should create “a more comfortable home environment” to sleep well.
ex.why: 研究人员建议营造更舒服的家居环境来睡好觉。

qs.stem: In which unit of a textbook can the text be found?

ex.ev: A group of researchers did a study and found the results were interesting.
ex.why: 讲的是一项关于温度和睡眠的科学研究，适合放在「有趣的科学」单元。

articles.src: 2024年信阳市平桥区中考三模
articles.title: If you’re a student, studying can use up your mental energy
body: If you’re a student, studying can use up your mental energy (心力) quickly. It’s hard to pay attention to your subjects for a long time.     32
Feed Your Brain

Healthy eating is one of the most important steps you can take for your well-being.     33     Studies show that those who eat healthy food are more possible to do better in tests. In other words, what you eat directly makes a difference to your ability to think and solve problems.
Exercise Often

34     Physical activities help your brain stay active and ready for everything. It, in turn, can lead to improved study abilities, problem-solving skills and creativity. Besides, doing exercise has been found to reduce stress and improve mental health.
Keep the Stress Away
Stress can greatly influence your ability to focus (集中注意力). Having tons of stress can make it difficult to deal with information. To reduce stress, it is important to take breaks properly.     35
Improve Your Social Life

A healthy social life is an important part of your success.     36     However, studies have shown that students who keep strong relationships and stay socially active can study better. Try calling a family member once a day or having a weekly dinner with friends.

opts: Good eating habits can be good for your body and mind.
Here are the ways to relax yourself and do better in studying.
Stay active, get enough rest, and take some small actions like deep breathing.
On the surface, staying with friends and family has nothing to do with scores.
Exercise is an excellent way to make your mind and body excited for a whole day.

32.ev: It’s hard to pay attention to your subjects for a long time.
32.why: 第一段说学习很耗精力，接着用 B「这里有一些放松自己、学得更好的方法」引出下面几条。

33.ev: Healthy eating is one of the most important steps you can take for your well-being.
33.why: 「喂饱大脑」讲健康饮食，A「好的饮食习惯对身体和头脑都有好处」。

34.ev: Physical activities help your brain stay active and ready for everything.
34.why: 「经常锻炼」这一段开头用 E「锻炼能让身心一整天都有活力」。

35.ev: To reduce stress, it is important to take breaks properly.
35.why: 减压要适当休息，C「保持活跃、休息够、做做深呼吸」接着给具体做法。

36.ev: However, studies have shown that students who keep strong relationships and stay socially active can study better.
36.why: 后面用 However 转折：其实社交好的学生学得更好，前面应是 D「表面上，和家人朋友在一起跟分数没关系」。

ex.why: 图里说新体系要考虑每个地区不同的需要——不同地区的环境不一样。

qs.stem: What’s this text mainly talking about?
opts: Red lines which China set to protect the environment.
The major targets of the system for managing the environment.
We should protect the environment in our daily lives.

ex.ev: Here are the highlights (亮点).
ex.why: 全文列出按区域管理环境的规定亮点。

articles.src: 2024年濮阳市中考三模
articles.title: One day, Frank was walking with his mother when they passed
body: One day, Frank was walking with his mother when they passed a pretty garden. Frank said to his mother,“Mom, these flowers are really beautiful. I want to take a closer look.”

A gardener heard that and kindly invited them into the garden. Frank’s mother thanked the man. Then she said to Frank, “I’ll take you for a walk in this garden, but remember not to make a mess of it.”
Frank nodded. He walked along the clean path, looked at the beautiful flowers, but touched nothing. He didn’t step on the grass and was careful not to let his clothes sweep the flowers.

The gardener was very pleased with Frank. He showed him the seeds (种子) and told him the names of the flowers and plants. While Frank was enjoying the beauty of a flower, a little boy came to the gate. Finding the gate locked, he shook it hard and shouted, “Let me in! Let me in!”
“No,” said the gardener,“I won’t let you in, Tom. When I let you in yesterday, you broke my flowers and pulled some of my fruit. I won’t let a boy who meddles with (乱动) plants into my garden.”
Frank saw all that and realized how important it is for a boy not to meddle with things that don’t belong to him.

qs.stem: Frank wanted to enter the garden to ________.

ex.ev: Mom, these flowers are really beautiful. I want to take a closer look.
ex.why: Frank 说花很漂亮，想走近看看。

qs.stem: What did Frank do in the garden?
opts: He made a mess of the garden.

ex.ev: He showed him the seeds (种子) and told him the names of the flowers and plants.
ex.why: 园丁给他看种子、告诉他花草的名字，他了解了很多植物。他什么都没碰，也没弄乱花园。

qs.stem: Which word can best describe Tom?

ex.ev: Finding the gate locked, he shook it hard and shouted, “Let me in! Let me in!”
ex.why: Tom 用力摇门、大喊「让我进去」，昨天还折花摘果子——很没礼貌。

qs.stem: Which of the following is TRUE?
opts: Tom had been in the garden before.
The gardener finally let Tom into the garden.
The gardener didn’t want Frank in the garden at first.

ex.ev: When I let you in yesterday, you broke my flowers and pulled some of my fruit.
ex.why: 园丁说昨天让 Tom 进来过，可见 Tom 以前来过花园。

qs.stem: What did Frank learn at the end of the story?
opts: It is important for us to protect plants.
Don’t meddle with other people’s things.
We should be polite and friendly to others.

ex.ev: Frank saw all that and realized how important it is for a boy not to meddle with things that don’t belong to him.
ex.why: 最后一句：不乱动不属于自己的东西很重要。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店经济开发区中考二模
articles.title: Emily Holmes Education Officer Kids for Planet Earth Head Of
body: Emily Holmes
Education Officer
Kids for Planet Earth
Head Office
23 High Street Manchester
April 28
Dear Emily,

I am a student at Brown Middle School. During the last week of May, we will be having a Save the Earth Week at our school. There will be many activities, such as learning how to recycle things and making eco-friendly crafts (环保工艺品).

I am very interested in your organization, Kids for Planet Earth. Your mission is to let school kids teach one another about the environment. This is really important. Kids everywhere should hear about it. I’d like to invite a student from your organization to speak to us during Save the Earth Week. They can talk about what kids can do to protect the Earth.

Please let me know if a student has the time to come and speak that week. If so, what day and time would be good? If possible, can you tell us the topic of the talk and send us a short summary (概要)? Looking forward to hearing from you.
Best wishes.
Sam Holden, Seventh Grade, Brown Middle School

qs.stem: Sam Holden wrote this letter to ________.
opts: ask Holmes to be a teacher at his school
tell Holmes about Save the Earth activities
find out the name of an environmental organization
invite a speaker from Holmes’ organization to a school event

ex.ev: I’d like to invite a student from your organization to speak to us during Save the Earth Week.
ex.why: 写信的目的是邀请她们组织的一名学生在「拯救地球周」来学校演讲。

qs.stem: In his letter, Holden mentioned ________. a. eco-friendly crafts   b. teaching kids about the Earth   c. saving water   d. recycling

ex.ev: There will be many activities, such as learning how to recycle things and making eco-friendly crafts (环保工艺品).
ex.why: 信里提到了回收利用（d）和做环保手工艺品（a），没提节约用水。

qs.stem: From the text, we know ________ has the same meaning as“goal”.

ex.ev: Your mission is to let school kids teach one another about the environment.
ex.why: 「你们的使命是让孩子们互相教环保知识」——mission（使命、任务）和 goal（目标）意思相近。

qs.stem: Holden wants the student to talk about ________.
opts: how to use old things to make crafts
what children can do to protect the Earth
why the student joined Kids for Planet Earth
how to pick a good topic for the school talk show

ex.ev: They can talk about what kids can do to protect the Earth.
ex.why: 他希望来的学生讲讲孩子们能为保护地球做些什么。

qs.stem: In which unit of a textbook can the text be found?

ex.ev: During the last week of May, we will be having a Save the Earth Week at our school.
ex.why: 信的内容是保护地球、环保，适合「人与自然」单元。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店经济开发区中考二模
articles.title: Memorizing new English words is hard.
body: Memorizing new English words is hard.     32

After learning a number of new words, you can write a short story using all of these words.    33     What’s more, you’ll learn how to use the words in the right context (语境), which is the best way to learn the correct meanings of the words. And, it’s fun!    34     If you can’t think of anything to write, why not just write about your day and try to use the new words?

Another method is to create associations (联系) between words. For example, when you try to remember a word that has a suffix (后缀) like“-ment”, think of some other words that also have this suffix.     35

It’s also fun to work together with your classmates. Do some word-guessing games or organize competitions like spelling bees during the class breaks.     36     When you have company, learning can become a part of your daily life.

opts: This way, you can remember many words at the same time.
This way, you can better remember the spelling and learn how to use the words.
You can get rid of the boring act of memorizing words and free your imagination.
How can you better memorize and learn English words?

32.ev: Memorizing new English words is hard.
32.why: 第一句说记单词很难，接着提问 E「怎样更好地记住和学习英语单词？」引出下面的方法。

33.ev: What’s more, you’ll learn how to use the words in the right context (语境), which is the best way to learn the correct meanings of the words.
33.why: 用新词写小故事，B「这样能更好地记住拼写、学会用法」，后面 What’s more 再补充语境的好处。

34.ev: If you can’t think of anything to write, why not just write about your day and try to use the new words?
34.why: 前面说写故事很有趣，D「摆脱死记硬背，放飞想象力」；后面接「想不出写什么……」。

35.ev: think of some other words that also have this suffix.
35.why: 想出其他带同样后缀的词，A「这样可以同时记住很多词」。

36.ev: Do some word-guessing games or organize competitions like spelling bees during the class breaks.
36.why: 和同学玩猜词游戏、拼写比赛，C「这些活动一点也不无聊」。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店市九年级中考模拟二模
articles.title: Do you want to work as an animal keeper in the zoo?
body: Do you want to work as an animal keeper in the zoo? Here is what you shouldn’t miss. Animal-Keeper for a Day

Experience animal training, cleaning, and food preparation—just to name a few tasks! Participants (参与者) will have the chance to touch a koala, learn about reptiles (爬行动物) and even watch the training of some of our raptors (猛禽)!
How long does it last? ★5 hours
How much is the ticket? ★ Adult ticket: $15 ★ Child ticket (for children between 5 and 15 years old): $10 ★ Children under 5: free
What are included? ★ Entry into the zoo ★ 5-hour guided experience with an education officer ★ Private, up-close animal encounters (邂逅) ★ Professional photos of your junior keeper
* Please note that all participants need to bring your own lunch to this event.

qs.stem: What can you do as an animal keeper for a day in the zoo?
opts: Take photos with an education officer.

ex.ev: Experience animal training, cleaning, and food preparation—just to name a few tasks!
ex.why: 可以体验给动物准备食物。能摸的是考拉，猛禽只是看训练；拍照是给小饲养员拍的专业照。

qs.stem: What does the writer mean by saying “just to name a few tasks”?
opts: All the tasks there must be finished in a day.
There are a few tasks you can take part in there.
You can experience much more than what are mentioned.
You need to remember the tasks if you want to take part in the event.

ex.ev: Experience animal training, cleaning, and food preparation—just to name a few tasks!
ex.why: just to name a few 意思是「只是举几个例子」，能体验的远不止这些。

qs.stem: When will the event end if it starts at 13:00?

ex.ev: How long does it last? ★5 hours
ex.why: 活动持续 5 小时，13:00 开始，18:00 结束。

qs.stem: How much should they pay if a 4-year-old boy and his parents take part in the event?

ex.ev: ★ Adult ticket: $15 ★ Child ticket (for children between 5 and 15 years old): $10 ★ Children under 5: free
ex.why: 父母各 15 美元，4 岁的孩子不到 5 岁免费：15 × 2 = 30 美元。

qs.stem: What’s the writer’s purpose of writing this text?
opts: To suggest that visitors bring their own lunch.
To offer some interesting facts about the zoo.
To let people know and take part in the event.
To tell people the importance of protecting animals.

ex.ev: Do you want to work as an animal keeper in the zoo? Here is what you shouldn’t miss.
ex.why: 介绍「一日饲养员」活动的内容、票价，目的是让人们了解并参加。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店市九年级中考模拟二模
articles.title: “Where’s Papa going with that ax (斧)?
body: “Where’s Papa going with that ax (斧)?” said Fern to her mother as they were setting the table for breakfast.
“To the pig house,” replied Mrs. Arable. “Some pigs were born last night.”
“I don’t see why he needs an ax,” continued Fern.
“Well,” said her mother, “one of the pigs is very small and weak, so your father has decided to do away with it.”
“Do away with it?” shouted Fern. “You mean kill it? Just because it’s smaller than the others?”
Fern pushed a chair out of the way and ran outdoors. Fern’s shoes were wet by the time she caught up with her father.
“Please don’t kill it!” she sobbed (哭诉). “     ▲     ”
“Fern,” he said softly, “you will have to learn to control yourself.”
“Control myself?” shouted Fern. “This is a matter of life and death, and you talk about controlling myself.”
“Fern,” said Mr. Arable, “I know more about raising pigs than you do. A weak pig makes trouble. Now run along!”
“The pig couldn’t decide whether it was born small, could it? If I had been very small at birth, would you have killed me?” said Fern.
Mr. Arable smiled. “Certainly not,” he said. “All right. You go back to the house and I will bring the pig when I come in. I’ll let you keep it. Then you’ll see what trouble a weak pig can be.”

When Mr. Arable returned to the house half an hour later, he carried a box under his arm. He set it down at Fern’s chair. When Fern came down the stairs, she saw the box. Then she opened it. There, inside, looking up at her, was the newborn pig.
“Look at it!” she said, “It’s absolutely perfect.”
(Adapted from Charlotte’s Web)

qs.stem: Why did Mr. Arable decide to kill the pig?
opts: Because it caused him a lot of trouble.
Because his wife asked him to do so.
Because it was very small and weak.
Because there were too many pigs.

ex.ev: “one of the pigs is very small and weak, so your father has decided to do away with it.”
ex.why: 妈妈说：有一头小猪又小又弱，所以爸爸决定除掉它。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be put in the “     ▲     ”?

ex.ev: “You mean kill it? Just because it’s smaller than the others?”
ex.why: Fern 觉得只因为小猪个子小就杀掉它，不公平，后面也说「它没法决定自己生下来小不小」。

qs.stem: What is the correct order according to the text? a. Mrs. Arable told Fern about the pig. b. Fern saw the newborn pig in the box. c. Fern stopped her father from killing the pig. d. Fern ran outdoors to catch up with her father. e. Mr. Arable returned to the house with the pig.

ex.why: 顺序：妈妈告诉她小猪的事（a）→ 她跑出去追爸爸（d）→ 阻止爸爸杀小猪（c）→ 爸爸抱着小猪回来（e）→ 她在盒子里看到小猪（b）。

qs.stem: What is the most important in Fern’s eyes?

ex.ev: This is a matter of life and death, and you talk about controlling myself.
ex.why: 她说这是生死攸关的事，在她眼里生命最重要。

qs.stem: What would probably happen to the pig according to the text?
opts: It would bring the family good luck.
It would become tall and strong.
It would be kept in the pig house.

ex.ev: “Look at it!” she said, “It’s absolutely perfect.”
ex.why: Fern 觉得小猪「太完美了」，她会好好对待它。

articles.src: 2024年驻马店市九年级中考模拟二模
articles.title: Spelling words correctly usually depends on how we hear a wo
body: [图:reading/43a4778c/image2.png]
Spelling words correctly usually depends on how we hear a word and how we change what we hear into letters on the page. But how can we become good at spelling? Follow these wise ways below.     16

Practice makes perfect. Practising difficult spellings can help you remember them. The more exposure (接触) you have to them, the more likely they are to stick in your mind.     17     You can read the letters out loud, and then them correctly. Why not write words on sticky notes and place them around your house?     18     Your deskmate is a good choice because you two can test each other. When you find a spelling mistake your deskmate makes, you are also more likely to remember it. If you are practising for a spelling test, try to look over the spellings in the days before it.

19     It is almost impossible to teach yourself something you don’t know without the help of someone who does know. Teachers and parents will want to help you get spellings right. If you are learning how to spell a word, learn what it means, too. Prepare yourself for the secret to spelling success—Read!     20     It will help you learn spelling patterns (模式), rules and exceptions. If you are enjoying yourself, you might not even realize you are learning.

opts: There are many different ways to practise.
Getting someone to test you will also help.
Read different kinds of material every day.
You might be surprised at the progress you make.
Ask for help when you find spelling a word really difficult.

16.ev: Follow these wise ways below.
16.why: 前面说「按下面这些方法做」，D「你可能会对自己的进步感到惊讶」接着说效果。

17.ev: You can read the letters out loud, and then them correctly.
17.why: 后面列了大声读字母、贴便签几种练法，前面先说 A「练习的方法有很多」。

18.ev: Your deskmate is a good choice because you two can test each other.
18.why: 后面说同桌是好人选，可以互相考，前面应是 B「请别人考考你也有帮助」。

19.ev: It is almost impossible to teach yourself something you don’t know without the help of someone who does know.
19.why: 这一段讲向老师、家长求助，开头用 E「觉得哪个词很难拼时就请人帮忙」。

20.ev: Prepare yourself for the secret to spelling success—Read!
20.why: 前面说拼写成功的秘诀是阅读，C「每天读各种不同的材料」接着说。

articles.src: 2024年南阳市新野县九年级下学期二模
articles.title: In spring last year, senior students at Nanjing University v
body: In spring last year, senior students at Nanjing University visited an exhibition (展览) of paintings in front of the school dining hall. There was something special about the exhibition: all the works came from a student dorm (宿舍) cleaner. Their themes are from simple plants to more complex (复杂的) objects.

49-year-old Wu Lidi became widely known by students of this university for her paintings. They called her “a cleaning lady who could have become an artist”. During the exhibition, many students left handwritten messages to express their thanks and send best wishes to Wu, which surprised and touched Wu a lot.

Wu has never received any professional training in painting. With a great interest in painting, she used to create blackboard newspapers for her class as a student. Later she worked as a cleaner at Nanjing University and started painting again by accident. One day, a student who was supposed to create a blackboard newspaper didn’t return to school in time. The blackboard only had a few words reading “Welcome Home”. Seeing that, Wu volunteered to improve the blackboard newspaper by creating some pictures on it.

Since then, Wu has put more energy into painting on blackboards, and learned and practiced painting skills online in her spare time. As she’s responsible for cleaning a whole building, she’s always busy. But she still takes the time to paint and has never influenced her work. “I love doing it, and I hope students will feel happy to see my paintings,” she said.

qs.stem: What can we know about the exhibition? ________
opts: It took place in a university.

ex.ev: senior students at Nanjing University visited an exhibition (展览) of paintings in front of the school dining hall.
ex.why: 画展在南京大学食堂门前举办，是在一所大学里。展出的是宿舍保洁员的画，不是学生的作品。

qs.stem: Which of the following may NOT be the students messages? ________
opts: “I dream of being an art teacher like you one day.”
“Your paintings have made me happy for four years.”
“Hope you can bring joy to more students by painting.”
“You’ve created a nice world with your painting brush.”

ex.ev: Wu has never received any professional training in painting.
ex.why: 吴阿姨是宿舍保洁员，没学过专业绘画，不是美术老师，所以 A 不会是学生的留言。

qs.stem: What does Paragraph 3 mainly talk about? ________
opts: Why Wu was interested in cleaning.
How Wu began painting by accident as a cleaner.
What voluntary work Wu used to do.

ex.ev: Later she worked as a cleaner at Nanjing University and started painting again by accident.
ex.why: 第三段讲她当保洁员后，因为一次偶然的机会（帮学生补黑板报）又开始画画。

qs.stem: What can we infer about Wu Lidi from the text? ________
opts: She only paints flowers and trees.
She used to study painting at an art school.
She may watch painting videos when she’s free.
She puts off cleaning because of painting sometimes.

ex.ev: and learned and practiced painting skills online in her spare time.
ex.why: 她业余时间在网上学画画，可以推断她空闲时会看绘画视频。她从没耽误工作。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text? ________
opts: A cleaning lady who paints well
The welcome ceremony of a university

ex.ev: They called her “a cleaning lady who could have become an artist”.
ex.why: 全文讲一位画画很好的保洁阿姨——「一位画得很好的保洁阿姨」。

articles.src: 2024年周口市郸城县模拟调研联考二模
articles.title: “Tina, there’s a school talent show in three weeks,” I shout
body: “Tina, there’s a school talent show in three weeks,” I shouted to my best friend. My older brother had been teaching me juggling (杂耍), and he would help me.
Tina ran over to the bulletin board. “Maura, what’s our act going to be?”
“Our act?” I said, holding my books tightly.
Tina smiled and said, “It says acts can be individuals, partners, or small groups.”
My grip (紧握) on my books became uncomfortably tight.
“It’ll be fun,” Tina said.
I thought for a second before continuing. “I’ve got an idea and...”
Tina interrupted me, “Yeah, me too. Let’s talk at lunch.”
During math, I tried to think of how I would tell Tina. After all, we are best friends.
We should be able to see eye to eye about this. The problem is Tina always takes charge.
I really wanted to win, but I wanted to win on my own—with an act that was all mine.
At lunch, Tina started talking, “I have it all planned out. We can sing along to a song and dance, and my mom can make costumes (服装).”
“But I had another idea.” I told her about my juggling act.
Tina considered it. “Nah, I don’t think I can learn to juggle in three weeks,” she said. “You don’t want us to feel stupid, right?”
When my grandmother picked me up, she drove a few minutes and finally said, “Cat got your tongue?”
I explained as she listened.
“Well, you weren’t respectful of your own ideas. I understand that you’re friends, but you’re still responsible for your own actions,” said my grandmother.
“Tell the truth,” she added.
When we got home, I took 12 deep breaths and called Tina.

The next day, she described her act and her costume like nothing bad had happened. I know everything worked out fine. But the biggest surprise came at break, when we played a game that I chose, not Tina.

qs.stem: How did Maura feel when saying “Our act?”?

ex.ev: “Our act?” I said, holding my books tightly.
ex.why: 她本想自己表演，听到「我们的节目」很意外，还紧紧抱着书——又惊讶又担心。

qs.stem: What does Maura want to do at the talent show?

ex.ev: My older brother had been teaching me juggling (杂耍), and he would help me.
ex.why: 哥哥一直在教她杂耍，她想在才艺表演上表演杂耍。

qs.stem: What might Maura most probably say about Tina?
opts: She is always in control of things.
She is not the best kind of friend.
She doesn’t want to respect Maura.
She always helps Maura solve problems.

ex.ev: The problem is Tina always takes charge.
ex.why: 问题是 Tina 总是说了算，什么都由她安排。

qs.stem: What does the word “interrupted” most probably mean in the text?

ex.ev: Tina interrupted me, “Yeah, me too. Let’s talk at lunch.”
ex.why: Maura 话还没说完，Tina 就插话了——interrupted 是「打断」。

qs.stem: What does “the biggest surprise” mean according to Maura?
opts: Tina was still her best friend.
She won with the juggle show.
The game they played was fun.
She got to make her own decision.

ex.ev: But the biggest surprise came at break, when we played a game that I chose, not Tina.
ex.why: 最大的惊喜是课间玩的游戏是她选的，不是 Tina 选的——她终于能自己做决定了。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市禹州市中考二模
articles.title: Want to spend a happy holiday with your teens?
body: Want to spend a happy holiday with your teens? Why not come and see these top places?

[图:reading/5a7b2bff/image1.png]Plan 1: Vista Guest Ranch What you can do here is different in different seasons. Summer is for riding horses and trips, while winter is for skating and hot baths. The place even offers two clubs. One is for kids aged 8 to 14 and the other is for adults (成年人). They both include activities like horse riding and boating. Price:＄80 for each.   [图:reading/5a7b2bff/image2.png]Plan 2: Club Med Resort For kids aged 12 to 15, it offers special areas to teens with art activities, dance floors and video games. Parents can also enjoy relaxing along the beach. Price:＄100 for each.Family Tickets (a couple with a child) have a 10% discount (折扣) in total.

[图:reading/5a7b2bff/image3.png]Plan 3: Mohan Mountain House There are 4,000 acres (英亩) of forest and many valuable wild animals. It gives teens a chance to stay away from the city life and enjoy nature. The Mountain Program is made for kids aged 10 to

14. It includes boating, fishing and so on. Price:＄110 for each.   [图:reading/5a7b2bff/image4.png]Plan 4: Grand Vela Resort It offers game rooms to kids aged 14 to 17, with ping-pong and a dance floor to relax. Teens can make new friends and enjoy free teen-friendly snacks and drinks. Price:＄90 for each.

qs.stem: What can teens do at Vista Guest Ranch?

ex.ev: Summer is for riding horses and trips, while winter is for skating and hot baths.
ex.why: Vista 牧场夏天可以骑马、旅行，两个俱乐部也都有骑马。

qs.stem: How much should the Smiths pay at least if they go to Club Med Resort with their 13-year-old son?

ex.ev: Price:＄100 for each.Family Tickets (a couple with a child) have a 10% discount (折扣) in total.
ex.why: 每人 100 美元，三人 300 美元；家庭票（父母加一个孩子）打九折：300 × 0.9 = 270 美元。

qs.stem: Which of the following can best describe Mohan Mountain House?
opts: The perfect environment to live in.
The best ground for feeding wildlife.
A relaxing place to get close to nature.
A place to stay away from the country life.

ex.ev: It gives teens a chance to stay away from the city life and enjoy nature.
ex.why: 那里有大片森林和野生动物，让青少年远离城市、亲近自然。

qs.stem: Where can Bob go if he is a 16-year-old student?

ex.ev: It offers game rooms to kids aged 14 to 17, with ping-pong and a dance floor to relax.
ex.why: Bob 16 岁，只有 Grand Vela 度假村适合 14–17 岁。

qs.stem: Who is the text written for?

ex.ev: Want to spend a happy holiday with your teens?
ex.why: 开头问「想和你家的青少年过个快乐假期吗」，是写给父母看的。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市禹州市中考二模
articles.title: Harold Jones is 100 years old.
body: Harold Jones is 100 years old. He has been walking about 40 circles every day in his garden since the beginning of 2020. At first, he just walked for exercise. Now, Jones is using his circles to help others.

In the beginning, Jones just had a target (目标) of raising $1,000,which seemed a lot to him. But, he soon collected more than that. He has raised over ＄43,000 for charity (慈善). The old man walked 41,550 circles around the back of his home.
Jones walks in all weather, but he does fewer circles in the rain. He does 20 circles after breakfast and then does more after lunch.

Jones was given the idea by Tom Moore who had raised money for the National Health Service. Moore, a 99-year-old man, walked slowly with the help of a walking tool in the garden. And he raised $17 million.
Jones said that although he began walking just for exercise, he saw what Moore did and that gave him the idea to raise money for charity. Jones didn’t expect to walk further than Moore but he did.
When Jones reached his early target, he just kept going. He had no idea how many people would join him when he reached £10,000.
Jones received a Points of Light Award (奖). Jones said that he was surprised by this.
But giving service to others plays a large role in his life. This was a well-deserved (当之无愧的) honor for this old man.

qs.stem: Why did Jones walk circles at first?

ex.ev: At first, he just walked for exercise.
ex.why: 一开始他走路只是为了锻炼身体。

qs.stem: What made Jones start to do charity?

ex.ev: he saw what Moore did and that gave him the idea to raise money for charity.
ex.why: 他看到 Moore 做的事，才有了为慈善筹款的想法——是 Moore 的行动启发了他，不是 Moore 建议他。

qs.stem: What is probably the most important thing in Jones’ life?

ex.ev: But giving service to others plays a large role in his life.
ex.why: 为别人服务在他的生活中占很重要的位置。

qs.stem: Which words can best describe Jones?

ex.ev: He has raised over ＄43,000 for charity (慈善).
ex.why: 100 岁还坚持走路为慈善筹款——善良、乐于助人。

qs.stem: What does the text mainly talk about?
opts: Jones got the Points of Light Award.

ex.ev: Now, Jones is using his circles to help others.
ex.why: 全文讲 Jones 通过每天绕花园走路来筹款做慈善。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市禹州市中考二模
articles.title: Learning can feel like a challenge (挑战), especially when tes
body: Learning can feel like a challenge (挑战), especially when tests and exams are coming. However, it is not just to pass exams.     16

Find out what your learning style is. People have different ways of learning that make the information easier to understand. Some find visual aids (直观教具) are the most useful, while some need to hear the things of the learning before they understand.     17
Once you have found out which style is the best for your learning, you can put it to good use in your learning.

Even if you decide that you are the learner of a certain style, try learning skills from learners of other styles. Use these in your learning to help find the ways that fit you best. It’s not a good idea to be too strict about only using one style.
Take breaks when studying. Study for 15 minutes and take a 5-minute break.     19
Get into this habit and stick to it, as it’s good for your body and brain.

Use rewards (奖励).     20     Set goals (目标) for finishing parts of learning, followed by some rewards like a night off from learning, a movie with a friend, a piece of chocolate cake or whatever. Prepare rewards for achieving everything, tests and exams included.

opts: Change your learning styles now and then.
Or study for 30 to 55 minutes, and then take a break.
The following ways will help you to make learning easy.
A reward can help you to keep going towards your success.
Others need to move, touch and make things in order to learn.

16.ev: However, it is not just to pass exams.
16.why: 第一段后面用 C「下面这些方法能让学习变容易」引出下面几条。

17.ev: Some find visual aids (直观教具) are the most useful, while some need to hear the things of the learning before they understand.
17.why: 前面说有人靠看、有人靠听，E「还有人要动手做才能学会」，Some…some…Others 是提示。

18.ev: Even if you decide that you are the learner of a certain style, try learning skills from learners of other styles.
18.why: 这一段讲试着学别的学习方式、别只用一种，小标题是 A「时不时换换学习方式」。

19.ev: Study for 15 minutes and take a 5-minute break.
19.why: 前面说学 15 分钟休息 5 分钟，B「或者学 30 到 55 分钟再休息」，Or 是提示。

20.ev: Set goals (目标) for finishing parts of learning, followed by some rewards like a night off from learning, a movie with a friend, a piece of chocolate cake or whatever.
20.why: 这一段讲用奖励，D「奖励能帮你一直朝成功努力」。

cand: pron. 无论什么；任何事物

articles.src: 2024年商丘市夏邑县第二初级中学教育集团中考二模
articles.title: There are many kinds of book clubs all over the world.
body: There are many kinds of book clubs all over the world. The book clubs always organize different activities for its members every year. Have you thought of starting one? Starting a book club is easy.     16     Here are some suggestions to show you how to get yours off to a start.

When you set up your book club, the first thing you should do is of course to get members for your club.     17     A small group of seven to ten people is usually an ideal (理想的) size for a book club. Too many make discussions difficult. Once you have a group, agree on how often you want to meet—usually clubs meet monthly. Pick a date and stick with it.     18     Send out emails a week before the meeting to give people a written reminder. Set meeting time length. An hour is a good start. Two hours usually does the trick.

Then, you need a good place. Libraries, parks and restaurants all make good meeting places.     19     Noisy public places can make talking hard. If members bring a plate of food or a bottle, it can help start conversation.

Please don’t forget the most important thing—the book! Think about the books your club will enjoy.     20     You can take turns to recommend (推荐) books. Let everyone discuss upon what book to read. Anyway, make sure to keep it light and fun.
After all this has been decided, your book club is ready. Now, it is time to hold the first meeting. Enjoy your reading.请你

opts: Members can easily plan for it that way.
Your club can choose books in different ways.
All you and the club members need is to love reading.
They could be friends, family or those you know through activities.
For many clubs, homes are the best places as you don’t have to get dressed up.

16.ev: Have you thought of starting one? Starting a book club is easy.
16.why: 前面说办读书会很容易，C「你和会员只需要热爱读书」接着解释为什么容易。

17.ev: the first thing you should do is of course to get members for your club.
17.why: 首先要找会员，D「可以是朋友、家人或在活动中认识的人」接着说会员从哪来。

18.ev: Pick a date and stick with it.
18.why: 定好日期并坚持，A「这样会员容易提前安排」说明好处。

19.ev: Libraries, parks and restaurants all make good meeting places.
19.why: 这一段讲聚会地点，E「很多读书会觉得家里最好，不用打扮」，后面又说吵闹的公共场所不方便聊天。

20.ev: You can take turns to recommend (推荐) books.
20.why: 后面讲轮流推荐、大家讨论选书，前面应是 B「读书会可以用不同方式选书」。

articles.src: 2024年周口市项城市联考中考二模
articles.title: Kitchen Safety Rules Preparation *Always wash your hands bef
body: Kitchen Safety Rules
Preparation   [图:reading/2d079750/image1.png]*Always wash your hands before and after touching food. Tie back long hair. *Wear an apron (围裙) and roll up your sleeves (挽起袖子).
Cleaning   *Keep the cutting board clean. *Wash fruit and vegetables under cold water before use.

3   *Always ask an adult before using knives or going near hot things. *Use knives and other sharp tools with care. *Don’t put tools on the edge (边缘) of the work table. *When not using a knife, always keep it away from your body to avoid hurting yourself. *Use oven mitts (手套) when taking out hot dishes from the oven or microwave (微波炉).
Special attention   *Clean food spills (溢出) as soon as they happen. *Do not run around the kitchen, especially when food is being prepared.

qs.stem: What should you do before you touch food?

ex.ev: *Always wash your hands before and after touching food.
ex.why: 碰食物前后都要洗手。

qs.stem: According to the poster, when should you ask for permission from your parents?
opts: Before you take out hot dishes from the oven.
Before you use knives or going near hot things.
Before you wash fruit and vegetables under cold water.

ex.ev: *Always ask an adult before using knives or going near hot things.
ex.why: 用刀或靠近烫的东西之前，一定要先问大人。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be filled in the blank (空白处)?

ex.ev: *Use knives and other sharp tools with care. *Don’t put tools on the edge (边缘) of the work table.
ex.why: 这一部分讲刀、利器、工具和烫的东西，用 Tools（工具）做小标题最能概括。

qs.stem: Who is this poster written for?

ex.ev: *Always ask an adult before using knives or going near hot things.
ex.why: 海报提醒「用刀前先问大人」，是给学生（孩子）看的。

qs.stem: Where can we see the poster?
opts: On the wall of a restaurant.

ex.ev: Kitchen Safety Rules
ex.why: 这是教孩子厨房安全的规则，最可能出现在烹饪网站上；餐厅墙上是给厨师看的，不会要求先问大人。

articles.src: 2024年周口市项城市联考中考二模
articles.title: Lily was a cheerful girl.
body: Lily was a cheerful girl. She always had a big smile on her face. One day, she noticed an old man Mr. Grumble sitting beside a river. The old man looked sad. Lily wanted to make him smile, so she walked up to him with a friendly greeting.“Good morning, Mr. Grumble! Why the long face?”she asked.

Mr. Grumble said, “What’s there to be happy about, young one? Life is full of troubles.” Lily laughed and replied, “Troubles are like big and scary thunderclouds (雷雨云), Mr. Grumble. But just like clouds, they pass, making way for the sun to shine again. You should try looking on the bright side!”
Lily made a bet with Mr. Grumble, saying, “I bet I can make you smile by the end of the day.” Mr. Grumble challenged her, “You’re welcome to try, but it won’t be easy.”

For the rest of the day, Lily did all kinds of funny and silly things to make Mr. Grumble laugh. She told jokes, sang like nobody was watching, and even made faces. However, Mr. Grumble was still unhappy. As the sun began to set, Lily decided to give it one last try. She took a deep breath and broke into a joyous dance.
Surprisingly, Mr. Grumble couldn’t help it. He let out a chuckle (咯咯笑声), and then another.
Before he knew it, he was laughing heartily, his sadness giving way to happiness. Lily had won the contest,but more importantly, she showed Mr. Grumble that becoming cheerful was not difficult.
Happiness is a choice, and we can find it when we choose to see the bright side of life.

qs.stem: What was Mr. Grumble like as Lily came over?
opts: He was as cheerful as a girl.
He had a big smile on his face.

ex.ev: The old man looked sad.
ex.why: Lily 过来时，老人看起来很难过。

qs.stem: Why did Lily compare troubles to thunderclouds?
opts: To say that life is full of troubles.
To show that troubles will go away.
To tell the old man to be careful.
To show that troubles are scary.

ex.ev: But just like clouds, they pass, making way for the sun to shine again.
ex.why: 麻烦就像乌云，会过去，太阳还会出来——说明麻烦会过去的。

qs.stem: What do the underlined words “made a bet” mean in Chinese?

ex.ev: “I bet I can make you smile by the end of the day.”
ex.why: 「我敢说今天结束前能让你笑」——make a bet 是「打赌」。

qs.stem: How did Lily make Mr. Grumble become happy?

ex.ev: She took a deep breath and broke into a joyous dance.
ex.why: 讲笑话、唱歌、做鬼脸都没用，最后她跳了一支欢快的舞，老人才笑了。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the story?
opts: Life is always filled with troubles.
It’s not a good choice to bet.
Happy or not, it’s up to you.
Everyone has a chance to be happy.

ex.ev: Happiness is a choice, and we can find it when we choose to see the bright side of life.
ex.why: 最后一句：快乐是一种选择——快不快乐取决于你自己。

cand: adj. 吓人的；令人害怕的

articles.src: 2024年周口市项城市联考中考二模
articles.title: School life isn’t always happy and colorful.
body: [图:reading/2d079750/image2.png]
School life isn’t always happy and colorful. There are also “dark” corners. Bullying (欺凌) is one of the big problems at school.

Over 200 million the students in the world are bullied each year, according to a study.     16     Saying or writing bad things is also bullying, including laughing at others or giving people terrible nicknames (外号).     17     For example, some children may tell other children not to be friends with someone.

Being bullied may make you feel sick and do badly at school.     18     First, you should talk to your parents or teachers about it. They love you and they have the ability to help you. Trust them. Second, ask your friends to stand up for you. If your friends are bullied, you should also stand up for them.     19     It’s safer to stay with others. Remember, feel good about yourself! It’s not your fault to be bullied! Sometimes, people may bully others for no reason at all.
But do you know? A bully (欺凌者) is always a coward (胆小鬼).     20     You just need to have more confidence and hold your head up high!

opts: It is also helpful that you should try not to be alone.
Hurting a person’s body is the most common kind of bullying, such as hitting or kicking.
The bullies look strong but they are weak inside.
What should you do if you are bullied?

16.ev: Saying or writing bad things is also bullying, including laughing at others or giving people terrible nicknames (外号).
16.why: 后面说「说坏话、写坏话也是欺凌」，also 提示前面先讲了一种：C「伤害身体是最常见的欺凌，比如打、踢」。

17.ev: For example, some children may tell other children not to be friends with someone.
17.why: 后面的例子是叫别人不跟某人做朋友，B「有些欺凌伤害人际关系」。

18.ev: First, you should talk to your parents or teachers about it.
18.why: 后面讲第一、第二怎么做，前面先问 E「如果被欺凌了，该怎么办？」

19.ev: It’s safer to stay with others.
19.why: 后面说和别人待在一起更安全，A「尽量不要一个人待着也有帮助」。

20.ev: A bully (欺凌者) is always a coward (胆小鬼).
20.why: 前面说欺凌者都是胆小鬼，D「他们看起来强大，其实内心很弱」。

articles.src: 2024年周口市项城市联考中考二模
articles.title: One day both brothers were fighting so much as if they were
body: One day both brothers were fighting so much as if they were ready to kill each other any minute. When Lao Li saw them like this, he laughed very loudly.
Seeing their father laughing, both brothers forgot about the fight and asked their father why he laughed.

The father said, “You are fighting so much over a small piece of land. Leave it, come with me and I will show you a priceless treasure. But if you continue to fight, then I will take neither of you to the treasure.”
Both sons made a pact (达成协议) for the treasure. No matter what happened, they would not fight and would go on the journey with their father.
After leaving their home, both sons got on a bus with their father. They traveled for about ten hours and then reached a village.

Lao Li took them to a very big house. When they entered the house, what they saw surprised Lao Li. Crying, he said, “You may not remember, but when you were young, I fought a lot with my elder brother for this house. At that time, I won, but I lost my brother forever because he cut ties with me and left to live in a place far away. Then time changed and one day we also had to desert (舍弃) this house.”
The sons were listening carefully. Just then the father said, “Tell me which seat we were sitting on when we came here. Would that seat be ours forever?”
Both sons said together, “How can the bus seat be ours forever?”

Lao Li said, “Journey of bus continues and passengers on the seat keep changing. Someone else must be sitting there before us and tomorrow someone else will sit the seat which belongs to us for a while.”
Remember that the passengers on the seat of the bus keep changing every day. Don’t sacrifice (牺牲) your relationship for that seat.

qs.stem: Why did Lao Li laughed loudly?
opts: Because he didn’t educate his sons well.
Because he didn’t give his sons a lot of treasure.
Because he found the sons fought for a piece of land.
Because he didn’t know how to teach his sons a lesson.

ex.ev: “You are fighting so much over a small piece of land.
ex.why: 老李笑，是因为看到两个儿子为了一小块地打得那么凶。

qs.stem: What might Lao Li see when they entered the big house?
opts: The house was kept very clean.
New people were living in the house.
There was a lot of treasure in the house.
Birds made their nests at a few places.

ex.ev: Then time changed and one day we also had to desert (舍弃) this house.
ex.why: 老李当年争来的房子后来也舍弃了，现在一进门很吃惊，可以推断已经住进了别人。

qs.stem: What does the underlined part “that seat” in the last paragraph refer to (指代)?
opts: The seat for a bus driver.
The chair we use every day.
The land, house, money and so on.
The time we spend with our family.

ex.ev: Don’t sacrifice (牺牲) your relationship for that seat.
ex.why: 「那个座位」比喻土地、房子、钱这些东西——它们只属于我们一会儿，不要为它们牺牲亲情。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the story?
opts: Treasure is ours only for a short while.
A running bus is always full of passengers.
Money is more important than any other things.
Brothers should live in the same place forever.

ex.ev: Someone else must be sitting there before us and tomorrow someone else will sit the seat which belongs to us for a while.
ex.why: 座位只属于我们一小会儿，财产也一样——它们只是暂时属于我们。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?
opts: Lao Li’s fight with his brother

ex.ev: Leave it, come with me and I will show you a priceless treasure.
ex.why: 父亲说要带他们看「无价之宝」，最后才明白宝贝是亲情——标题「什么是无价之宝？」

cand: adj. 年龄较大的；年长的

articles.src: 2024年郑州市中考一模
articles.title: Let’s imagine this: Your parents are going out of town for a week.
body: Let’s imagine this: Your parents are going out of town for a week. You’re left with 800 yuan. How will you spend it? It would be unwise to spend the money at the mall, especially if you already have great clothes, right?     32     You’d probably also want to put some money aside for unexpected situations.
Well, you need to learn how to budget (做预算). It’s all about deciding what matters the most to you and how much you want to spend on those things.

Working out your priorities (优先事项) is the most important part of budgeting.     33     You have to consider saving money. The next time your friend invites you to join them for a party, you might as well decide to pass.

But having a budget doesn’t mean you can’t have fun. You just have to get creative. Instead of meeting your friends at the pizza shop and then going to the movies, you can invite them over to your house. You can buy some frozen pizzas at the supermarket and watch a movie online.     34
If you search the Internet for budgeting tips, you’ll find many.     35     Once you find a way that works for you, it’s easier to get excited about budgeting.
36     If you go over your budget, just try to learn from your mistakes. It’s part of becoming a responsible spender.

opts: It’s a lot cheaper but just as fun.
You have plenty of chances to test them.
For example, you plan to buy a new bike.
Keep in mind that even adults make mistakes at times.
A smarter way to spend that money would be on food and transportation.

32.ev: It would be unwise to spend the money at the mall, especially if you already have great clothes, right?
32.why: 前面说钱花在商场买衣服不明智，E「更聪明的是花在吃饭和交通上」。

33.ev: You have to consider saving money.
33.why: 这里讲先定好最重要的事，C「比如你打算买一辆新自行车」，所以要考虑存钱。

34.ev: You can buy some frozen pizzas at the supermarket and watch a movie online.
34.why: 请朋友到家里吃冷冻披萨、在网上看电影，A「便宜很多，但一样好玩」。

35.ev: If you search the Internet for budgeting tips, you’ll find many.
35.why: 网上做预算的小窍门很多，B「你有很多机会去试试它们」，后面说找到适合自己的就好。

36.ev: If you go over your budget, just try to learn from your mistakes.
36.why: 后面说超了预算就从错误中学习，前面应是 D「记住，大人有时也会犯错」。

articles.src: 2024年郑州市郑中国际学校中考一模
articles.title: Come and buy books at our great sale!
body: Come and buy books at our great sale! Here is the information about some new books. You will get 50% off if you buy three or more books together.
Chinese Clothing(￥50)

It’s written by Hua Mei, a professor of a university. It’s about typical Chinese clothing styles in different historical periods. From the book, readers can know traditional Chinese customs have made a big difference in clothing culture.
A Little Bit of Beijing (¥60)
The writers are Li Han and Hu Yan. The book is about the beautiful buildings in Beijing. It’s a great gift for kids who love picture books with colorful houses, cars and flowers.
The Brightest from the Best(¥40)

The writers are Hong and Zhang Xiaolong. The book tells us some stories about choices and growth. It records the real lives of eleven young people. They graduated from top universities and went to serve the people in the poor areas in China.
Stories of China(¥30)
It’s written in both English and Chinese. All the writers are from China and UK. The folk stories in this book help readers understand Chinese history and culture better.

qs.stem: Who wrote Chinese Clothing according to the passage?

ex.ev: It’s written by Hua Mei, a professor of a university.
ex.why: 《中国服饰》的作者是大学教授华梅。

qs.stem: Which book is the best gift for kids who like colorful pictures?

ex.ev: It’s a great gift for kids who love picture books with colorful houses, cars and flowers.
ex.why: 《一点点北京》是送给喜欢彩色图画书的孩子的好礼物。

qs.stem: What is The Brightest from the Best about?
opts: The real stories of young people.

ex.ev: It records the real lives of eleven young people.
ex.why: 这本书记录了 11 个年轻人的真实生活。

qs.stem: How much will you pay if you buy these four books together?

ex.ev: You will get 50% off if you buy three or more books together.

qs.stem: What do you know from the passage?

ex.ev: Here is the information about some new books.
ex.why: 文中介绍了几本新书的作者和内容——是书籍介绍。

cand: adj. 典型的；有代表性的
adj. 历史的；有关历史的
adj. 真实的；实际存在的

articles.src: 2024年实验中学中考模拟
articles.title: People enjoy eating together with family and friends all ove
body: People enjoy eating together with family and friends all over the world. However, customs around the dinner table are quite different.     16     They use chopsticks.

17     In some parts of the world, people think it is impolite to eat your food noisily or to make any noise when you drink.     18     In China, for example, it is considered polite to eat and drink noisily, because this is a sign that you are enjoying your meal. What more, Chinese people also show respect (尊敬) to their hosts by leaving a little food in their bowls.     19     However, in India, people show respect to their hosts by finishing all their food.

And what about when the meal is over and the restaurant bill arrives? In France, the custom is for one person to pay the whole bill.     20     Then, finally, there is the problem of whether or not to leave a tip (小费), people only give one if the service has been especially good. In Japan, people almost never tip, while in the USA, you are expected to leave at least 15—20%.
So, before you travel anywhere, make sure you know the local customs!

opts: Eating everything that is given to you is considered impolite.
For example, not everybody eats with a knife and fork.
What is polite in one country may be impolite in another.
In Germany, however, it is divided up according to how much each person has eaten.
But in some countries, this is actually seen as a good thing.

16.ev: They use chopsticks.
16.why: 后面说「他们用筷子」，前面应是 B「比如，不是每个人都用刀叉吃饭」。

17.ev: In some parts of the world, people think it is impolite to eat your food noisily or to make any noise when you drink.
17.why: 这一段讲同一件事在不同国家礼不礼貌不一样，开头用 C「在一个国家有礼貌的事在另一个国家可能不礼貌」。

18.ev: In China, for example, it is considered polite to eat and drink noisily, because this is a sign that you are enjoying your meal.
18.why: 前面说有的地方吃饭出声不礼貌，E「但在有些国家这是好事」，后面举中国的例子。

19.ev: However, in India, people show respect to their hosts by finishing all their food.
19.why: 中国人剩一点饭表示尊敬，A「把给你的东西全吃完被认为不礼貌」，后面 However 转到印度相反的做法。

20.ev: In France, the custom is for one person to pay the whole bill.
20.why: 法国是一个人付全部，D「而德国按每个人吃了多少来分」，however 表示对比。

articles.src: 2024年焦作市中考一模
articles.title: Accidents may happen at any time, as schools always hold a l
body: Accidents may happen at any time, as schools always hold a large number of people. Safety first! We should learn to protect ourselves from every possible danger. The following notice in the school will help you.

Prepare the first aid box in the classrooms.  [图:reading/dc8ffff2/image2.png]● Look through the first aid box and learn how to use each thing.  ● The first aid box should be opened easily so that you can use it quickly if necessary.  ● Check the first aid box from time to time to make sure that you have all necessary things.

Protect yourself from dangers.  [图:reading/dc8ffff2/image3.png]● Watch out the steps while you go out.  ● Avoiding crowded places can always help you keep safe.  ● Remember to warm up your body before running or exercising.  ●Follow the teacher’s words and the steps in books if you make experiments (实验) in the lab.

Never do any of the following things.  [图:reading/dc8ffff2/image4.png]● Play with fire.  ● Fight with others.  ● Bring knives to school.  ● Stand too close to the buildings on windy days.  ● Run after others while going up or down stairs (楼梯).  —You are taking your life in your hands.

qs.stem: What’s the main reason for school accidents according to the text?
opts: The management is not in place.
There are too many people there.
Students don’t follow their teachers’ advice.

ex.ev: Accidents may happen at any time, as schools always hold a large number of people.
ex.why: 学校里人多，所以随时可能出事。

qs.stem: What is necessary in the classrooms to keep safe?

ex.ev: Prepare the first aid box in the classrooms.
ex.why: 教室里要准备急救箱。

qs.stem: What can help save you from dangers according to the notice?
opts: Running or exercising as often as possible.
Going up and down steps with eyes closed.
Keeping yourself away from a large group of people.

ex.ev: Avoiding crowded places can always help you keep safe.
ex.why: 避开人多的地方能保证安全。

qs.stem: Which one of the following things you cannot do is not mentioned?

ex.ev: ● Play with fire.  ● Fight with others.  ● Bring knives to school.
ex.why: 不能做的事里有玩火、打架、带刀，B 图玩电源插座没有提到。

qs.stem: What is the main purpose of the text?
opts: To warn students not to break the school rules.
To encourage students to build a good relationship with each other.
To advise schools to provide a safe environment to study for students.
To remind children to stay away from danger and protect themselves at school.

ex.ev: We should learn to protect ourselves from every possible danger.
ex.why: 全文提醒学生在学校远离危险、保护自己。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市禹州市中考一模
articles.title: “Look at this,” I said to my friend Mandy, holding up the br
body: “Look at this,” I said to my friend Mandy, holding up the bright-red paper. “There’s a five-day art camp at White Cliff this summer!”

Mandy looked at the paper, “It’s during the last week of July,” she said. “That’s the same time as the Hill County Fair and we always go to the fair.” Mandy handed the paper back to me. “Tessa, you’re the artist, but I’m not,” she smiled. “My little brother thought the flowers I painted were spaceships.”
“You may not think you can draw, but you can learn,” I said in my most encouraging voice. I really didn’t want to go alone.
Later, I called my friends Emily and Yoshiko. Yoshiko was going to the fair, and Emily would be out of town in July. I sighed (叹气) and dropped my head down on the red paper.

To relax myself, I went outside to draw the Westons’ pine tree (松树). When I sat on the stone, I thought about the art camp and wished I could be a little braver. Mandy could make friends with other kids in 10 minutes, but I always feel nervous when I don’t know anyone around me. So I decided to give up the camp.

A moment later, Mr. Weston, my neighbor, came. He told me something about the pine. The roots (根) of the pine couldn’t be too near the surface or too deep so that they could reach outward. He also praised me that I drew very well. After his leaving, I thought about what Mr. Weston had told me. It made me think about the art camp and my own roots. I wasn’t reaching them out at all. Instead, I was planting myself into one deep place because I felt safer. I suddenly realized that if I wanted to grow, I had to start reaching out too.
That night, I took a deep breath and made a new decision.

qs.stem: What did Mandy think of drawing?
opts: She was not good at it.
She could draw better than her brother.

ex.ev: “My little brother thought the flowers I painted were spaceships.”
ex.why: 她画的花被弟弟看成宇宙飞船，说明她不擅长画画。

qs.stem: How did Tessa feel after knowing Emily’s and Yoshiko’s plans?

ex.ev: I sighed (叹气) and dropped my head down on the red paper.
ex.why: 朋友们都去不了，她叹气、把头趴在宣传单上——很失落。

qs.stem: Why did Tessa decide to give up the camp?
opts: Because she was not interested in it.
Because she planned to go to the Hill County Fair.
Because she was afraid of going to the camp alone.
Because she was busy drawing the pine tree for Mr. Weston.

ex.ev: but I always feel nervous when I don’t know anyone around me. So I decided to give up the camp.
ex.why: 身边没有认识的人她就紧张，所以不敢一个人去。

qs.stem: What may Tessa’s decision be at last?
opts: Inviting Mr. Weston to the camp.

ex.ev: I suddenly realized that if I wanted to grow, I had to start reaching out too.
ex.why: 她明白了想成长就要走出去，当晚做了新决定——一个人去参加艺术营。

qs.stem: What is the best title for the text?
opts: Get out of your safe place
Treat your friends with your heart

ex.ev: Instead, I was planting myself into one deep place because I felt safer.
ex.why: 她发现自己总待在觉得安全的地方，要走出去才能成长——「走出你的安全区」。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市禹州市中考一模
articles.title: Two Swedish students have invented a new kind of bicycle helmet (头盔).
body: Two Swedish students have invented a new kind of bicycle helmet (头盔). It’s invisible (隐形的) because you cannot see it on a rider’s head.

The helmet is really a kind of airbag. It is inside a large collar (衣领). People wear it around their neck like a scarf. When the rider falls off his or her bike, the collar quickly fills with air and an airbag appears around the head.

The two students, Anna Haupt and Terese Alstinat, wanted to change the way people ride bikes. They said, “Bicycle helmets have always been the same. They’re so bulky, like a hard mushroom (蘑菇) on the head.” They called their new invention the Hövding. The pair said it looked so cool that people would be happy to wear it.

The inventors started researching and developing the helmet a few years ago. They studied thousands of accidents. They wanted to find out how to make the safest helmet. They worked with a Swedish airbag company called Alva. And then the invisible helmet came out. Today, the two inventors have their own company that sells the new helmets. There are 17 workers in their company. They hope their helmet will change how people all over the world ride bikes.

In their video, Haupt and Alstinat said, “Cars are so yesterday. Bikes are the future.” People can not only take exercise but also experience the beauty of nature when they ride bikes. Now people can only buy the helmet online in Europe. It sells for around $530. The company did not say when people in the rest of the world could buy it.

qs.stem: What is special about the new helmet?
opts: It is an airbag that looks like a mushroom.
It is an airbag that is around the head all the time.
It is an airbag that can stop people falling down.
It is an airbag that cannot be seen when it’s safe.

ex.ev: It’s invisible (隐形的) because you cannot see it on a rider’s head.
ex.why: 这种头盔其实是个气囊，平时藏在衣领里看不见，摔倒时才弹出来——安全时看不见。

qs.stem: What is Paragraph 3 mainly about?
opts: Why they invented the new helmet.
How they invented the new helmet.
Where they invented the new helmet.
When they invented the new helmet.

ex.ev: They’re so bulky, like a hard mushroom (蘑菇) on the head.
ex.why: 第三段讲她们觉得老式头盔又笨又难看，想改变人们骑车的方式——这是发明新头盔的原因。

qs.stem: What did the inventors do to create the safest helmet?
opts: They worked in a bicycle factory.
They researched how people ride bikes around the world.

ex.ev: They studied thousands of accidents.
ex.why: 为了做出最安全的头盔，她们研究了几千起事故。

qs.stem: What does the underlined sentence mean in the last paragraph?
opts: Cars were invented earlier than bicycles.
In the future, people won’t drive cars any more.
Riding bikes will be more popular than driving cars.
Cars are more expensive than bikes so few people will buy cars.

ex.ev: Bikes are the future.
ex.why: 「汽车过时了，自行车才是未来」——意思是骑车会比开车更受欢迎。

qs.stem: Who can buy the helmet online now?

ex.ev: Now people can only buy the helmet online in Europe.
ex.why: 现在只能在欧洲网上买，四个选项里只有英国在欧洲。

cand: adj. 庞大笨重的；占空间的

articles.src: 安阳市殷都区重点名校2024年中考一模
articles.title: When I was young, my father used to grow carnations—a kind o
body: When I was young, my father used to grow carnations—a kind of flower that was red, pink and white. He took care of them with much love and devotion (挚爱). When he came home from work every day, he would enjoy watching them. And he used to tell us, “No one should touch my flowers.”

One day, my younger sister Clemence, who loved Dad very much, wanted to help him. So she cut the carnations from their stems (枝干) one by one and arranged them on the ground. She believed that Dad would be very pleased to see them that way. When Mom and I realized what my sister had done, we became completely speechless. However, my sister didn’t know why no one showed her any appreciation (欣赏). When Dad came back, he went straight to watch the flowers as usual. Seeing his flowers lying on the ground like dead animals, he was surprised at first. He looked towards the street to see if it was any of the neighbor’s children who could have done it. Then he looked at Mom in silence. Finally Mom, who always taught us to tell the truth, said, “No bad neighbors did this great job, only your lovely daughter Clemence.” Dad’s face changed into a smile and then he said, “Do I have better flowers than my lovely daughter?” My younger sister smiled and hugged Dad strongly.

qs.stem: How many kinds of colors do carnation have according to the passage?

ex.ev: my father used to grow carnations—a kind of flower that was red, pink and white.
ex.why: 康乃馨有红、粉、白三种颜色。

qs.stem: Why did Clemence cut the carnations from their stems?
opts: Because Dad told her to do so.
Because Mum told her to do so.
Because she wanted to help her dad.

ex.ev: One day, my younger sister Clemence, who loved Dad very much, wanted to help him.
ex.why: 妹妹很爱爸爸，想帮他，以为爸爸看到会高兴。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “speechless” mean in Chinese?

ex.ev: When Mom and I realized what my sister had done, we became completely speechless.
ex.why: 看到花都被剪了，妈妈和我一句话也说不出来——speechless 就是「无语的」。

qs.stem: What did the father feel after hearing what the mother said?

ex.ev: Dad’s face changed into a smile
ex.why: 听说是心爱的女儿做的，爸爸露出了笑容，很高兴。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for this passage?

ex.ev: “Do I have better flowers than my lovely daughter?”
ex.why: 爸爸说「我还有比我可爱的女儿更好的花吗？」——女儿才是爸爸最好的花。

articles.src: 安阳市殷都区重点名校2024年中考一模
articles.title: We all know that lying (说谎) is wrong.
body: We all know that lying (说谎) is wrong. But do you know that it is bad for both your physical and mental health? A recent study shows that telling fewer lies helps people physically and mentally.

“For ten weeks, 110 people aged from 18 to 71 were tested to see the relationship between the number of lies they told and their health,” said Anita Kelly, a professor at the University of Notre Dame in Indiana. “When they lied more, their health declined,” said Kelly.

Researchers divided the people into two groups. Group A was told to avoid telling any lie for any reason to anyone. They may omit (忽略) the truth, refuse to answer questions, and keep secrets, but they can’t say anything that they know are not true. Group B was not told anything like this.

Over the study period, when people in Group A told fewer lies in a week than they did in other weeks, they experienced fewer health problems such as sore throats and headaches. Professor Linda Stroh said, “When you find that you don’t lie, you have less stress (压力).” The results of past research show that each American tells about 11 lies a week. In both groups, when people lied less during a week, they reported better physical and mental health during that period.

“It’s certainly a good thing to have people be more honest,” said Robert Feldman of the University of Massachusetts. “It may improve our mental health, but I don’t think it can improve our physical health.”

qs.stem: The underlined word “declined” means “________” in Chinese.

ex.ev: “When they lied more, their health declined,” said Kelly.
ex.why: 说谎越多，健康就……；前面说说谎对健康不好——declined 是「变差」。

qs.stem: From the second paragraph, we can learn that ________.
opts: the test continued for no more than one month
older people lie less than younger people
the number of lies one tells can affect one’s health
many people feel sick when they don’t tell lies

ex.ev: were tested to see the relationship between the number of lies they told and their health,
ex.why: 研究的是说谎次数和健康的关系，结论是说谎多会影响健康。测试进行了十周，不是不到一个月。

qs.stem: People in Group A were allowed to ________. ① omit the truth                                                     ② refuse to answer questions ③ keep secrets                                                     ④ tell lies to strangers

ex.ev: They may omit (忽略) the truth, refuse to answer questions, and keep secrets, but they can’t say anything that they know are not true.
ex.why: A 组可以不说真相、拒绝回答、保守秘密，但不能说假话——①②③。

qs.stem: According to Linda Stroh, ________.
opts: mental health is more important than physical health
when people don’t lie, they feel more relaxed
to be honest can’t improve our physical health

ex.ev: “When you find that you don’t lie, you have less stress (压力).”
ex.why: Linda Stroh 说不说谎压力就小，人会更放松。

qs.stem: We would most probably find this passage ________.

ex.ev: A recent study shows that telling fewer lies helps people physically and mentally.
ex.why: 讲说谎和身心健康的关系，最可能登在健康杂志上。
