articles.title: “Pulling your leg ” A: Fred, is it true that I didn’t pass t
body: “Pulling your leg ” A: Fred, is it true that I didn’t pass the math test this time? B：I don’t know, Joe! It was a joke!   I was pulling your leg,that’s all. A：Oh,dear. You mean you are kidding. B：Yes,pardon me.

Good Boy Little Robert asked his mother for two cents,“What did you do with the money I gave you yesterday?”  “I gave it to a poor old woman.”He answered. “ You are a good boy. ”Said the mother proudly. “Here are two more,but why are you so interested in the old woman?” “She is the one who sells the candy!”

New Teacher George came back from school on the first of September,“ George,how did you like your new teacher”,asked his mother.“I didn’t like her,because she said that three and three were six and then she said that two and four were six ,too...”

A Good Box of Matches Mother sent Tommy to the store across the street to buy a good box of matches, when Tommy came back,mother asked him,“Did you buy a good box of matches?”“Yes,mom.”Tommy replied,“I have tried them all..”

qs.stem: George didn’t like his teacher because he thought___________.

ex.ev: because she said that three and three were six and then she said that two and four were six ,too...
ex.why: 老师说三加三等于六，又说二加四也等于六，George 以为老师总出错（其实两个都对，这就是笑点）。

qs.stem: Tommy tried all the matches in order to _________.
opts: make sure if they are all good.

ex.ev: “I have tried them all..”
ex.why: 妈妈要一盒好火柴，Tommy 把火柴全划了一遍，想确认它们都是好的（笑点：全用掉了）。

qs.stem: According to” Good Boy”,we learned ______________.
opts: Little Robert asked his mother for two cents to help the old woman.
Little Robert’s mother was very happy at last when she heard his son’s words.

ex.ev: “She is the one who sells the candy!”
ex.why: 钱给了老奶奶，原来她是卖糖的——Robert 是拿钱去买糖了，他喜欢吃糖。

qs.stem: All of the above are jokes EXCEPT_____.

ex.why: 后三则都有出人意料的笑点；Pulling your leg 只是一段解释习语「开玩笑」的对话，不是笑话。

qs.stem: Which of the following is TRUE ?
opts: Joe didn’t pass the math test.
Little Robert was very kind to the old woman.
“I was pulling your leg” means “ I was just kidding.”
Tommy bought a good box of matches for his mother .

ex.ev: You mean you are kidding.
ex.why: 对话里解释了：pulling your leg 就是「开玩笑」。Joe 有没有及格不知道；Robert 是去买糖；Tommy 把火柴全用了。

articles.title: If someone said they’d pay you $1,800 to stay off social med
body: If someone said they’d pay you $1,800 to stay off social media for 6 years, could you do it? Could you? An American mom challenged her son to do just that, and he succeeded.

Sivert Klefsaas is the youngest of Lorna Gold-strand Klefsaas’ four children, and his three older sisters all used social media growing up. It was influencing their feelings, as well as their friendships. So, Lorna thought, “If I could, I’d be willing to do whatever to keep Sivert off social media as long as I could, whatever that looks like.” And that’s where the idea for this challenge came from.

It all started when Lorna heard about a similar “16 for 16 challenge” on the radio, where a mother called Amanda Green gave her daughter Teresa $1,600 when she turned 16 if she stayed off social media. So, Lorna decided to create her own “18 for 18 challenge”. Not only did Sivert finally complete this challenge, but he would do it again, too.
“It wasn’t too difficult to live without social media, and I didn’t think about it much during the 6 years,” Sivert said. “As time went on, it was more of a proud thing.”

He had his friends keep him up to update on the latest information. Sivert added, “I got to avoid all the unnecessary things that were on there. It also meant I had more time to focus on my grades and sports instead.”
Now that he’s done with the challenge, Sivert joined Instagram (照片墙), but has no plans to let social media define (定义) him.
“Social media is great. We certainly need to use it,” Sivert said. “But also make sure you spend time in other areas of your life, especially those personal relationships.”
Still, Lorna is proud of her son’s success. “We are certainly not against social media, but it’s the healthy using of it,” Lorna told CNN.

qs.stem: Who does the underlined word “she” refer to?

ex.ev: where a mother called Amanda Green gave her daughter Teresa $1,600 when she turned 16 if she stayed off social media.
ex.why: she 指女儿 Teresa：她满 16 岁时，如果没用社交媒体，就能拿到 1600 美元。

qs.stem: How did Sivert get the latest information?

ex.ev: He had his friends keep him up to update on the latest information.
ex.why: 他让朋友告诉他最新消息。

qs.stem: What does Sivert think of social media now?
opts: Social media is a way to define people.
It’s important to use social media healthily.
It is too difficult to live without social media.
Social media is great and he needs it all the time.

ex.ev: “Social media is great. We certainly need to use it,”
ex.why: 他说社交媒体很好要用，但也要把时间花在别处——要健康地使用。

qs.stem: Which words can best describe Sivert?

ex.ev: Not only did Sivert finally complete this challenge, but he would do it again, too.
ex.why: 6 年不用社交媒体，还愿意再来一次——意志坚强。

qs.stem: What can we learn about Lorna from the passage?
opts: She is a mother of a 16-year-old teenager.
She helped his son successfully stay off the social media.
She doesn’t really agree with the “16 for 16 challenge” on the radio.
She is not against social media because her son succeeded in using it.

ex.ev: So, Lorna decided to create her own “18 for 18 challenge”.
ex.why: Lorna 设计了挑战，帮儿子成功做到 6 年不用社交媒体。她儿子已经 18 岁，不是 16 岁。

cand: n. 大众传播媒介；媒体
pron. 无论什么；任何事物
v. 更新；使掌握最新情况

articles.src: 2024年郑州市实验中学中考三模
articles.title: People are always trying to live a healthy life.
body: People are always trying to live a healthy life. You might have read so much on this topic.     32
Exercise when you are tired.
After a long tiring day of study, exercising might not sound like a good idea, but it really helps a lot. In fact, physical activities can provide you with the missing energy.     33
Write by hand to help the brain be active.

Although writing something with a computer is faster, it is much better to remember the whole thing by writing it down by hand.     34     When you read a handwritten text, naturally it’s easier for your brains to remember the information.
By sparing the time for yourself and just being alone for a while, you can have a chance to think and get to know yourself better. And you won’t behave impulsively (冲动地).
Drink hot drinks on a hot day.

What makes you cool fast on a hot summer morning, cold water or hot water?     36     When you are drinking something hot, the body will feel the change in temperature and increase the perspiration (流汗), which helps you make cool down!

opts: Also, it’s a kind of exercise for teenagers.
The following tips may sound strange but helpful.
The study shows that the hot water makes people feel cooler.
Research shows that exercising for just 30 minutes can make you feel good!

32.ev: You might have read so much on this topic.
32.why: 前面说这方面的建议你可能读过很多，B「下面这些建议听起来奇怪但很有用」引出下文。

33.ev: In fact, physical activities can provide you with the missing energy.
33.why: 累的时候锻炼能补充精力，E「研究表明只锻炼 30 分钟就能让你感觉很好」。

34.ev: Although writing something with a computer is faster, it is much better to remember the whole thing by writing it down by hand.
34.why: 手写更容易记住，A「对青少年来说这也是一种锻炼」，Also 表示再补充一个好处。

35.ev: By sparing the time for yourself and just being alone for a while, you can have a chance to think and get to know yourself better.
35.why: 这一条的小标题，下面讲留时间给自己——D「多留点时间给自己」。

36.ev: What makes you cool fast on a hot summer morning, cold water or hot water?
36.why: 前面问喝冷水还是热水更凉快，C「研究表明热水让人觉得更凉快」回答这个问题。

cand: adj. 活跃的；积极参与的

articles.src: 2024年平顶山市中考三模
articles.title: Schools help protect kids’ mental (心理的) health in many ways.
body: Schools help protect kids’ mental (心理的) health in many ways. Some states in the US let kids take mental health days. Should schools offer mental health days? Here’s what some students have to say.

Bibi Tooren, 11 Schools should give kids days off for mental health, because mental health is an important part of the whole health. If you don’t feel well, it will have a big influence on your ability to focus (集中). Kids get stressed with long school days. Also, kids don’t have much experience dealing with mental health crises (危机).   [图:reading/32473c65/image6.png]

[图:reading/32473c65/image7.png]   Nugg Canales, 8 Kids should get mental health days off from school. Sometimes, we need to stay at home to calm our minds. Some schools don’t allow music, and I need soft music to make me feel good about myself and the world. If you take a mental health day, you should not make up work because it adds stress to your life.

Hailey Young, 12 The weekend was created to give us time off, and we children need to learn to better manage our time. We hardly get our schoolwork done in the five school days we get. And schools would need students to make up mental health days. They would probably do so during our real breaks: in summer vacation or winter vacation. Another thing is that, for some kids, school might be safe.   [图:reading/32473c65/image8.png]

[图:reading/32473c65/image9.png]   Johnny Gabel, 9.  I don’t think schools should give students days off for their mental health. Having too many days off can have a bad influence on grades. And many students’ parents have to go to work. If students get too many days off, they might get left home too much. This could make some students’ mental health problems worse.

qs.stem: According to Bibi Tooren, kids with mental health problems ________.
opts: are able to deal with their mental health crises
shouldn’t make up work which adds stress to their life
can’t pay full attention to what they are learning in class
need to listen to soft music to make themselves feel good

ex.ev: If you don’t feel well, it will have a big influence on your ability to focus (集中).
ex.why: Bibi 说心情不好会影响注意力，学不进去。不补作业、听轻音乐是 Nugg 说的。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “so” refer to?
opts: Making up mental health days they have got.
Finishing schoolwork in the five school days.
Giving children a safe place like their school.

ex.ev: And schools would need students to make up mental health days.
ex.why: 前一句说学校会要求学生补上请的心理健康假，so 指的就是「补上这些假」。

qs.stem: Who thinks kids may have low grades in exams if they get mental health days off?

ex.ev: Having too many days off can have a bad influence on grades.
ex.why: Johnny 说放假太多会影响成绩。

qs.stem: What is the text mainly about?
opts: The discussions about kids’ mental health crises.
The importance of offering kids mental health days.
Several suggestions for improving kids’ mental health.
Some opinions on whether kids should get mental health days off.

ex.ev: Should schools offer mental health days? Here’s what some students have to say.
ex.why: 几个学生发表看法：该不该放心理健康假——有支持也有反对。

qs.stem: In which part of a newspaper can you read the text?

ex.ev: Schools help protect kids’ mental (心理的) health in many ways.
ex.why: 讲学校该不该给学生放心理健康假，属于教育版块。

cand: adj. 真实的；实际存在的

articles.src: 2024年平顶山市中考三模
articles.title: Middle school matters a lot in everyone’s life.
body: Middle school matters a lot in everyone’s life. You will be given more responsibility. Of course, there can be fear as well, but with a little common sense you will survive.

Know and obey your school’s rules!     32     Teachers want to be sure you know what to do and whether you understand their instructions or not. So don’t be afraid to ask questions! Teachers are there to help you! If you’re not sure, just ask.

Avoid drama and talking behind others. Naturally, people talk about other people’s problems and lives.     33     They only break friendships, create enemies, hurt feelings, and make things worse for everyone.
Choose your friends wisely. This is very important. Be friends with people who don’t start or take part in drama and you’ll avoid the worst things that happen in middle school.     34

Don’t let your friends get you in trouble. Don’t be friends with people who get you in serious trouble. It is similar to the step above.     35     Don’t be afraid to tell an adult if someone asks or tells you to do something really bad.

36     Just like you don’t want to do something to hurt other people, you shouldn’t do anything to hurt yourself. Don’t drink or smoke, or do any kind of self-harm like cutting yourself. If you need help, there are always people who will help you.

opts: Don’t do anything that you think is wrong.
Don’t do anything that will harm your body.
However, you should never start rumors (谣言).
Try to have a group of close friends who you can trust.
Just like in primary school, there are rules that you have to follow.

32.ev: Know and obey your school’s rules!
32.why: 小标题说要遵守校规，E「就像在小学一样，有规则必须遵守」。

33.ev: They only break friendships, create enemies, hurt feelings, and make things worse for everyone.
33.why: 后面说「它们只会破坏友谊、制造敌人」，they 指 C 里的谣言：「但你绝不能造谣」。

34.why: 这一段讲慎重交友，D「尽量交一群你信得过的好朋友」。

35.ev: Don’t be afraid to tell an adult if someone asks or tells you to do something really bad.
35.why: 别被朋友带进麻烦，A「不要做你认为不对的事」，后面说有人让你做坏事要告诉大人。

36.ev: you shouldn’t do anything to hurt yourself. Don’t drink or smoke, or do any kind of self-harm like cutting yourself.
36.why: 这一段讲不要伤害自己——不喝酒、不吸烟、不自残，小标题是 B「不要做伤害身体的事」。

articles.src: 2024年新乡市名校联考中考三模
articles.title: The Sunshine Library The Sunshine Library provides all kinds
body: [图:reading/41a09b55/image1.png]The Sunshine Library
The Sunshine Library provides all kinds of services, as well as plenty of activities.Opening Hours

Monday: 9: 00 a. m.-5: 30 p. m.        Tuesday: 9: 00 a. m.-5: 00 p. m.  Wednesday: 9: 00 a. m.-5: 30 p. m.        Thursday: 9: 00 a. m.-8: 00 p. m.  Friday: 9: 00 a. m.-5: 30 p. m.        Saturday: 9: 00 a. m.-4: 00 p. m.  Sunday: closed  Closed on public holidays.
Activities on January 22nd

Children’s Story-time  Experience the magic of story-time with your children at the library. It includes stories, songs and bookmark making activities for children aged 2-5. Time: 10: 00 a. m.-10: 30 a. m.  Cost: Free   Maker Space Come and join us for interesting craft (手工艺) activities in the library. The activities are for children aged 2-10. Time: 11: 00 a. m.-2: 00 p. m.  Cost: Free

Manage Your Time The holiday is coming. Learn how to make your to-do list, track (跟踪) your habits, or just be creative. It is for those aged 12 and older. Time: 2: 00 p. m.-3: 30 p. m.  Cost: Free   English Conversation Group  Our friendly group meets at the library every Monday afternoon. Come along to make new friends and improve your English. Learners of all levels are welcome. Time: 1: 00 p. m.-2: 00 p. m.  Cost: Free
For more information, please visit our website: www.sunshinelibrary.com.

qs.stem: How long does the library open on Wednesdays?

ex.ev: Wednesday: 9: 00 a. m.-5: 30 p. m.
ex.why: 周三从上午 9:00 开到下午 5:30，一共 8.5 小时。

qs.stem: What’s special in Children’s Story-time?
opts: Parents can join it with kids.
Kids can learn how to be creative.

ex.ev: Experience the magic of story-time with your children at the library.
ex.why: 「和你的孩子一起」体验故事时间——家长可以陪孩子一起参加。

qs.stem: Who can take part in Manage Your Time?
opts: Children who are five years old.
Children who are eight years old.
Children who are eleven years old.
Children who are fourteen years old.

ex.ev: It is for those aged 12 and older.
ex.why: 时间管理活动是给 12 岁及以上的人的，四个选项里只有 14 岁符合。

qs.stem: How often do the members of English Conversation Group meet?

ex.ev: Our friendly group meets at the library every Monday afternoon.
ex.why: 英语角每周一下午见面，一周一次。

qs.stem: What’s the main purpose of the text?
opts: To introduce the books and activities in the Sunshine Library.
To ask people to do more useful things for the Sunshine Library.
To explain why the Sunshine Library is the most popular in the city.
To encourage people to take part in the activities in the Sunshine Library.

ex.ev: Activities on January 22nd
ex.why: 主要介绍图书馆 1 月 22 日的几项免费活动，鼓励大家参加；没有介绍图书。

articles.src: 2024年新乡市名校联考中考三模
articles.title: I have seen many parents wonder whether they did enough to c
body: [图:reading/41a09b55/image2.png]
I have seen many parents wonder whether they did enough to create happy memories for their kids. My own experiences have taught me that I cared most about the simple things I did with my dad.
When I was growing up, I was not able to spend much time with my dad. He worked about 70 hours a week. He had to make money to support our family.

But I remember there were summers when my dad and I would go to the local park near our house and play soccer with some of his friends on a Saturday afternoon. It was fantastic! I loved playing sports and I loved being able to do that with him. After we played, we would get ice cream at the ice cream shop on the way back home. Sometimes during the summer time, if I was playing basketball in our yard, he would also come outside and played with me. We would talk and relax for those few moments. It was amazing.

It didn’t happen as often as I would like. As a result, I cherished (珍惜) every chance to get along with him. But I never told him how happy I was when he would come outside with me, because I never wanted him to feel bad that he had to work so much and couldn’t be with me. I wanted to learn from him and I wanted him to teach me how to be a responsible man, just like him.

Years have passed. I still clearly remember those simple things that we did together. I have learned that when I become a dad, I can’t win my children’s love through gifts or money. Love is won through the time I spend with them.

qs.stem: What might be the writer’s sweetest memory?
opts: Eating ice cream with his brother.

ex.ev: My own experiences have taught me that I cared most about the simple things I did with my dad.
ex.why: 他最在乎的是和爸爸一起做的那些简单的事。

qs.stem: Where did the writer go to play soccer with his father?

ex.ev: my dad and I would go to the local park near our house and play soccer with some of his friends on a Saturday afternoon.
ex.why: 他和爸爸去家附近的公园踢足球；在院子里打的是篮球。

qs.stem: Why didn’t the writer share his feelings with his father?
opts: Because he didn’t have a proper chance.
Because he thought it was difficult to express.
Because he wanted to give his father a surprise.
Because he didn’t want to make his father feel bad.

ex.ev: because I never wanted him to feel bad that he had to work so much and couldn’t be with me.
ex.why: 他不想让爸爸因为工作忙、不能陪他而难过。

qs.stem: Which of the following can best describe the writer’s father?

ex.ev: I wanted him to teach me how to be a responsible man, just like him.
ex.why: 爸爸每周工作 70 小时养家，作者想成为像他一样负责任的人——爸爸很有责任感。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?

ex.ev: I still clearly remember those simple things that we did together.
ex.why: 和爸爸做的简单小事，却有很深的意义——「简单的事，大大的意义」。

articles.src: 2024年新乡市名校联考中考三模
articles.title: Everybody knows that protecting the environment today will p
body: Everybody knows that protecting the environment today will prepare for a better tomorrow. Kids can also be taught to do their bit for helping the environment.
A large number of people just have the water running when they are washing faces or brushing teeth.     16     Another thing kids can do is taking a shorter shower.
Video games use a lot of energy. Encourage kids to go out to play in the fresh air or finish their homework instead of playing these video games.     17
Teach kids to turn off lights when they are not in use.     18     Since kids are not told about environmental problems, they do not know they are wasting electricity.
19     Try not to use paper cups and plates whenever possible. Cutting down on use of paper wherever possible will help to save more trees. Use recycled paper.
Kids must be educated about saving the environment at a young age.     20     And we can together make a great effort to have a cleaner and greener earth.

opts: In this way, kids can save energy.
Ask your kids to try to save paper.
If kids can also play a role in helping to save the earth, it will be great.
Kids should be taught to turn off the tap when they do the same things.
Most of the time, kids will leave the lights on when they leave the classroom.

16.ev: A large number of people just have the water running when they are washing faces or brushing teeth.
16.why: 很多人洗脸刷牙时一直开着水，D「要教孩子做这些事时关掉水龙头」。

17.ev: Encourage kids to go out to play in the fresh air or finish their homework instead of playing these video games.
17.why: 让孩子出去玩、不玩电子游戏，A「这样孩子能节约能源」。

18.ev: Since kids are not told about environmental problems, they do not know they are wasting electricity.
18.why: 教孩子随手关灯，E「孩子离开教室时常常不关灯」，后面说他们不知道在浪费电。

19.ev: Try not to use paper cups and plates whenever possible.
19.why: 这一段讲少用纸杯纸盘、用再生纸，开头用 B「让孩子尽量节约用纸」。

20.ev: Kids must be educated about saving the environment at a young age.
20.why: 最后总结：孩子要从小学环保，C「如果孩子也能为拯救地球出力，那就太好了」。

cand: adj. 自然环境的；环保的

articles.src: 2024年洛阳市中考三模
articles.title: Do you find it hard to say no whenever someone asks you for help?
body: Do you find it hard to say no whenever someone asks you for help? Do you feel guilty (内疚的) when you have to tell people that you really can’t help them? If your answer is yes, you may be a “people-pleaser”.
16     It helps you build lasting friendships. However, trying to please others even at the cost of your own happiness can make you feel stressed.     17
To start with, be clear about what you are willing to take on. You can tell others that you are only available for a certain period of time.     18

When someone asks you for help, tell him or her that you need some time to think about it.You can use this time to ask yourself: Do you really want to do this?     19     In this way, you’ll be better able to decide if it’s something you have the desire (意愿) and time to do.

Some people always try to please others because they have little confidence in themselves. If so, you can try positive self-talk.     20     You don’t have to give away your time and energy to do things that don’t bring you joy.
Stopping being a people-pleaser doesn’t mean you have to give up being kind and helpful.You can still do good things—but on your own terms.

opts: How much time will it take?
You can’t be there all the time.
Being friendly and helpful is a good thing.
Remind yourself that you have dreams too.
Here are some steps to help you stop being a people-pleaser.

16.ev: It helps you build lasting friendships.
16.why: 后面说「它能帮你建立长久的友谊」，it 指 C「友善、乐于助人是好事」。

17.ev: However, trying to please others even at the cost of your own happiness can make you feel stressed.
17.why: 牺牲自己去讨好别人会有压力，接着用 E「下面几步帮你不再做讨好型的人」引出方法。

18.ev: You can tell others that you are only available for a certain period of time.
18.why: 你只在某段时间有空，B「你不可能一直在」。

19.ev: You can use this time to ask yourself: Do you really want to do this?
19.why: 问自己几个问题：真想做吗？A「要花多少时间？」后面说这样能判断有没有意愿和时间。

20.ev: If so, you can try positive self-talk.
20.why: 积极地跟自己对话，D「提醒自己：你也有自己的梦想」。

cand: adj. 可获得的；可使用的

articles.src: 2024年南阳市宛城区第三中学中考三模
articles.title: Have you ever imagined the life in space?
body: Have you ever imagined the life in space?     16
● Eating in space

If you go camping for more than a week with some friends, you will make sure you have plenty of foods and keep them properly. At the end of your camping trip, you would deal with your rubbish properly.
Astronauts almost do the same thing when they go to space. Preparation changes with the food type.
Some foods can be eaten in their natural forms, such as chocolate cakes and fruits.     17
● Sleeping in space

After a long day at work, nothing is better than a good night’s sleep! Just like on the earth, astronauts go to bed at a certain time in space.     18     When going to sleep, they have to tie themselves, so they don’t float (飘浮) around. Generally, astronauts have an eight-hour sleep each day when they finish their task.
●Doing sports in space
Exercise is an important part of every astronaut’s daily life to prevent muscle loss (肌肉萎缩).

19     Lifting 200 pounds on the earth may be a lot of work. But lifting that same object in space would be much easier. That means the things for exercise need to be specially designed, so astronauts can receive the exercise needed.
Living in space is not just all work and no play.     20     They like to look out the window and play with their food. Fun plays an important role in the quality of their life.

opts: After that, they get up and prepare for work again.
Usually, astronauts exercise two hours every day.
The following will show you the astronauts’ daily life.
Other foods require adding water, such as cheese.

16.ev: Have you ever imagined the life in space?
16.why: 开头问你想象过太空生活吗，C「下面带你看看宇航员的日常生活」引出下文。

17.ev: Some foods can be eaten in their natural forms, such as chocolate cakes and fruits.
17.why: 有些食物可以直接吃，E「另一些要加水，比如奶酪」，Some…Other 对应。

18.ev: Just like on the earth, astronauts go to bed at a certain time in space.
18.why: 按时睡觉，A「之后起床，再准备工作」。

19.ev: Exercise is an important part of every astronaut’s daily life to prevent muscle loss (肌肉萎缩).
19.why: 锻炼是宇航员每天必做的，B「宇航员通常每天锻炼两小时」。

20.ev: Living in space is not just all work and no play.
20.why: 太空生活不只有工作，D「宇航员也会玩」，后面说看窗外、玩食物。

articles.src: 2024年许昌市中考三模
articles.title: ①“In this life, what did you miss?
body: ①“In this life, what did you miss?”
②The wife asked the husband when she was 25. Despondently (沮丧地), the husband replied, “I missed a new job chance.”
③When she was 35, the husband angrily told her that he had just missed the bus.
④At the age of 45, the husband sadly said, “I missed the chance seeing my close relative before his last breath.”
⑤At 55, the husband said disappointedly, “I missed a good chance to get more money.”
⑥At 65, the husband hurriedly replied, “I missed visiting my dentist.”
⑦At75, the wife did not ask the husband any more. She was very sick. Remembering the question the wife used to ask him, this time the husband asked the wife the same question.
⑧The wife, with a smile and peaceful look, replied, “In this life, I did not miss having you!”

⑨The husband was full of tears. He always thought they could be together forever. He was always busy with work and other things. He had never thought of his wife. The husband gave a big hug to the wife and said, “Over 50 years, how I had allowed myself to miss your deep love for me!”

⑩Life does not last forever, so always live in the now. Don’t miss the loved ones who care for you. Express your thankfulness to your loved ones in words. Show your love with actions. Treat every day as the last day of life. In this way, when you are gone, your loved ones would have nothing to feel sorry about.

qs.stem: Every time the wife asked the husband what he missed in his life, the husband thought of many things EXCEPT _______.

ex.ev: He had never thought of his wife.
ex.why: 丈夫想到的是工作、公交车、亲人、钱、牙医，却从没想到妻子。

qs.stem: What did the husband realize at last?
opts: He should give his wife a big hug.
His wife loved him very much.
He should ask his wife the same question.

ex.ev: “Over 50 years, how I had allowed myself to miss your deep love for me!”
ex.why: 他终于明白妻子一直深深爱着他，自己却错过了。

qs.stem: Why was the husband full of tears in Paragraph 9?
opts: Because he was sad but loving.
Because he was moved but regretful.
Because he was joyful and excited.
Because he was angry and disappointed.

ex.ev: The husband was full of tears.
ex.why: 听到妻子说「这辈子我没错过你」，他既感动，又后悔错过了她的爱。

qs.stem: What does the writer suggest us doing in the last paragraph?
opts: Working hard to make our life better.
Expressing our love to our loved ones.
Asking our family what they missed in their life.

ex.ev: Express your thankfulness to your loved ones in words. Show your love with actions.
ex.why: 最后一段建议：用语言感谢、用行动表达对爱人的爱。

qs.stem: In what order is the text written?

articles.src: 2024年许昌市中考三模
articles.title: Last week, our school held a “Green School Project”.
body: Last week, our school held a “Green School Project”. In order to reply to the call, our class did something meaningful as a team. Some of us wrote down the whole plan. Some prepared the necessary materials. I found it was much easier and faster than doing something alone.     16     Of course, team activities aren’t always easy. In fact, they can be stressful if people don’t know how to work well together. Here are some tips to make team work successful.

17     There’s a saying, “If you don’t know where you’re going, you probably won’t get there.” So the clear goal is important. Before doing a class project, you need to check the goal and instructions carefully.

Teams work better when people have their own roles.     18     There might also be a note-taker who writes down the team’s ideas during meetings, and a time-keeper to make sure people don’t waste time chatting.

For large projects, divide the work into smaller tasks. Team members can choose tasks they do well in or enjoy. Other people might be good at writing or making reports. Of course, you shouldn’t always do the same task.     19

When you’re working in a team, respect is necessary.     20     Do your fair share, so other members don’t have to do work for you. Finally, try to stay active and enjoy yourself. Everything is easier when you’re having fun!

articles.src: 2024年南阳市镇平县中考三模
articles.title: When I was about 12, I had a classmate, a girl who liked to
body: When I was about 12, I had a classmate, a girl who liked to point out my shortcomings (缺点). Week by week her list grew: I was very thin, I wasn’t a good student, I talked too much, I was too proud, and so on. I tried to hear all these as long as I could. At last, I became very angry. I ran to my father with tears in my eyes.

He listened to me quietly, then he asked. “Are the things she said true or not? Janet, didn’t you ever wonder what you’re really like? Well, you now have that girl’s opinion. Go and make a list of everything she said and mark the points that are true. Pay no attention to the other things she said.”

I did as he told me. To my great surprise, I discovered that about half the things were true. Some of them I couldn’t change (like being very thin), but a good number I could—and suddenly I wanted to change. For the first time I got a fairly clear picture of myself.

I brought the list back to Daddy. He refused to take it. “That’s just for you,” he said. “You know better than anyone else the truth about yourself. But you have to learn to listen, not just close your ears in anger and feeling hurt. When something said about you is true, you’ll find it will be of some help to you. Our world is full of people who think they know your duty. Don’t shut your ears. Listen to them all, but hear the truth and do what you know is the right thing to do.”
Daddy’s advice has returned to me at many important moments. In my life, I’ve never had a better piece of advice.

qs.stem: Why did the writer run to her father with tears?

ex.ev: At last, I became very angry. I ran to my father with tears in my eyes.
ex.why: 同学一直挑她的毛病，她又生气又难过，哭着跑去找爸爸——她受伤了。

ex.ev: To my great surprise, I discovered that about half the things were true.
ex.why: 她非常惊讶地发现大约一半是真的。

qs.stem: What advice did Daddy give Janet?
opts: To close her ears in anger.
To ask for advice from others.

ex.ev: Listen to them all, but hear the truth and do what you know is the right thing to do.
ex.why: 爸爸让她别生气堵住耳朵，要听进真话。

qs.stem: How has Daddy’s advice helped Janet?
opts: It has helped her to make friends.
It has helped her to become proud.
It has helped her to become a good student.
It has helped her in many important moments.

ex.ev: Daddy’s advice has returned to me at many important moments.
ex.why: 在很多重要时刻，她都会想起爸爸的建议。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?

ex.why: 全文围绕爸爸给她的建议，结尾说这是她听过最好的建议——「爸爸的建议」。

articles.src: 2024年南阳市镇平县中考三模
articles.title: There are many colours in nature.
body: [图:reading/aff81642/image2.png]
There are many colours in nature. But do you know if a colour has weight? I think you’ll say “no”.     32     If you don’t believe, you may do a small experiment.

First, put two objects with the same weight into two boxes.     33     Third, wrap one box with a red piece of paper, the other with a white piece of paper. OK. Now hold the boxes with your hand one by one. It is certain that you will think the red one is a little heavier.

Why do you think so? A scientist found that different colours have different weight in a man’s mind.     34     That is to say, every colour has its own weight in our mind and their order is the same.

The heaviest colour is red, then blue, green, orange, yellow and white. The scientist told us that colours also have smell. Can you smell the colour? Of course not.     35     That is because every colour stands for a kind of light with a certain wave length. It reaches our brain through sense organs (器官).

According to this discovery, scientists say that people accept the colours they like, and refuse the colours they hate. So your body and mind will be healthy by using the colours you like.     36     For example, if you stay in a room with red windows, wallpapers and furniture for two hours, you’ll feel you have been there for four hours. But if the room is blue, you’ll feel you have been there for only an hour. Another example, if a person walks out of a red room and into a blue room, his temperature will fall. That means our body temperature will change with different colours.

opts: But I am afraid you are wrong.
Then why did the scientist say so?
Or you’ll be nervous or even get ill.
So he did many tests and at last he got the result.

32.ev: But do you know if a colour has weight? I think you’ll say “no”.
32.why: 你会说颜色没有重量，B「但恐怕你错了」，后面让你做实验。

33.ev: First, put two objects with the same weight into two boxes.
33.why: First…Third…，中间是第二步：A「然后把盒子盖上」。

34.ev: That is to say, every colour has its own weight in our mind and their order is the same.
34.why: 科学家发现颜色在人心里有不同重量，E「于是他做了很多测试，最后得出结果」。

35.ev: That is because every colour stands for a kind of light with a certain wave length.
35.why: 我们闻不到颜色，C「那科学家为什么这么说呢？」后面 That is because 回答。

36.ev: So your body and mind will be healthy by using the colours you like.
36.why: 用喜欢的颜色身心健康，D「否则你会紧张甚至生病」。

articles.src: 2024年实验中学中考二模
articles.title: On the top of a tree, an old eagle raised her young.
body: On the top of a tree, an old eagle raised her young. She got her food from the ocean, but this tree stood ten miles from the beach. It had long been known as the “Old Eagle Tree”.

On a warm, sunny day, the workmen were working in the fields. At a certain hour of the day, the old eagle was known to leave for the seaside to get food for her young. As she returned with a large fish, the workmen stood around the tree, shouting and throwing stones. They scared the poor bird. So she dropped her fish, and they carried it off.

The bird soon returned to her home without food. The babies at once started to cry for food. The parent bird seemed to try to comfort them, but the babies were so hungry that she couldn’t calm them down. She then stood near the babies, and looked down into the home in a manner that seemed to say, “I don’t know what to do next.” A minute later, she spread her wings and was away again for the sea.

She was away for nearly two hours, about double her usual time for a trip. When she again returned on slow, weak wings, she flew uncommonly low to have more air to support her with another fish in her claws. On nearing the field, she flew around it to see if her enemies were again there. Finding the field clear, she once again reached the tree. Again the baby eagles began to cry. But soon they became quiet, busy having their big meal.
What a great bird! We can learn a lesson from her. Others might give up, but this bird, at once recovering (恢复) from the loss, has tried her best to finish her task.

qs.stem: How did the workmen get the fish?
opts: They happened to meet the eagle with fish by accident.
They shouted and threw stones to frighten the eagle away.
They followed the eagle to the seaside and returned with her.
They worked in the fields and waited for eagle at the same time.

ex.ev: As she returned with a large fish, the workmen stood around the tree, shouting and throwing stones.
ex.why: 工人们围着树大喊、扔石头，吓得老鹰把鱼丢了，他们就把鱼拿走了。

qs.stem: What is the correct order according to the story? a. The workmen scared the eagle away and got the food. b. The eagle flew to the seaside to get food for her young. c. The babies were disappointed and cried for food at once. d. The eagle flew to the sea again and returned with another fish.

ex.why: 顺序：老鹰去海边找食物（b）→ 工人吓跑老鹰拿走鱼（a）→ 小鹰饿得马上哭（c）→ 老鹰又飞去海边带回一条鱼（d）。

qs.stem: Which picture can best express the eagle’s feeling in the underlined sentence?

ex.ev: and looked down into the home in a manner that seemed to say, “I don’t know what to do next.”
ex.why: 「我不知道接下来该怎么办」是发愁、着急的样子，C 图是冒汗发愁的表情。

qs.stem: Why did the eagle double her usual time for the trip the second time?
opts: Because she wanted to wait until the workmen left.
Because it was so hard for her to find another fish.
Because she was too tired to finish the trip as usual.
Because she didn’t know how to avoid the workmen.

ex.ev: When she again returned on slow, weak wings, she flew uncommonly low to have more air to support her with another fish in her claws.
ex.why: 她回来时翅膀又慢又无力，飞得特别低，可见她太累了，所以这一趟用了平时两倍的时间。

qs.stem: What does the writer mainly want to tell us in the story?
opts: The hard time in life can make one wise and strong.
Don’t cry over spilt milk and try your best to get what you want.
The most important thing for a parent is to raise the young babies.
Love for babies can encourage one to overcome all the difficulties.

ex.ev: Others might give up, but this bird, at once recovering (恢复) from the loss, has tried her best to finish her task.
ex.why: 老鹰没有为丢了鱼难过太久，马上振作起来再去捕鱼——不要为失去的东西难过，要尽力去争取。

articles.src: 2024年洛阳市中考二模
articles.title: Recently, Luoyang Tengfei Middle School in Henan held an activity.
body: Recently, Luoyang Tengfei Middle School in Henan held an activity. It asked students to tell the stories of their family heirlooms (传家宝). More than 300 students took part in the activity. They brought photos of their heirlooms to school and shared their stories. Here are the results from three students.
Name   Age   Heirloom   Owner   Prize
Sun Chenxi   14   Cassette radio   Grandmother   The first prize

“My grandmother bought the radio in the 1980s and listened to the news on it.” “My mother used it to listen to music and old poems for me on the radio.” “There are now many more cool players. But we still keep this cassette radio because it recorded beautiful memories of my family.”
Yao Xue   14   Food coupons   Grandmother   The first prize

“My grandmother used to tell her stories about food shortages (短缺) when she was a kid.” “Back then, even buying rice needed a special ticket.” Without the ticket, they can’t buy things they need. “My grandma wants me to be thankful for what we have today and work hard for a better tomorrow.”
Guo Xingke   13   Medal of honor   Grandfather   The first prize

“My grandfather took part in the War to Resist Us Aggression and Aid Korea (抗美援朝战争).” “The medal stands as an honor for my family.” “Whenever I see my grandfather’s medal, I feel very proud. In my heart, my great grandfather is a hero. I see him as an example and will make my country a better place in his honor.”

qs.stem: Which photo is not mentioned in the passage?

ex.why: 文中的传家宝是收音机、粮票和奖章，C 图的古钱币没有提到。

qs.stem: Why does Sun Chenxi and his family still keep the cassette radio?
opts: Because it stands as an honor for her family.
Because her grandma wants her to be thankful.
Because her grandmother likes to listen to music on it.
Because it brings back her family's beautiful memories.

ex.ev: But we still keep this cassette radio because it recorded beautiful memories of my family.
ex.why: 现在有很多更酷的播放器，但还留着它，因为它记录了家里美好的回忆。

qs.stem: Whose heirlooms are about people's daily life in the past?

ex.ev: “Back then, even buying rice needed a special ticket.”
ex.why: 收音机用来听新闻、听音乐，粮票用来买米，都和过去的日常生活有关；奖章是荣誉。

qs.stem: What’s the purpose of the activity held in Tengfei Middle School in Henan?
opts: To let the students get the prizes by telling stories.
To learn from the past and care for the present life.
To know how much money the heirlooms are worth.
To know how many families have their own heirlooms.

ex.ev: “My grandma wants me to be thankful for what we have today and work hard for a better tomorrow.”
ex.why: 讲传家宝的故事，是为了了解过去、珍惜现在的生活。

qs.stem: Where is the passage most probably from?

ex.ev: Recently, Luoyang Tengfei Middle School in Henan held an activity.

articles.src: 2024年洛阳市中考二模
articles.title: In daily life, people often talk about sadness and happiness.
body: In daily life, people often talk about sadness and happiness. Most people want themselves to be happy forever, but few know how to find happiness.     16     However, money and success alone do not bring lasting happiness. A famous Greek thinker, Aristotle said, “Happiness depends on ourselves.” That is to say, we make our own happiness.     17

The first secret of happiness is to enjoy the simple things in life. Too often, we spend so much time thinking about the future.     18     We fail to enjoy the present time. You should enjoy life’s simple pleasures, such as reading a book, listening to your favorite music or spending time with close friends. People who have several close friends often live happier.
19     Many people go dancing or play sports. People can forget about their problems and only think about the activities.

Finally, many people find happiness in helping others. Studies show that people feel good when they spend their time helping others.     20     You can help a friend with his or her studies, go shopping, or help an elderly person.请你

opts: Here are a few suggestions to help you be happier.
Another secret of living a happy life is to be active.
For example, getting into college or getting a good job.
If you want to feel happier, do good things for someone.
Some people say if they own lots of money and success, they will be happy.

16.ev: However, money and success alone do not bring lasting happiness.
16.why: 后面 However 说钱和成功不能带来长久的快乐，前面应是 E「有人说拥有很多钱和成功就会快乐」。

17.ev: That is to say, we make our own happiness.
17.why: 快乐靠自己创造，A「下面几条建议帮你更快乐」引出后面几段。

18.ev: Too often, we spend so much time thinking about the future.
18.why: 我们总想着将来，C「比如考上大学、找到好工作」举例说明「将来」。

19.ev: Many people go dancing or play sports.
19.why: 前面讲第一个秘诀，这里 B「快乐生活的另一个秘诀是积极活跃」，后面说跳舞、运动。

20.why: 帮助别人让人感觉好，D「想更快乐，就为别人做点好事」，后面举例。

articles.src: 2024年焦作市中考二模
articles.title: The 2022 Beijing Winter Olympic Games were not only a sports
body: The 2022 Beijing Winter Olympic Games were not only a sports meeting, but also a party of delicious food.     32     The most popular foods in Olympic Villages were dishes including beef, roast duck, and of course, dumplings.

It is not only the players’ competitions, but also their love of Chinese food. Videos of China’s 18-year-old Gu Ailing eating a steamed bun (馒头) became popular. Chinese people were also surprised by the love for steamed buns by a player Jenise Spiteri.     33
US player Julia Marino said she loves dumplings best. She caught Chinese fans by surprise. “     34     It’s the only thing I feel like is always good,” she said in an interview.
Even Thomas Bach, the president of the International Olympic Committee, said that he ate many dumplings and grew fatter.     35

Yang Chen, a cook of players’ restaurant at the Yanqing Olympic Village, said that the menu in the village took turns every eight days, and 30 percent of the dishes were Chinese, while 70 percent were Western. He mentioned that some foreign players had no idea of how to eat Chinese food, so restaurant workers would offer help.     36     I believe more foreign people will know about our food culture through this Games.

He also said that he liked spicier (辛辣的) food better.
I’ve probably had 200 dumplings since I’ve been here.
We also hope to spread Chinese food culture through this chance.
It is known to us that China is well-known across the world for its different kinds of food.

33.why: 这位选手很爱吃馒头，A「她说她每天吃六个馒头」。

34.why: 她最爱饺子，C「我来这儿以后大概吃了 200 个饺子」，后面说饺子总是很好吃。

articles.title: Tiangong Class takes the name for the Chinese space station.
body: Tiangong Class takes the name for the Chinese space station. To catch students’ interest in science and space, Chinese astronauts work as teachers and give students lessons from space.

articles.src: 2024年平顶山市中考二模
articles.title: In Chinese culture, name plays an important role in people’s life.
body: In Chinese culture, name plays an important role in people’s life. Parents want to choose a good name for their baby.     32

There is a family name and a given name in a Chinese name.     33     Chinese “surnames” (family name) come first when written, different from the Western name order. The most common surnames are Wang and Li.

Almost all Chinese given names are made up of one or two Chinese characters, which are written after the surnames.     34     Some of these people have their mother’s family name as the first character of their given names.

A Chinese generation (一代，一辈) name is one of the characters in a standard two-character Chinese given name. Especially in a big traditional Chinese family, you will see many young boys or girls sharing the same generation character in their given names.     35

Given names of a certain year often commemorate (纪念) some important event. For example, Jianguo (Establish Country) was used by many babies born during the year that Modern China was founded (1949). Most Chinese given names have meanings of “happiness”, “beauty”, or “good wishes”.     36     When a family name and a given name join together, some of them can be very funny. For example, a man whose family name is Qian (Money) could have the full name Qian Duo (Money Much), which means “lots of money”!

opts: The family name comes first followed by a given name.
Only a few people have three characters for their given names.
They believe good names will bring good luck to their children.
For example, Li Zuyang and Li Zuli share the same character “Zu”.
Many Chinese characters have the same pronunciation but different meanings.

32.ev: Parents want to choose a good name for their baby.
32.why: 父母想给孩子取个好名字，C「他们相信好名字会给孩子带来好运」。

33.ev: Chinese “surnames” (family name) come first when written, different from the Western name order.
33.why: 中国名字有姓有名，A「姓在前，名在后」，后面接着说和西方顺序不同。

34.ev: Some of these people have their mother’s family name as the first character of their given names.
34.why: 名字一般一两个字，B「只有少数人的名是三个字」，后面说这些人有的把母亲的姓放进名里。

35.ev: you will see many young boys or girls sharing the same generation character in their given names.
35.why: 很多孩子名字里有同一个辈分字，D「比如李祖阳和李祖立都有一个“祖”字」。

36.ev: For example, a man whose family name is Qian (Money) could have the full name Qian Duo (Money Much), which means “lots of money”!
36.why: 钱多 = 钱多，E「很多汉字发音相同、意思不同」，所以姓名连起来有的很有趣。

articles.src: 2024年郑州市四中教育集团中考二模
articles.title: Pen Pals for 80 Years Twice a month, Nona Avery sits down, p
body: Pen Pals for 80 Years

Twice a month, Nona Avery sits down, picks up her pen and writes a letter to her best friend. The British woman has been doing it for 80 years. she has sent more than 1,500 letters to her pen pal in America.

The hobby started in 1942, Nona, then 12, was reading a magazine. Some ads in the magazine were asking for pen pals. One of them caught Nona’s eye. It was from Alice Powers. She lived in America and was also 12. “I was very excited,” Nona said, “I sat down immediately, wrote a letter, put it in an envelope—together with a picture of myself and posted it.”

Nona spent every day waiting for the postman. Two weeks later—which felt like a lifetime—a reply dropped through the letterbox. “I was overjoyed,” Nona said. “There was a letter and a picture of my new friend. She was all the way on the other side of the world!”
Nona and Alice wanted to learn more about each other. They kept writing. The two found that they had a lot in common. They liked the same books and the same films.

However, both Nona and Alice were too poor to afford a plane ticket. It was not until 1987 that they met. “I was excited to see the person I had been writing to for four decades,” Nona said. “We had a big hug and then sat down, chatting for hours.”

Now in their nineties, Nona and Alice are still writing to each other. And they still write by hand. “Writing is much more intimate, So why shall we change the habit of a lifetime?” Nona said. “I’m so glad that I wrote that first letter 80 years ago.”

qs.stem: When did Nona Avery and Alice Powers become pen pals?

ex.ev: The hobby started in 1942, Nona, then 12, was reading a magazine.
ex.why: 1942 年 Nona 12 岁时开始和笔友通信。1987 年是她们第一次见面。

qs.stem: Where did Nona first see Alice’s information?

ex.ev: Some ads in the magazine were asking for pen pals.
ex.why: 她在杂志上的征笔友广告里看到了 Alice 的信息。

qs.stem: The underlined word “overjoyed” (in paragraph 3) probably means “________.”

ex.ev: “There was a letter and a picture of my new friend.
ex.why: 等了两周终于收到回信和照片，她非常高兴——overjoyed 就是「非常开心」。

qs.stem: According to the article, what did Nona and Alice have in common? ①They liked the same films. ②They were of the same age. ③They liked the same books. ④They liked the same movie stars.

ex.ev: They liked the same books and the same films.
ex.why: 她们喜欢同样的书和电影，而且都是 12 岁——①②③。文中没提电影明星。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the last paragraph?
opts: Nona and Alice will keep writing by hand.
Nona doesn’t know how to use a computer.
Nona and Alice will write to each other by email.

ex.ev: And they still write by hand.
ex.why: 九十多岁了还在手写信，还说「为什么要改变一辈子的习惯」——她们会继续手写。

articles.src: 2024年郑州陈中实验学校中考二模
articles.title: Rong Zichen, 13, Chengdu Sichuan Students from different cou
body: [图:reading/fb61be83/image6.png]Rong Zichen, 13, Chengdu   Sichuan Students from different countries share what their school day is like. So I made a report about their school day life.

[图:reading/fb61be83/image7.png]Amelia Gon, 12. The American School Foundation   Every morning I get up early to catch the bus. I get to school at about 7: 15 am. After meeting with my friends, we go to our classes. The first class starts at 7: 45. All my classes are 1 hour and 15 minutes long. Between classes, we have a 5-minute break. After the first class, I go to homeroom for 30 minutes. Then, it’s time for a break! I eat snacks (零食) and talk with friends. At 10: 00, I walk to my next class. At 11: 30, the third class starts and lunch starts at 12: 50. After lunch, I have the last class, then I take the bus home.

[图:reading/fb61be83/image8.png]Chelsea Wang, 13. Barker College   My day starts with my debate (辩论) practice at home because I am on my school debate team. The first class starts at 9: 45 a.m. Normally, we have seven classes on Tuesday and six classes on the other school days. The children go to different classrooms for the different subjects. In different classes, we can meet different friends. It is great!

[图:reading/fb61be83/image9.png]Niu Hanliang, 15. Western Boarding Schools   Our classes in school end at 3: 15 pm. You also can go to clubs like drama club and the school band from Monday to Thursday. My classes start at 9: 30 am. Monday through Wednesday, we have three classes in the morning. At about 12, we have lunch for about an hour. After that, we have two more classes. At 3 pm, classes end and tutorial (辅导) will start. You can go to any teacher if you have questions. After tutorial ends, I will go to cross country or tennis practice. We have Friday afternoons off.

qs.stem: When does Amelia’s second class begin?

ex.ev: At 11: 30, the third class starts and lunch starts at 12: 50.
ex.why: 第三节 11:30 开始，每节课 1 小时 15 分钟，课间 5 分钟，往前推：第二节 10:10 开始。

qs.stem: Why does Chelsea’s day start with the debate practice?
opts: Because her class begins at 9: 15 am.
Because she has to catch the early bus.
Because she is on her school debate team.
Because she wants to meet different friends.

ex.ev: My day starts with my debate (辩论) practice at home because I am on my school debate team.
ex.why: 她是学校辩论队的成员，所以每天先练辩论。

qs.stem: What may Niu Hanliang do Friday afternoon?

ex.ev: We have Friday afternoons off.
ex.why: 周五下午不上课，最可能在家写作业。辅导课和两节课都是周一到周三的安排；辩论是 Chelsea 的事。

qs.stem: How many class does Chelsea have on Monday?

ex.ev: Normally, we have seven classes on Tuesday and six classes on the other school days.
ex.why: 周二七节，其他上学日六节，周一是六节。

qs.stem: What’s the purpose of the text?
opts: To ask students to join school clubs.
To tell students to make more friends.
To present ideas about different subjects.

ex.ev: Students from different countries share what their school day is like.
ex.why: 几个不同国家的学生介绍自己的一天——介绍不同的学校生活。

articles.src: 2024年郑州陈中实验学校中考二模
articles.title: Lifestyles of children around the world are very different.
body: Lifestyles of children around the world are very different.
In Colombia, family relationships are strong and children usually live close to their parents all their lives.     32     Colombian children like to play chess. They play the game well.

Children in Sweden experience a different lifestyle. Their school day begins at 8:15 a.m. and most of them cycle to school. After school, many of them go to clubs or take part in sport until their parents pick them up. In the summer, days are long and nights are short.     33

Traditional opinions influence the lives of many children and this is also true in Japan. Japanese children today are surrounded by the very latest and most modern inventions and technologies.     34     They are also expected to study hard and succeed in life.

The children of Uganda also enjoy parties and special days but these parties are organized for them by the “Save the Children Fund”, rather than by their parents.     35     Because of this, many children have lost one or both of their parents to the disease called AIDS. During the weekends, they join group meetings that are run by trained volunteers. These groups give children the chance to play with one another.
36     However, whatever their lifestyles, children should be loved and supported, especially during the early years of their lives.

opts: Large families often live in the same house.
The lives of children are different all over the world.
This is because their country is facing a health crisis.
However, their lives are still influenced by the traditions.

32.ev: In Colombia, family relationships are strong and children usually live close to their parents all their lives.
32.why: 哥伦比亚家庭关系紧密，孩子一辈子住在父母附近，B「大家庭常住在一起」。

33.ev: In the summer, days are long and nights are short.
33.why: 瑞典夏天白天长，A「一家人在户外一起过」。

34.ev: Japanese children today are surrounded by the very latest and most modern inventions and technologies.
34.why: 日本孩子身边都是最新科技，E「但他们的生活仍受传统影响」，和这段第一句对应。

35.ev: Because of this, many children have lost one or both of their parents to the disease called AIDS.
35.why: 后面「因为这个，很多孩子因艾滋病失去父母」，前面应是 D「因为他们国家正面临健康危机」。

36.ev: However, whatever their lifestyles, children should be loved and supported,
36.why: 最后一段总结，先说 C「世界各地孩子的生活各不相同」，再用 However 转折。

cand: pron. 无论什么；任何事物

articles.src: 2024年南阳市、名校联考中考二模
articles.title: Lin Yi’s Lantern: A Moon Festival Tale $8.
body: [图:reading/c74a9dbc/image6.png]   Lin Yi’s Lantern: A Moon Festival Tale   $8.99 Lin Yi goes to the market to buy things for the Moon Festival. Towards the end of his trip, he realizes that he doesn’t have enough money to buy both peanuts(花生) for his uncle and a red rabbit lantern for himself. He takes peanuts home at last and surprisingly, his uncle arrives with a gift --- a red rabbit lantern.

[图:reading/c74a9dbc/image7.png]   The Discovery of Fireworks and Gunpowder   $16.95 Dao, a red panda, can travel through time and space. He guides two school kids, Ethan and Emma, back in time to discover how fireworks and gunpowder(火药) were made! As Dao leads the way, the kids learn about surprising historical facts, travel to ancient China and go back to the future.

[图:reading/c74a9dbc/image8.png]   The Moon Lady   $7.99 On a rainy afternoon, three sisters wish for the rain to stop. Ying-Ying, their grandmother, tells them a story: on one night of the Moon Festival when Ying-Ying was a little girl, she met the Moon Lady and learned from her that the best wishes were those you could make come true yourself.

[图:reading/c74a9dbc/image9.png]   A Gift for My Sister   $ 16.95 A gift has come for Amy in time for Chinese New Year. Since Amy’s aunt and uncles live in China and are not able to make a new-year visit, they have sent Amy a special gift to show their love and their wish to keep the family together.

qs.stem: How may Lin Yi feel when he sees what his uncle takes?

ex.ev: He takes peanuts home at last and surprisingly, his uncle arrives with a gift --- a red rabbit lantern.
ex.why: 他把钱给叔叔买了花生，没想到叔叔送来的正是他想要的兔子灯，他会很兴奋。

qs.stem: What can we learn from The Moon Lady?
opts: Everyone should make their wishes come true by themselves.
It’s important for children to learn some history.

ex.ev: she met the Moon Lady and learned from her that the best wishes were those you could make come true yourself.
ex.why: 她从月亮女神那里明白：最好的愿望是自己能实现的——要靠自己实现愿望。

qs.stem: What did Amy’s elder sister sent her a gift for?

ex.ev: A gift has come for Amy in time for Chinese New Year.
ex.why: 礼物是春节前寄到的，是为了春节（题干说的「姐姐」原文其实是姑姑叔叔，不影响答案）。

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is true?
opts: The Discovery of Fireworks and Gunpowder is not as cheap as The Moon Lady.
A red rabbit helps Ethan and Emma travel back in time to ancient China.
Amy’s sister couldn’t come back home because she was abroad for business.
Ying Ying wishes for the rain to stop.

ex.ev: The Discovery of Fireworks and Gunpowder   $16.95
ex.why: 《烟花与火药的发现》16.95 美元，比《月亮女神》7.99 美元贵。带孩子穿越的是小熊猫；许愿雨停的是三姐妹。

qs.stem: Who is the text written for?

ex.why: 介绍几本关于中国节日、文化的故事书，适合青少年读。

cand: adj. 令人惊讶的；出乎意料的
adj. 历史的；有关历史的

articles.title: It was sunny last Sunday.
body: It was sunny last Sunday. David went to the park with his brother. They got there at 8:00 by bus. There were lots of people doing morning exercises. Soon David found there were lots of empty bottles and paper bags in the park. David and his brother decided to clean the park. They picked them up and threw them into the dustbins(垃圾箱). They worked hard. About two hours later, the park was clean again.

At last they made a sign, saying “ No littering ” in the park. They wanted people to keep the park clean. After that, they went to restaurant nearby to have lunch. They had two large bowls of beef noodles there, and then went home. Though they were very tired, they felt very happy.

qs.stem: The weather was ______ last Sunday.

ex.ev: It was sunny last Sunday.
ex.why: 第一句：上周日是晴天。

qs.stem: David and his brother took a ______ to the park.

ex.ev: They got there at 8:00 by bus.
ex.why: 他们坐公交车 8 点到公园。

qs.stem: David and his brother spent about ______ cleaning the park.

ex.ev: About two hours later, the park was clean again.
ex.why: 大约两小时后，公园又干净了。

qs.stem: What’s the meaning of  “ No littering ”?

ex.ev: They wanted people to keep the park clean.
ex.why: 他们想让人们保持公园干净——No littering 是「禁止乱扔垃圾」。

qs.stem: Which of the following is TRUE?
opts: There were few people in the park.
David got to the park at 9:00 last Sunday.
David and his brother had lunch in a restaurant.
Both of them were unhappy because they were too tired.

ex.ev: After that, they went to restaurant nearby to have lunch.
ex.why: 他们去附近的饭馆吃了午饭。公园里人很多；8 点到的；虽然累但很开心。

cand: adj. 阳光充足的；晴朗的

articles.src: 2024年洛阳市宜阳县中考二模
articles.title: Jia Ling is popular with people of all ages.
body: Jia Ling is popular with people of all ages. She had been quietly working on her fitness journey for the past one and a half years. Before the Spring Festival, the well-known star shared that she lost weight for a new movie role during her break.

In 2021, Jia Ling directed her first film Hi, Mom!, which turned out to be a huge success. The movie made $1.12 billion and became the third most-watched movie in China. The film told a warm story between mother and daughter, which moved so many people.
In 2023, she announced her new project titled YOLO (《热辣滚烫》), in which she will serve as both director and lead actress.

Pictures from the movie were introduced to the public, and Jia Ling looks totally different in them. According to Jia Ling, she worked hard and lost 50 kg in six months to play a boxer (拳击手) through strict training and hard work.

People were shocked by her change, with some wondering how difficult it was to go through with the process. “I’m super envious (羡慕的) of those who have the strength to put their mind to losing so much weight,” a message left on the Internet. Others also left messages reminding Jia Ling to take care of her health.
The film was shown in most cinemas. Now you can see it on the Internet. If you are interested, it’s a good idea to see the film with your family together.

qs.stem: Why did Jia Ling lose weight?

ex.ev: the well-known star shared that she lost weight for a new movie role during her break.
ex.why: 她是为了新电影里的角色减肥的。

qs.stem: How is Hi, Mom!?
opts: It was directed by Jia Ling’s friends.
It is the most popular movie in China.

ex.ev: In 2021, Jia Ling directed her first film Hi, Mom!, which turned out to be a huge success.
ex.why: 《你好，李焕英》非常成功，是中国观影人数第三的电影，不是第一。

qs.stem: Which word can describe Jia Ling best according to the passage?

ex.ev: she worked hard and lost 50 kg in six months to play a boxer (拳击手) through strict training and hard work.
ex.why: 通过严格训练、刻苦努力，半年减了 50 公斤——非常勤奋。

qs.stem: What’s people’s attitude (态度) towards Jia Ling?

ex.ev: Others also left messages reminding Jia Ling to take care of her health.
ex.why: 网友羡慕她的毅力，还提醒她注意身体——大家是支持她的。

qs.stem: What is the purpose of this text?

ex.ev: Jia Ling is popular with people of all ages.
ex.why: 全文介绍演员贾玲：她的电影、减肥、大家对她的看法。

articles.src: 2024年洛阳市宜阳县中考二模
articles.title: If you are in school or at university, you will surely have
body: If you are in school or at university, you will surely have made the experience that there are students of different levels. Some students are good at studying, while others are not. How can you become part of the group of great and outstanding students?

16     An outstanding student is a person who has a natural curiosity and sees things differently. He asks interesting questions, tries to connect things and link what he has learnt in class with other experiences.     17

You should not focus first on the grades. You don’t start with good grades, but you try to do your best in studying and other things you care about. During the practice, you may find out that you become clever and outstanding.
18     The more knowledge you have, the more you are able to connect these different parts, facts and relations in unusual ways. In this way, you become better at solving problems.     19

If you don’t have to spend too much time on random (随机的) facts, because you really understand them, then you can focus on the problem at hand. It can also save a lot of time.     20     As a result, you will achieve high grades.
It is true what they say: the more you know, the more you want to know.

opts: He always has many ideas and likes to have a try.
Then you’ll come up with exciting answers.
You can only have creative ideas about things you know.
In an exam, you can easily solve the questions asked.

16.ev: An outstanding student is a person who has a natural curiosity and sees things differently.
16.why: 后面解释什么是优秀学生，前面先问 B「什么是优秀学生？」

17.ev: He asks interesting questions, tries to connect things and link what he has learnt in class with other experiences.
17.why: 接着描述优秀学生，A「他总有很多想法，喜欢尝试」，主语还是 he。

18.ev: The more knowledge you have, the more you are able to connect these different parts, facts and relations in unusual ways.
18.why: 知识越多越能把东西联系起来，D「你只能对你了解的东西有创造性想法」。

19.ev: In this way, you become better at solving problems.
19.why: 更会解决问题，C「然后你就会想出令人兴奋的答案」。

20.ev: As a result, you will achieve high grades.
20.why: 后面说「结果你会取得好成绩」，前面应是 E「考试时，你能轻松答出题目」。

cand: adj. 不寻常的；与众不同的

articles.src: 2025年鹤壁市中考一模
articles.title: Jamal retied his running shoes for the third time.
body: Jamal retied his running shoes for the third time. All month he’d been talking about his first 5K race and how he was going to come in first in his age group. Several of his friends from school had come out to watch or run the race too.[图:reading/298129fc/image2.png]
“You ready?” Christian asked.

“Yeah, no problem.” Jamal did a few warm-up stretches (热身) to cover up the fact that his hands were shaking. He’d trained for this race, but there were so many people both in the race and watching. What if he didn’t win his age group? What if he tripped and fell?
A whistle (哨声) blew and the starter called everyone to the starting line.
“I’ll try to keep you in sight,” Christian said, “but you’re a lot faster than I am.” He leaned closer. “I’m kind of just hoping I can finish the race without having to stop.”

Jamal clapped Christian on the back. “Don’t go out too fast and you’ll be fine. It doesn’t matter what place you finish in. The run is for a good cause.” The school was raising money for a teacher who had lost his house in a hurricane.
Christian nodded. “Right. Let’s do this for Mr. Martin.”
Jamal stood on the starting line and noticed Mr. Martin next to him.
“Thanks for getting so many of your classmates to come out today, Jamal.” Mr. Martin said. “No matter what place you come in, you’re a winner in my book.”

The starting buzzer sounded and Jamal took off, thinking of Mr. Martin’s words. After the first mile, Jamal glanced back and saw Christian grabbing (抓着) his side. He must have had a cramp (抽筋). Mr. Martin was still next to Jamal, matching his pace with each step.
“We’re all winners, right?” Jamal asked Mr. Martin between breaths.
Mr. Martin looked back at Christian and a few other students falling behind. “Every single one of you.”
Jamal nodded and ran back to Christian and the others. “Arms up over your heads and take long slow breaths,” Jamal said.
His friends listened.
“Good. Now move your arms again and focus on your breathing.” Jamal continued to coach his friends until he saw the finish line. “There’s the end. Come on, guys. Let’s finish this together.”
They crossed the finish line as a group and found Mr. Martin waiting for them. “Why did you come back for us, Jamal?” Christian asked, still out of breath. “You could have won.”
“________,” Jamal said, smiling at Mr. Martin.

qs.stem: Why were Jamal’s hands shaking at first?
opts: Because he was warming up for the race.
Because he was too tired because of training.
Because he was too cold because of the weather.
Because he was very nervous as he wanted to win.

ex.ev: What if he didn’t win his age group? What if he tripped and fell?
ex.why: 他担心拿不到第一、怕摔倒——是因为想赢而紧张，才手发抖。

qs.stem: What advice did Jamal give Christian before the race?
opts: Run as fast as you can.

ex.ev: “Don’t go out too fast and you’ll be fine.
ex.why: 他建议 Christian「开头别跑太快」。

qs.stem: What was the purpose of the race?
opts: To find the best runners in the school.
To raise money for a teacher in trouble.
To encourage the students to do exercise.

ex.ev: The school was raising money for a teacher who had lost his house in a hurricane.
ex.why: 学校在为一位房子被飓风毁掉的老师筹款。

qs.stem: Why did Jamal run back to Christian and the others?
opts: He was told to offer help.
He was too tired to finish alone.
He wanted to show off his speed.
He wanted to win together with them.

ex.ev: “We’re all winners, right?” Jamal asked Mr. Martin between breaths.
ex.why: 老师说每个人都是赢家，他就回去陪落后的同学，想和大家一起完成比赛。

qs.stem: What would Jamal say possibly at the end of the story?

ex.ev: Mr. Martin looked back at Christian and a few other students falling behind. “Every single one of you.”
ex.why: 老师说过每个人都是赢家，所以最后 Jamal 会说「我们都是赢家」。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县第七教研区中考一模
articles.title: Are you an “I” person or an “E” person?
body: Are you an “I” person or an “E” person? People have talked about it a lot online recently. They are part of a popular personality test called MBTI.
Everyone’s result has four letters. “I” and “E” are the first letters. People are either “I”, meaning introverted (内向的), or “E”, for extroverted (外向的).

But sometimes introverted people can be extroverted, too. For example, an “I” person will go out with a group of introverted friends. The person may do things that a more “extroverted” person would do. For example, he or she may share their thoughts and feelings with others.
Don’t label yourself just for MBTI results. The personality test is just for fun. Everyone’s personality is different. Don’t let the test tell you who you are.

For example, you did the test and got your results. At the same time, you would be very curious (好奇的) about your friends’ MBTI results. You would get upset if their results didn’t match the way you see them.
Soon, you think everyone might have a “personality stamp (特征)”. For example, “P” people don’t like to make plans. On the other hand, “J” people are planners and list-makers.
Do we really need to be worried about the result? In fact, the four letters don’t tell you everything about a person. And no one should live according to what the four letters tell you.

ex.ev: They are part of a popular personality test called MBTI.
ex.why: MBTI 是一种很流行的性格测试。

articles.title: Some people think they know everything.
body: Some people think they know everything. Anansi, the spider didn’t think that. He was a clever spider. And he knew that to have real wisdom, he had to learn more.

One day, Anansi found an empty gourd (葫芦) on the ground and he had an idea. “If I get advice from others and put it in this gourd, then I’ll be wiser than anyone else in the world.” So, he went from house to house and asked the other animals, “What’s your best piece of advice?” And they were all happy to share their wisdom, because they could see that Anansi needed it.
The snail (蜗牛) said, “Don’t be in a hurry. Life is not a 100-meter race.”
The butterfly said, “Life is short. Enjoy every day.”
The ant said, “You’ll never be great on your own. Everyone needs the help of others.”

Anansi was very happy with all the advice. He took it and put it in his gourd. And when he’d filled the gourd, he thought to himself, “Now, I have more wisdom than anyone else, I must hide the wisdom, so no one can steal it.” He looked around and saw a hole high up in a tree, then he had an idea.

Anansi held the gourd in two legs and tried to climb the tree with his other six legs. But the gourd was too big and he couldn’t climb. His son was nearby watching him. “Daddy,” he said, “why don’t you tie the gourd to your back and then climb the tree?” “That’s very good advice,” said Anansi. “Thank you for sharing it with me.” And then Anansi realized that advice is only useful when we share it with someone.

So, he climbed the tree with the gourd on his back. And when Anansi reached the top, he held the gourd up to the wind. All the advice flew into the sky and traveled across the land. And wisdom came to everyone.
[图:reading/f9b06e6b/image3.png]

ex.ev: And he knew that to have real wisdom, he had to learn more.
ex.why: 他知道要有真正的智慧就得多学，想收集建议让自己更有智慧。

ex.why: 「别着急，人生不是百米赛跑」——生活需要耐心。

qs.stem: How did Anansi finally climb the tree with the gourd?
opts: He tied the gourd to his back.
He asked his son to help him.
He broke the gourd into pieces.
He waited for the wind to blow it up.

ex.ev: So, he climbed the tree with the gourd on his back.
ex.why: 他听了儿子的建议，把葫芦绑在背上爬上了树。

qs.stem: Which of the following can best describe Anansi’s change?

ex.ev: And then Anansi realized that advice is only useful when we share it with someone.
ex.why: 一开始想把智慧藏起来不让人偷，后来明白要分享，把建议撒向大地——从自私变得乐于分享。

ex.ev: And wisdom came to everyone.
ex.why: 故事讲 Anansi 收集、最后分享智慧的经过——「Anansi 的智慧」。

body: Have you ever helped your parents arrange (布置) the furniture (家具) in your house? It can be hard to put everything in the right place to make your home look more pleasant.     32

Don’t put all the large pieces on one side and all the small pieces on the other.     33     Be sure not to block the windows with large pieces of furniture. Otherwise the room will look crowded and uncomfortable. After all, natural light is important.

34     It’s not a good choice to push everything up against the walls of the room. Even leaving just ten centimeters of space between the walls and some pieces of furniture can make the room look bigger. You can also try placing some pieces of furniture diagonally (斜着地).

Using fewer pieces of furniture will make your rooms have much space for you to walk through. This is especially true in small space, such as bedrooms.     35     It will give you the same storage room but take up less space. And remember to have some space for traffic when putting your furniture. People should be able to walk through the room without falling down because of any piece of furniture.
Whether it’s the bedroom or the living room, every room should have a focal point (焦点). It’s the thing your eyes land on when you enter the room.     36

articles.title: Liu Lingli has been a teacher for hearing-impaired (听力受损的) c
body: [图:reading/359be2f9/image5.png]

Liu Lingli has been a teacher for hearing-impaired (听力受损的) children for 33 years. Her first communication with hearing-impaired people was with her neighbor, Mrs. Wang. One day, when Liu was playing in her house, Wang used sign language to communicate with her. But Liu couldn’t understand, Wang’s husband told Liu that Mrs Wang wanted to make friends with her.
“I was moved, and thought it would be great if she could speak,” Liu said, “so I decided to become a teacher for hearing-impaired students.”

At first, Liu almost gave up because of difficulties. She then thought about her neighbor and the pain on her face when she could not make people understand what she was trying to say. That made Liu stick to her dream of being a “special education” teacher and she succeeded.

Although she was only 18 at that time, she regarded the students as her children. Every day, she spent much time teaching them to speak. One of her students, Jiang Yan, said Liu would show over 100 times how to speak just one word. She also taught the students how to wash their face and clothes, and clip their nails (剪指甲).

Liu Lingli put lots of efforts to help them live better, too. With her help and encouragement, another student Liu Hanxiang could communicate normally with others. Liu Hanxiang learned dancing and is a member of an art group now.

Thanks to Liu’s devotion (奉献), more than 20 students have received higher education. “Whenever they tried to say ‘mom’ or ‘dad’ for the first time, I felt it was the sweetest sound in the world,” Liu Lingli said.

articles.title: In some countries, textbooks belong to the school and are pa
body: In some countries, textbooks belong to the school and are passed on from one group of students to another for repeated use. One Monday morning, Mrs. Green entered the classroom and caught Joe drawing a picture in his math book. This happened just a day after she spoke to the class about the importance of taking care of school property (财产).

On any other day, she would be angry and send him straight to the office. However, this time, she simply walked over to his desk and stood there. Joe quickly closed the book, trying to hide his drawing. Mrs. Green said, “Let me repeat what I said yesterday: Other students will use these textbooks for the next three years. I expect you all to take good care of them.” “Sorry,” Joe said. “I forgot.”

When Mrs. Green came back to Joe’s desk again, he was using his small old eraser to remove (清除) the drawing. Mrs. Green handed him her own eraser and a drawing pad. “Here, this might make the job easier. And you can use this pad whenever you feel the need to draw,” she said. Joe looked very amazed and said, “Thank you very much.” Mrs. Green nodded and continued her lesson.

Since then, Joe has never drawn in his textbook again. He keeps the pad in his schoolbag and from time to time shows Mrs. Green his drawings. Mrs. Green is very glad that she didn’t send him to the office that day. Sending him to the office might stop him from drawing in his books, but they wouldn’t have the good relationship they do now. And who knows? Maybe Mrs. Green encouraged a future Picasso (毕加索).

qs.stem: What was Joe doing when Mrs. Green entered the classroom?
opts: He was doing his math homework.
He was drawing in his math textbook.
He was talking to his friend in class.
He was writing in the teacher’s textbook.

ex.ev: caught Joe drawing a picture in his math book.
ex.why: 老师进来时，Joe 正在数学课本上画画。

qs.stem: How might Joe feel when he performed the underlined actions?

ex.ev: Joe quickly closed the book, trying to hide his drawing.
ex.why: 被老师看见，他赶紧合上书、想藏起画——又害怕又紧张。

qs.stem: Why did Mrs. Green lend Joe her pad?
opts: Joe forgot to bring his own pad.
Joe couldn’t afford to buy a new pad.
She wanted to encourage Joe to keep drawing.
She hoped to help Joe improve his drawing skills.

ex.ev: And you can use this pad whenever you feel the need to draw,
ex.why: 老师给他画本，让他想画就画在本子上——鼓励他继续画画（但别画在课本上）。

qs.stem: What can we know from the last paragraph?
opts: Joe stopped drawing from then on.
Joe will become a famous artist like Picasso.
Mrs. Green regrets not sending Joe to the office.
Mrs. Green and Joe now have a good relationship.

ex.ev: but they wouldn’t have the good relationship they do now.
ex.why: 最后一段说他们现在关系很好，Joe 还常给老师看画。他没停止画画，只是不在课本上画了。

qs.stem: What does the story tell us?
opts: Hard work can lead to success.
Lend a helpful hand when someone is in trouble.
A clever way to fix a problem brings good results.

ex.ev: Mrs. Green is very glad that she didn’t send him to the office that day.
ex.why: 老师没批评他，而是给他画本，既保护了课本又鼓励了他——聪明的办法带来好结果。
