body: New Robot Helps Hikers at Mount Tai
[图:reading/21127dc4/image12.png]

On February 1, 2025, Mount Tai Scenic Area in Shandong Province, China, tested a new robot. This robot helps people climb the mountain and was made by TaiShan Tourism and Culture Group and Shenzhen Kenqin Technology Co. Ltd.

A visitor tried the robot and said, “It feels like someone is pulling me up the mountain. It’s really cool!” The robot is very light, weighing only 1.8 kilograms. It has special parts that make it comfortable to wear, a power system, and smart technology that can tell when the wearer’s legs are moving. Then it gives just the right help to make climbing easier.

This robot can work for more than five hours without needing to be charged (充电) again. It can go about 14 kilometers a single charge. It is great for older people or those who don’t have a lot of strength. They can still enjoy the beautiful views of Mount Tai and feel like they’re climbing.

The robot looks like “mechanical armor (机械装甲)” from science fiction movies. It is small and easy to wear, and can be used for climbing, exercising, running, walking, and even going upstairs. It helps people in many ways.
Right now, the robot is still being tested. But soon it will be ready for everyone to use. People will be able to rent it and try climbing Mount Tai with its help.

qs.stem: The new robot tested at Mount Tai is designed to help people with climbing. How long can it work on a single charge?

ex.ev: This robot can work for more than five hours without needing to be charged (充电) again.
ex.why: 充一次电能工作 5 小时以上。

qs.stem: The word “mechanical” in the phrase “mechanical armor” most likely means ________.

ex.ev: It has special parts that make it comfortable to wear, a power system, and smart technology
ex.why: 它有动力系统，靠机器带动——mechanical 就是「机械的、由机器驱动的」。

qs.stem: What is the weight of the new robot tested at Mount Tai?

ex.ev: The robot is very light, weighing only 1.8 kilograms.
ex.why: 机器人只有 1.8 公斤。

qs.stem: The new robot can be used for several activities. Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a use for the robot?

ex.ev: can be used for climbing, exercising, running, walking, and even going upstairs.
ex.why: 能用来爬山、锻炼、跑步、走路、上楼，没提游泳。

qs.stem: Where can you most likely find this article?

ex.ev: On February 1, 2025, Mount Tai Scenic Area in Shandong Province, China, tested a new robot.
ex.why: 报道一项新的机器人技术，最可能出现在科技新闻网站上。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县四校联考中考三模
articles.title: One day during a lunch break in junior high school, Leo noti
body: One day during a lunch break in junior high school, Leo noticed his classmate Francis was sitting alone and looked upset. Leo, who had always been a caring boy, decided to talk to him and lend a helping hand.

Leo sat down beside Francis and asked him what was wrong. Francis thought for a moment before finally sharing that he had been struggling (斗争) with a difficult math problem but he couldn’t work it out. He had suffered from such a situation for a long time and he was feeling quite upset these days. Leo offered to help Francis with the problem at once, and they spent the next hour working together, going through the steps and working out the problem. There was a big smile on Francis’s face.

As they worked together, Leo realized that Francis was not the only one who was struggling. Many of their classmates were facing the similar difficulty in their studies and were feeling very worried. Leo saw a chance to make a good influence on his classmates and decided to organize a study group after school.

The study group quickly became a hit, and many students started to attend. Leo and his classmates would work together, help each other with their homework and share different methods of success. Day by day, most of them made great progress and they were much more confident than before. The group not only  ▲ , but also brought them closer together.

By being kind, caring and helpful, Leo was able to help his classmates and create a better learning environment for everyone. Leo knew that he could continue to make a difference to the world by spreading kindness and helping others, one act of kindness at a time.

qs.stem: Why did Francis look upset?
opts: Because he failed the math test.
Because he lost some important things.
Because he couldn’t work out a math problem.

ex.ev: he had been struggling (斗争) with a difficult math problem but he couldn’t work it out.
ex.why: 他一直在做一道很难的数学题，怎么也做不出来。

qs.stem: Which of the following words can best describe Leo?

ex.ev: Leo, who had always been a caring boy, decided to talk to him and lend a helping hand.
ex.why: 主动帮同学解题，还组织学习小组——乐于助人。

qs.stem: What did Leo and his classmates do in the study group?
opts: They did the homework by themselves.
They played chess with other classmates.
They shared different methods of success.
They taught other students a foreign language.

ex.ev: Leo and his classmates would work together, help each other with their homework and share different methods of success.
ex.why: 在学习小组里，他们一起写作业、分享成功的方法。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be the best to fill in “ ▲ ” in the text?
opts: encouraged students to do volunteer work
encouraged students to start some other groups

ex.ev: Day by day, most of them made great progress and they were much more confident than before.
ex.why: 大家进步很大、更自信了，所以小组不仅帮大家提高了成绩，还让大家更亲近。

qs.stem: What’s the main idea of the text?
opts: Leo kindly offered to help his classmates.
Francis made progress in the study group.
The teacher lent a helping hand to students.
The students work hard to get success.

ex.ev: By being kind, caring and helpful, Leo was able to help his classmates and create a better learning environment for everyone.
ex.why: 全文讲 Leo 热心帮助同学。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县四校联考中考三模
articles.title: 16 “Even though the computer is widely used today, Chinese p
body: 16     “Even though the computer is widely used today, Chinese people should not forget the skill of writing with hands, because it is part of our country’s culture,” said a Chinese government official (官员).

The computer has become a very useful tool to help people write. As people use computers more often than before, many of them have difficulties writing Chinese characters (字) correctly.     17     Many experts see these mistakes as a result of using the computer.

Nowadays, China is trying to help students and teachers to improve their writing with the help of information technology. With the technology, it is hoped that teachers can write their teaching contents on the blackboard and students can respond by writing, too.

The Chinese character test shows that nowadays, many college students’ handwriting has become worse. Many college students do not know how to write words or sentences in Chinese character in the right way.     18     They might be able to tell the general (大概的) form of a certain character. However, if you ask these adults to write the character in detail (详细地) on paper, they can’t.     19

In the national language teaching course, we can solve this problem with the use of certain technologies.     20     For example, we may ask students to finish their homework by writing with hands instead of typing (打字).

opts: They often make a lot of mistakes in writing.
China is a nation with a rich culture in handwriting.
In fact, besides technology, there are a lot of ways we can do.
Not only students, many adults also meet the same problem.
But, it is much easier for them to spell characters on a computer.

16.ev: Chinese people should not forget the skill of writing with hands, because it is part of our country’s culture,
16.why: 官员说手写是我们文化的一部分，前面应是 B「中国是一个书法文化丰富的国家」。

17.ev: Many experts see these mistakes as a result of using the computer.
17.why: 后面说「专家认为这些错误是用电脑造成的」，前面应是 A「他们写字常出很多错」。

18.ev: Many college students do not know how to write words or sentences in Chinese character in the right way.
18.why: 大学生写不对字，E「但他们在电脑上打字容易得多」。

19.ev: However, if you ask these adults to write the character in detail (详细地) on paper, they can’t.
19.why: 前面说到「这些成年人」也写不出，D「不仅学生，很多成年人也有同样问题」。

20.ev: For example, we may ask students to finish their homework by writing with hands instead of typing (打字).
20.why: 后面举例让学生手写作业，前面应是 C「其实除了技术，我们还有很多办法」。

articles.src: 2025年新乡市太行中学中考三模
articles.title: Nowadays, you may feel tired when spending time with friends
body: Nowadays, you may feel tired when spending time with friends or other people. It is called social exhaustion (疲劳). This may have a bad influence on your life. So what can you do when you have social exhaustion?

You don’t have to join in every social activity. Pick and choose the ones that excite you. Saying yes to every invitation all the time can make you feel worried. Also, although you can’t evade some social activities, such as a family member’s wedding (婚礼) or birthday party, you can usually decide who you would like to spend time with during the activity.

Find out what makes you feel worried and which situations make you feel the most exhausted. Knowing what really tires you in social situations can help you find out how to solve it better. Having family or friends to depend on is helpful. Talk to them about how you are feeling and listen to their advice. They might have ideas to help you feel less worried in social situations.

Taking some time alone can help you feel better. It can help you understand yourself and how you feel in social situations. Then you can plan your day according to what you need and how much time you can spend with others.
These methods can help you solve social exhaustion. Remember, it is good to find a balance (平衡) between looking after yourself and joining in social activities.

qs.stem: What is social exhaustion?
opts: Feeling tired when spending with others.
Feeling excited when spending with others.

ex.ev: Nowadays, you may feel tired when spending time with friends or other people. It is called social exhaustion (疲劳).
ex.why: 和朋友或别人在一起时感到累，就叫社交疲劳。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “evade” in Paragraph 2 mean?

ex.ev: although you can’t evade some social activities, such as a family member’s wedding (婚礼) or birthday party,
ex.why: 家人的婚礼、生日会这种活动没法……——evade 是「躲开、避免」。

qs.stem: Why is it important to know what makes you feel worried in social activities?
opts: Because it can help you make more friends.
Because it can help you have more social activities.
Because it can help you choose better social activities.
Because it can help you find out how to solve things better.

ex.ev: Knowing what really tires you in social situations can help you find out how to solve it better.
ex.why: 知道什么让你累，能帮你找到更好的解决办法。

qs.stem: How can family and friends help you in social situations?
opts: By spending more time with you.
By creating friendly situations for you.
By helping you plan some meaningful activities.

ex.ev: Talk to them about how you are feeling and listen to their advice.
ex.why: 跟家人朋友说说感受，听听他们的建议。

qs.stem: What is the writer’s purpose in writing the text?
opts: To explain different types of social activities.
To suggest ways to deal with social exhaustion.
To compare social exhaustion with physical tiredness.
To warn people about the dangers of social exhaustion.

ex.ev: So what can you do when you have social exhaustion?
ex.why: 全文给出应对社交疲劳的几个方法。

articles.src: 2025年新乡市太行中学中考三模
articles.title: Thanks to AI, work will look very different in the near futu
body: Thanks to AI, work will look very different in the near future than it does today. According to the World Economic Forum, 85 million jobs will be influenced by AI by 2030.     16     In this fast-changing era (时代), our university degrees or past achievements don’t matter so much now. What’s more important are the skills we have.

To stay competitive, we need two groups of skills. The first is AI skills. Having AI skills doesn’t mean becoming an AI engineer or computer scientist.     17     We will become an AI collaborator and supervisor (合作者和监督者). AI will soon appear everywhere in our daily life.     18

Human soft skills make up the second group. It means abilities that AI still cannot handle as well as humans.     19     For example, humans are good at working as a team, thinking of new ideas, and building trusting relationships with others. In schools and workplaces, these abilities are always needed. So as AI grows stronger, these human skills become even more important.
20     Most importantly, we must stay curious, accept changes, and develop lifelong learning. This is how we grow with technology instead of being replaced by it.

opts: At the same time, millions of new jobs will be created.
To succeed in the AI era, we need AI skills and human skills.
These abilities come from the human strengths throughout history.
So, being able to make the best of AI tools will help us do better than others.
Instead, it means the ability to use AI effectively and check its work carefully.

16.ev: According to the World Economic Forum, 85 million jobs will be influenced by AI by 2030.
16.why: 8500 万个工作会受影响，A「同时会产生几百万个新工作」。

17.ev: Having AI skills doesn’t mean becoming an AI engineer or computer scientist.
17.why: 有 AI 技能不是说要当 AI 工程师，E「而是指会有效使用 AI、认真检查它的成果」，Instead 是提示。

18.ev: AI will soon appear everywhere in our daily life.
18.why: AI 很快就无处不在，D「所以会用好 AI 工具能让我们比别人做得更好」。

19.ev: It means abilities that AI still cannot handle as well as humans.
19.why: 人类软技能是 AI 比不上人的能力，C「这些能力来自人类一直以来的长处」。

20.ev: Most importantly, we must stay curious, accept changes, and develop lifelong learning.
20.why: 最后一段总结，B「要在 AI 时代成功，我们需要 AI 技能和人类技能」。

cand: adj. 竞争激烈的；竞争性的
adj. 好奇的；求知欲强的

articles.title: Here are some popular English places of interests for children.
body: Here are some popular English places of interests for children. It can be wonderful to have fun there in your free time. If you want to know more, please visit our website www.travel.com.cn.

[图:reading/38d0dd59/image1.png]   The Old Town of York York is a city in the north of England. It is three hours by train from London. It’s over two thousand years old. You can still walk round the old city walls and the old town. Don’t miss some interesting museums there. Entrance fees to the museums are between £5 and £10 for adults.

[图:reading/38d0dd59/image2.png]   The Museum of the Moving Image This is a museum about films and the cinema. It has examples of the first cameras and information on old film stars and the history of TV. Entrance: Adults £8     Children £4     Children under 5 free

[图:reading/38d0dd59/image3.png]   Legoland This theme park is in Windsor near one of the Queen’s castles. You can walk round hundreds of models of famous places which are made out of Lego. There are also lots of fun rides. Entrance is £25 and all rides are included in the price.

[图:reading/38d0dd59/image4.png]   Sea Life Centre It’s at Plymouth. Special attractions include a quiz and hourly feeding time for different animals and fish, starting at 9: 30. The latest attraction at the centre is a big glass tunnel you can walk through. All around you, you will see big fish swimming, sometimes even over your head. £3.70 for adults, £2.00, for children, less for over sixties and school groups.

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县三校联考三模
articles.title: Ed was a professional football player, but in 2017 he had an
body: Ed was a professional football player, but in 2017 he had an accident in a swimming pool. After that, he couldn’t move his body from the shoulders down.

Doctors told him that he’d probably never walk again, but Ed didn’t want to believe this. He had recently got engaged (订婚) to the woman who is now his wife and he said that she was the main reason he wanted to get better. He spent six days staring at his toes (脚趾) and trying to make them move—and, finally, he succeeded! This was the start of a long journey.

While in hospital, Ed met Paul, a man in his late thirties. Doctors had also told Paul he would never walk again, but Ed encouraged him not to give up and six months later, Paul told Ed he was walking with a stick.

Only a year after his accident, Ed climbed the highest mountain in Wales. Since then he has also climbed a 6,500-meter mountain in Nepal and he said that after each big climb he noticed his body could do new movements.

Two years later, 31-year-old Ed climbed 8,848 meters, the height of the world’s highest mountain, by going up and down his parents’ stairs 2,783 times. When he finished, he told a news reporter he had loved it although it sometimes was “painful” and “boring”. He also raised £46,000 for charity.
Ed hopes his story can help people. That’s why he started his own charity, M2M, which aims to support “people facing challenges in life.”

qs.stem: Who did Ed want to get better mainly for?

ex.ev: he said that she was the main reason he wanted to get better.
ex.why: 刚订婚的妻子是他想好起来的主要原因。

qs.stem: What is Ed like according to Paragraph 3?

ex.ev: but Ed encouraged him not to give up and six months later, Paul told Ed he was walking with a stick.
ex.why: 第三段讲 Ed 鼓励病友 Paul 不要放弃——乐于助人。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “it” in Paragraph 5 refer to?

ex.ev: by going up and down his parents’ stairs 2,783 times. When he finished, he told a news reporter he had loved it
ex.why: it 指前面他在父母家上下楼梯 2783 次这件事。

qs.stem: Put the events about Ed into the correct order according to the passage. a.Ed started M2M. b.Ed succeeded in making his toes move. c.Ed had an accident in a swimming pool. d.Ed climbed the highest mountain in Wales. e.Ed climbed his parents’ stairs 2,783 times.

ex.why: 顺序：泳池出事（c）→ 让脚趾动起来（b）→ 爬上威尔士最高峰（d）→ 爬楼梯 2783 次（e）→ 创办慈善机构 M2M（a）。

qs.stem: What would be the best title for the passage?

ex.ev: which aims to support “people facing challenges in life.”
ex.why: 受伤后不断挑战自己：动脚趾、爬山、爬楼梯——「一个热爱挑战的人」。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县三校联考三模
articles.title: So far, China has successfully sent a large number of satell
body: So far, China has successfully sent a large number of satellites (卫星) and spaceships into space. Space scientists have been greatly inspired (赋予灵感) by the old stories and ancient famous people when giving them names.

Since thousands of years ago, Chinese people have dreamed of going to the moon. Chang’e Flies to the Moon is one of the most popular stories. As you can see, China’s first man-made satellite to circle around the moon was named Chang’e I. More interestingly, the moon rover (巡视器) was named after the Jade Rabbit, who is the partner of Chang’e in the story. These old stories carry people’s best wishes and dreams. With the development of science and technology, our scientists have made them come true.

Kua Fu Runs After the Sun is another story to show how much ancient Chinese people wanted to know about the unknown world. Now, Kua Fu is going with the scientists to “visit” the sun, because we have a space project called KuaFu Mission.

Besides the ancient stories, space scientists also get ideas from ancient famous people. For example, Mozi, an ancient scientist, discovered that light travels in a straight line over 2, 000 years ago. His discovery made space study take a big step at that time. So, China’s first quantum (量子) science satellite was named Mozi, making China the first country in the world to achieve quantum communication between satellites and the ground.
From such simple things as giving names to the satellites, we can see how great our traditional culture is and what influence it has on our modern science and technology.

qs.stem: In China, space scientists get ideas from ________ when naming satellites. ①old stories             ②traditional projects ③ancient famous people             ④ popular inventions

ex.ev: Space scientists have been greatly inspired (赋予灵感) by the old stories and ancient famous people when giving them names.
ex.why: 科学家起名的灵感来自古老的故事和古代名人——①③。

qs.stem: What do we know about Chang’e I according to the passage?
opts: It “visits” the sun with the scientists.
It is the world’s first man-made satellite.

ex.ev: China’s first man-made satellite to circle around the moon was named Chang’e I.
ex.why: 嫦娥一号是中国第一颗绕月飞行的人造卫星。去「拜访」太阳的是夸父。

qs.stem: How does the writer support his opinion in Paragraph 4?

ex.ev: For example, Mozi, an ancient scientist, discovered that light travels in a straight line over 2, 000 years ago.
ex.why: 第四段用墨子的例子说明科学家从古代名人那里得到灵感。

qs.stem: Which is the right structure of the passage? (①=Paragraph 1                    ②=Paragraph 2,…)

ex.why: ①总起（起名灵感来自故事和名人），②③④三个例子（嫦娥、夸父、墨子），⑤总结——A 图。

qs.stem: What’s the writer’s main purpose of writing the passage?
opts: To spread the traditional Chinese culture.
To explain how our scientists develop the space industry.
To introduce the achievements in our science and technology.
To tell how traditional Chinese culture influences our space science.

ex.ev: we can see how great our traditional culture is and what influence it has on our modern science and technology.
ex.why: 最后一段点明：传统文化对现代航天科技的影响。

cand: adj. 未知的；不为人知的

articles.src: 2025年周口市项城市付集二中等校联考中考三模
articles.title: Sleep, sleep, beauty bright, Dreaming in the joys of night;
body: Sleep, sleep, beauty bright,
Dreaming in the joys of night;
Sleep, sleep, in thy (你的) sleep,
Little sorrows (忧伤) sit and weep.
Have you ever experienced being put to sleep by singing songs like that when you were kids? What do you usually think before sleeping? When it is difficult to fall to sleep, what will you do?

Some people are lucky. They fall asleep as soon as their heads hit the pillow. Others aren’t so lucky. Sleep takes longer to come, and sometimes it doesn’t come at all. For these people, counting sheep may be the answer. Counting sheep seems like a way to help people fall asleep. With their eyes closed, people often picture a line of white sheep. Then, they count each one as they jump over a fence. The activity seems to be easy and may calm them to sleep.

This way is as old as time. Some people believe it comes from the Islamic (伊斯兰的) culture. Others believe it started with shepherds (牧羊人) in old Britain. They needed to make sure all their sheep were there each night. So, they counted them before they went to sleep.

A team of scientists at Oxford University carried out a study on counting sheep. They wanted to see if the method really worked. They put people with sleep problems in three groups. One group went to sleep in the way they usually do. Another group were asked to imagine peaceful things like waterfalls, the blue sky and white clouds to help them fall asleep. The last group were asked to count sheep. From the study, the scientists got some interesting results. The people in the second group got to sleep around 20 minutes faster than usual. However, those in the last group took longer than usual to fall asleep. The scientists believed counting sheep made the people feel nervous. As a result, they had more difficulty falling asleep. So, it looks like counting sheep may not be the answer for people with sleep problems.

qs.stem: How does the writer lead into the topic at the beginning of the text?

ex.ev: What do you usually think before sleeping? When it is difficult to fall to sleep, what will you do?
ex.why: 开头一首摇篮曲后连问几个问题，引出话题。

qs.stem: Which of the following pictures matches the underlined word “pillow”?

ex.ev: They fall asleep as soon as their heads hit the pillow.
ex.why: 「头一碰到……就睡着」，pillow 是枕头，D 图是枕头。

qs.stem: What is the last paragraph mainly about?
opts: The three ways of falling asleep.
The sleep problems of three groups.
The peaceful things on helping you sleep faster.

ex.ev: A team of scientists at Oxford University carried out a study on counting sheep.
ex.why: 最后一段讲牛津大学关于数羊的研究。

qs.stem: What do we know about counting sheep to sleep?
opts: It really works to solve the sleep problem.
It comes from the Islamic shepherds in old Britain.
It may not be the best way for people with sleep problems.
It helps people get to sleep around 20 minutes faster than usual.

ex.ev: So, it looks like counting sheep may not be the answer for people with sleep problems.
ex.why: 研究发现数羊的人反而更难睡着，对失眠的人可能不是好办法。快 20 分钟的是想象美好事物那一组。

qs.stem: Why is this text written?

ex.why: 介绍数羊的来历和科学研究结果，目的是提供信息。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县五所学校三模
articles.title: In a heartwarming story, Mr.
body: In a heartwarming story, Mr. Sun from Fushun, Liaoning province, made a video using AI technology to make his grandma happy. He used a special computer technology to make himself look and sound like his dad, who had been dead. It took him almost half a month to finish it. Then he sent the video to his 91-year-old grandma. Sun had lots of feelings while making the video. He felt a lot of sadness thinking about his dad and how much he missed him.

Sun’s dad died in 2023 because of a serious disease. Sun’s grandma didn’t know about it because her family worried it would make her too sad. They told her that her son was still in hospital far away. However, the grandma missed her son a lot and wanted to talk to him.

Sun got a creative idea from movies. He decided to use a computer program to make a video where he looked like his dad. He even had his hair cut to look more like his dad. With the computer program, he changed his face into his father’s in the video and said, “Mom, it’s Jihai, your son. I’m doing well in Beijing.” The video wasn’t very clear, but the grandma believed it was really her son.

In fact, Sun made the video to help himself say goodbye to his dad as well and to start a new page in his life. Although it’s hard, Sun wants to be strong like his dad and take care of his family. Now, Sun is taking care of his grandma like his dad would have.

Because her family worried it would bring her much sadness.

ex.ev: Sun’s grandma didn’t know about it because her family worried it would make her too sad.
ex.why: 家人怕奶奶太伤心，没告诉她。

articles.title: For Internet Safety Think before you post!
body: For Internet Safety

Think before you post! Before you post a photo or video online, you should ask yourself: ◆ Is it against the law or rules? ◆Will it make anyone feel uncomfortable? ◆Could it affect your life? ◆Would you be happy for your parents or friends to see it?   Use passwords! ◆ Keep your password safe and change it regularly (定期地). ◆ Don’t use your name or anything easy to guess. ◆Don’t share it with anyone, even your best friends. ◆Use a mixture of capitals, numbers and special characters. ◆If anyone knows your password, change it right now.

Pay attention to your privacy! ◆Use another name or a nickname (昵称) instead of your real name. ◆Always make sure your settings are really private and choose who can see your account! ◆Don’t discuss your problems online. ◆Only give your phone number to the people you actually know.   Don’t trust everything online! ◆Don’t fall for it—things aren’t always what they seem! ◆Everyone exaggerates (夸大其词)—you probably do it as well! ◆Remember that most people only tell you the good bits. ◆Don’t be fooled by “free” offers！ [图:reading/a5711fd1/image1.png]

articles.src: 2025年驻马店市正阳县四校联考三模
articles.title: With a birthday usually comes a party, as well as a cake, pr
body: [图:reading/a5711fd1/image2.png]
With a birthday usually comes a party, as well as a cake, presents and wishes from friends. But beyond these, what does a birthday mean?

One year, I spent my birthday by myself in a completely new place. Calls and messages poured in as usual. However, I was not certain about what to do. I had nowhere to go; I didn’t know anyone to share the joy of the event with, either.
At that moment, my mother called me, asking, “What are you planning for your birthday?”

“I’m not sure, Mum. There’s no one here. I’m so far from home.…” Although my voice sounded so weak, I could still hear its tremble clearly in the empty, quiet room. “You don’t always need a lot of people for your birthday. Just follow your heart and make this day yours.” What Mum said made me less unhappy.

Then I picked up a book and lost myself in it, with music on. I did as my mother had told me and enjoyed “my own day”. But unexpectedly, this solitary day became a bridge—connecting me with my inner self. It was a peaceful but satisfying day. I realized my growth for the first time—from a preschool (学龄前的) child who shared birthday chocolate with the class to someone who could now celebrate alone.

When I lay in bed that night, I remembered my mother’s words, “You came into our lives this day. We are thankful for it.” And indeed, that is the true meaning of birthday celebrations—the valuable gift of life itself. From the moment we are born, every day is a new chance to learn, to love, and to enjoy the world around us.

ex.ev: However, I was not certain about what to do. I had nowhere to go; I didn’t know anyone to share the joy of the event with, either.
ex.why: 在陌生地方过生日，不知道做什么、没人分享——有点迷茫和孤单。

qs.stem: Why did the writer’s mother call him?
opts: She wanted to say “Happy birthday” to him.
She wanted to celebrate his birthday with him.
She wanted to know about his plans for his birthday.
She wanted to tell him that she loved him so much.

ex.ev: my mother called me, asking, “What are you planning for your birthday?”
ex.why: 妈妈打电话问他生日打算怎么过。

opts: By replying to messages and preparing a party.
By sharing birthday chocolate with the class.

By reading a book and listening to music.

ex.ev: Then I picked up a book and lost myself in it, with music on.
ex.why: 他听着音乐看书，这一天让他和内心的自己连在了一起。

qs.stem: Which of the following made the writer realize the true meaning of a birthday?

ex.ev: When I lay in bed that night, I remembered my mother’s words, “You came into our lives this day. We are thankful for it.”

ex.why: 生日的意义是生命本身这份礼物——提醒我们珍惜生命和每一天。

articles.title: For Emma, PE class was the most difficult part.
body: For Emma, PE class was the most difficult part. She didn’t mind the tiredness but the looks her classmates gave her. Emma was bigger than others of her age. A group of students often ran behind her, laughing and talking about how Emma ran.
“Just one more year,” Emma kept telling herself, “one more year and I’ll graduate and won’t have to take this stupid PE class anymore.”

But everything changed when a girl called Kit joined the class. She had short hair, bright eyes, and a long scar (伤疤) across the left side of her face. She introduced herself, “Hi, everyone, I’m Kit. I love sports and fashion. You might be wondering about the scar. I got it when I fell off my bike. I see it as a cool mark now.” Emma listened in surprise. How could the girl be so confident?

During lunchtime, Emma was sitting at her usual table. Kit walked over to join Emma. Emma couldn’t believe such a confident girl would like to sit with her. She worked up the courage to share what was troubling her. “Hug yourself!” said Kit. Hearing that, Emma felt a wave of warmth wash over her. And she felt the weight lift off her shoulder.

It was time for PE class again, but this time Kit was with her. Emma discovered that true confidence comes from within, not from others’ words. In the beautiful sunshine, the two girls walked together— one with a scar on the face and the other with a body that she finally felt she owned.

qs.stem: Why did Emma hate PE class?
opts: Because she thought it was boring.

ex.why: 她不怕累，怕的是别人的眼光：她块头大，有同学在后面笑她跑步的样子。

ex.why: 「抱抱自己」是让她接纳自己，不在乎别人说什么——真正的自信来自内心。

qs.stem: How did Emma feel after talking with Kit?
opts: She was surprised at Kit’s story.
She was relaxed about her PE grades.
She wasn’t worried about her body shape.
She was happy about choosing her favorite class.

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县五所学校中考二模
articles.title: Recently, I asked a seeing friend who had just walked in the
body: Recently, I asked a seeing friend who had just walked in the woods what she had noticed. “Nothing special,” she replied.

How was it possible, I asked myself, to walk through the woods and see nothing worthy of note? I who cannot see find hundreds of things to interest me only through touch. If I can get so much pleasure from touch, how much more beauty must be found by sight (视力)? And I have imagined what I should most like to see if I were given the use of my eyes for just three days.

On the first day, I should want to see the people who have made my life worth living and the books which have been read to me. In the afternoon, I should take a walk in the woods and admire the beauties of nature. That night, I should not be able to sleep.
On my second day, I should go to the museums to see man’s progress. I should try to explore the spirit of man through his art. In the evening, I should spend at the movies.

The following day, I should spend in the world of common people going about the business of life. At midnight permanent (永久的) night would close in on me again, and I should realize how much I had left unseen.

I who am blind can give one suggestion to those who see: Use your eyes as if tomorrow you would be blind. The same is true of other senses. Hear the songs of birds, as if you would be deaf tomorrow. Smell the flowers, as if tomorrow you could never smell again…But of all the senses, I’m sure that sight must be the most pleasant.
（Adapted from “Three Days to See” by Helen Keller）

qs.stem: What makes the writer start imagining the three days?

ex.ev: How was it possible, I asked myself, to walk through the woods and see nothing worthy of note?
ex.why: 朋友说「没什么特别的」，作者问自己怎么可能，接着就开始想象如果能看见三天——是她问自己的问题引出了想象。

qs.stem: What does the writer want to do during the three days?
opts: Read books to people on the first day.
Go to the movies on the second day.
Succeed in business on the third day.
Have a wonderful dream every day.

ex.ev: In the evening, I should spend at the movies.
ex.why: 第二天晚上去看电影。第一天是看人和书（别人读给她听的），不是读给别人听。

qs.stem: What does the last paragraph mainly talk about?
opts: A method of living a pleasant life.

ex.ev: I who am blind can give one suggestion to those who see: Use your eyes as if tomorrow you would be blind.
ex.why: 最后一段是一个盲人给看得见的人的建议。

qs.stem: Which is the best structure (结构) of the passage? （①=Paragraph 1        ②=Paragraph 2…）

ex.why: ①②引出想象，③④⑤是三天（并列），⑥给读者建议——D 图。

qs.stem: Which of the following sayings may the writer agree with?
opts: Time is what we want most, but what we use worst.
Never leave until tomorrow what you can do today.

ex.ev: Hear the songs of birds, as if you would be deaf tomorrow.
ex.why: 她让我们珍惜每一种感官，好像明天就会失去——珍惜每一刻、感恩所拥有的。

articles.title: Taking a great photo is not easy and there are lots of thing
body: Taking a great photo is not easy and there are lots of things to consider. How do you choose and organize your subjects within your photo?     16     Here are some tips from the art, design and photography experts.

Find a focus. When taking a picture, ask yourself, “What’s the focus?” If you are taking a picture of a crowded street, choose a subject which draws your eye.     17     If it’s a landscape photo of a field, the focus could be a big tree.

18     It’s a bit boring to put your subject right in the middle. Place it a little on the left or right of your photo. Imagine your photo is divided into a three-by-three grid (网格) of boxes. One of the corners of your central square is where your focus should be.

Create colorful contrasts (对比). Color in a picture is more easily noticed if it has a contrast.    19     They will stand out more if they are taken beside a grey stone wall, or photographed against a bright blue sky.

Try different angles. To add more interest to a photo, try taking it from different angles. This means you need to move around, taking photos from different sides, from above or from below. For example, if you photograph a building from a plane, it looks tiny, but a photo of the same building looking up from the street makes it look huge.    20
Practice makes perfect. Try everything for the perfect shot.

opts: It can tell a different story.
Think about focus, color, light and more.
It could be a person wearing bright colors.

16.why: 怎么安排拍摄对象？D「要考虑焦点、颜色、光线等」，后面引出专家建议。

articles.src: 2025年商丘市夏邑县中考二模
articles.title: Last Saturday, the sky was full of thick clouds, and it was
body: Last Saturday, the sky was full of thick clouds, and it was pouring cats and dogs outside. I was watching TV, feeling bored out of my mind. The rain beat against the windows. Looking out of the window, I couldn’t see cars or people on the street clearly.

Just then, above the noise of the rain, I heard a loud knock on my door. When I opened the door, I saw a delivery man (快递员) standing there. His clothes, hair, shoes...were all wet. He held my online shopping package (包裹) carefully, protecting it from the rain as if it were the most important thing in the world.

I quickly invited him to come in. As he stepped inside, he bowed and said sorry for being late. He explained that the bad weather had made it difficult for him to ride his bike. He couldn’t go ahead quickly as usual. I told him not to worry and rushed to the kitchen to get him a cup of hot tea. He thanked me with a big smile.

While he was drying himself, we started talking to each other. He told me that he had been working as a delivery man for two years to support his family. His parents were both retired (退休的)，so he tried to raise his family. Even on days like this, when the weather was at its worst, he never thought of giving up because he knew that people were waiting for their packages.

Before he left, I thanked him again for his hard work. Seeing him disappear into the rain, I realized how these common people keep their lives running smoothly, and how they face all kinds of weather and difficulties bravely. This experience made me see the beauty in the efforts of common people, and I’ll always be thankful for what they do.

ex.why: 天上乌云密布，雨打窗户，看不清街上——rain cats and dogs 是「下大雨」。

qs.stem: What did the writer do for the delivery man?
opts: Offer him a cup of hot tea.

ex.ev: I told him not to worry and rushed to the kitchen to get him a cup of hot tea.
ex.why: 作者给他倒了一杯热茶。

ex.ev: As he stepped inside, he bowed and said sorry for being late.
ex.why: 他鞠躬为迟到道歉，再坏的天气也坚持送件——勤劳又有礼貌。

articles.src: 2025年商丘市夏邑县中考二模
articles.title: Imagine having a conversation with your friend, and you feel
body: Imagine having a conversation with your friend, and you feel happy about it at the end of the conversation, but you are not quite sure why. Now imagine having the same conversation, but this time you feel excited because you know more about your friend. What’s the difference?

In the second case, you know exactly how you feel, which helps you deal with the situation effectively (有效地). This way of understanding and naming feelings in different situations is called emotional granularity (情绪粒度).

Life is like a box of chocolates. It often presents us with different emotions. Understanding these feelings is important for a happy life. Those with high emotional granularity can name their feelings exactly. Instead of saying “I feel happy”, they would say, “I’m happy about the deep friendship and satisfied with the moment with my friend. I value our friendship and will remember it forever.”

People with higher emotional granularity have more developed brain structure in emotional-processing areas. These areas in the brain work well together. They help us notice our emotions, name them, and react to them more correctly. Developing the ability to name feelings very well can build an emotional immune system (免疫系统) against mood disorders.

The benefits of emotional granularity are far-reaching. It helps people manage their emotions better, and then improve relationships with family and friends. Actually, emotional granularity is not only gifted but can also be nurtured. To build emotional granularity, you can learn more emotional words, keep an emotional diary, try different emotional experiences, and often play emotional role-playing games.

All in all, in real conversations, emotional granularity helps people make better decisions in many social situations. It also makes us stronger and better at dealing with stress by noticing emotional problems early.

qs.stem: Why does the writer begin the passage by comparing facts?
opts: To teach us how to deal with emotions.
To encourage us to express our feelings.
To lead into the topic of emotional granularity.
To show the difference between feelings and expressions.

ex.ev: This way of understanding and naming feelings in different situations is called emotional granularity (情绪粒度).
ex.why: 开头比较两种情况，是为了引出「情绪粒度」这个话题。

qs.stem: How do people with high emotional granularity express their feelings?
opts: They share their true feelings easily.
They show the facts and avoid expressing their feelings.

ex.ev: Those with high emotional granularity can name their feelings exactly.
ex.why: 情绪粒度高的人能准确说出自己的感受。

qs.stem: How can you build an emotional immune system?

ex.ev: Developing the ability to name feelings very well can build an emotional immune system (免疫系统) against mood disorders.
ex.why: 练习准确说出感受，能建立情绪免疫系统。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “nurtured” mean in Paragraph 5?

ex.ev: To build emotional granularity, you can learn more emotional words, keep an emotional diary,
ex.why: 不仅是天生的，还可以通过学情绪词、写日记来培养——nurtured 是「培养」。

qs.stem: Why does the writer write this text?
opts: To show the ways to control emotions.
To call us to develop emotional granularity.
To explain the benefits of noticing emotions.
To give opinions about emotional granularity.

ex.ev: The benefits of emotional granularity are far-reaching.
ex.why: 文章讲了什么是情绪粒度、它的好处和怎样培养，目的是号召我们培养情绪粒度。

articles.src: 2025年商丘市夏邑县中考二模
articles.title: Have you ever wanted to achieve a goal and ended up doing lo
body: Have you ever wanted to achieve a goal and ended up doing lots of research on how to achieve it? You learn more and more.     16     That is because when you learn a new idea, you find that there is a lot more to know about it.
Usually, people think they need to get more and more information before trying a new idea.     17     But when you let learning get in the way of doing, you will never get going.

One of the best ways to learn is to take action and learn from the results that you get from those actions. Don’t be afraid of not being perfect and just take the first step. You will go further than those who are still in preparation.     18     But over-preparation in trying to reach a goal won’t get you results. The knowledge and skills that you will need will be picked up along the way.

If a baby wants to learn how to walk, it doesn’t do it by just sitting there and thinking about how to walk.     19     Sure he may fall, but with every fall, he learns what is working and what is not and adjusts (调整) to it. By doing this over and over, he will finally learn to walk. This is the method you should use when you want to achieve your goals as well.     20
Learning more is great but if all you’re doing is learning and not taking action, it’s time to change that. Just take the first step.

opts: But it seems that you know less and less.
There is nothing wrong with learning a lot.
The best way for a baby to walk is to actually start walking.

16.why: 后面解释「因为学了一个新东西，发现还有更多要学」，前面应是 C「但你好像知道得越来越少」。

17.why: 后面 But 转折说学习挡住了行动就永远开始不了，前面应是 D「学很多本身没有错」。

18.ev: But over-preparation in trying to reach a goal won’t get you results.
18.why: 后面 But 说准备过头没结果，前面应是 A「有准备是好的」。

articles.src: 2025年商丘市宁陵县部分初中联考中考二模
articles.title: At the Shanghai Natural History Museum, there’s a large coll
body: At the Shanghai Natural History Museum, there’s a large collection of fossils (化石). These fossils tell us a lot about the world millions of years ago. But have you ever thought about fossilizing (使成化石) something so that future people can learn about the world we live in today? If so, what would you choose?

[图:reading/3764d197/image1.png]Betty Yu, 14   I would fossilize a kite. More and more people are glued to their screens. Few people today understand the simple joy of flying a kite. I want future people to know about this fun activity.

[图:reading/3764d197/image2.png]Edison Chen, 14   A newspaper. Nowadays, people don’t use newspapers to learn about the world. Instead, they pay more attention on the Internet. A fossilized newspaper would show how people used to get information.

[图:reading/3764d197/image3.png]Lily Wu, 11   I’d like to fossilize a fish. As we know, living things are always evolving (进化). Fish may look very different many years from now. Wouldn’t it be interesting to show people in the future what fish looked like centuries ago?
[图:reading/3764d197/image4.png]Jack Yang, 15   I would choose a book about the history of my hometown. It could help my descendants (后代) understand their roots and the events that shaped their world.

qs.stem: What does Betty want to fossilize?

ex.ev: I would fossilize a kite.
ex.why: Betty 想把风筝做成化石。

qs.stem: What would a fossilized newspaper show?
opts: How people used to get information.

ex.ev: A fossilized newspaper would show how people used to get information.
ex.why: 报纸化石能让人看到人们过去怎样获取信息。

qs.stem: From whose fossils can we learn something about animals?

ex.ev: I’d like to fossilize a fish.
ex.why: Lily 想把鱼做成化石，让未来的人看到现在的鱼长什么样——和动物有关。

qs.stem: Why does Jack choose to fossilize a book?

ex.ev: It could help my descendants (后代) understand their roots and the events that shaped their world.
ex.why: 家乡历史的书能帮后代了解自己的根和历史。

qs.stem: What may be the writer’s opinion on fossilizing something for future people?

ex.ev: But have you ever thought about fossilizing (使成化石) something so that future people can learn about the world we live in today?
ex.why: 作者问「你想过把东西做成化石让未来的人了解今天吗」，还请几个人谈想法，态度是支持的。

articles.src: 2025年平顶山市鲁山县两所中学中考二模
articles.title: Will couldn’t wait for September when school would start.
body: Will couldn’t wait for September when school would start. It was early August, and he was at the same summer camp. He had been going to for the last five years. His dad went to the camp when he was a boy and loved it, so Will didn’t want to disappoint his dad by telling him that he didn’t even like it.
By the middle of August, Will had had more than enough. He had had enough of the horses, enough of the baseball games, and enough of the camp food.

He wrote to his mom and asked her if she would pick him up early, but he didn’t want his mom to tell his dad. She replied in a letter which said, “I can’t do that. I am always honest with your dad. If you really want to leave, I will talk to him about it.”

Will was still too worried about disappointing his dad, so he wrote back to his mom that he would stay for the last two weeks and try to make the best of it. He asked his mom if she would make his favorite meal when he got home.

During that last week, Will was looking so forward to the meal his mom would be making that. Every time he ate a camp meal he imagined he was eating his mom’s cooking. All of a sudden, the food didn’t taste so bad.

Will decided to be honest with his camp counselors (顾问). He told the head horseback counselor that he wasn’t comfortable with the horse he had been given. The counselor asked Will which horse he might feel better riding. Will was then given to Misty for the last week, and he started to like horseback riding.
Will never liked playing baseball because he didn’t like playing baseball. He told the baseball counselor, and the counselor switched (调整) him to play catcher. Will started to actually like baseball.

When Will’s parents came to pick him up from camp, he said to them in all honesty, “This was the best summer at camp ever.” He then added that he couldn’t wait for next year’s camp, and he might even want to stay for an extra week or two.

qs.stem: What did Will expect at the summer camp?

ex.ev: By the middle of August, Will had had more than enough.
ex.why: 他早就受够了夏令营，盼着九月开学——盼着夏令营结束。

qs.stem: What is Will like according to the passage?

ex.ev: Will decided to be honest with his camp counselors (顾问).
ex.why: 他怕让爸爸失望（关心家人），后来又诚实地告诉顾问自己的想法——体贴又诚实。

qs.stem: How did Will make himself feel better at the camp?

ex.ev: He told the head horseback counselor that he wasn’t comfortable with the horse he had been given.
ex.why: 他把真实想法告诉顾问，换了马、换了位置，慢慢喜欢上了夏令营——靠说真话。

qs.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of the story? a. Will praised the camp. b. Will went to the camp to please his dad. c. Will stayed till the end of the camp. d. Will talked to counselors. e. Will wrote a letter to his mom.

ex.why: 顺序：为让爸爸高兴去夏令营（b）→ 写信给妈妈（e）→ 跟顾问说实话（d）→ 坚持到结束（c）→ 夸夏令营（a）。

qs.stem: What can we learn from this text?
opts: We should join a summer camp.
We should make full use of time.
We should speak out our thoughts.
We should get out of parents’ control.

ex.ev: When Will’s parents came to pick him up from camp, he said to them in all honesty,
ex.why: Will 说出自己的想法后，问题都解决了——要说出自己的想法。

articles.src: 2025年周口市太康县中考二模
articles.title: Do you believe that friendship sometimes has a magic power?
body: Do you believe that friendship sometimes has a magic power? Once upon a time, in a quiet small town, there lived a boy named Frank. Frank was a shy and lonely boy. He always felt nervous when he was around other kids. One day, his teacher announced (宣布) a group project, and Frank was paired with a girl named Betty. At first, Frank was very nervous. He didn’t know what to say or how to work with her. But Betty was kind and friendly. She smiled at him and said, “Don’t worry. We can do this together.” Frank felt a little better.

As they worked on the project, Frank started to feel happy. Betty was full of ideas, and Frank found himself enjoying their conversations. They laughed and shared stories. Frank felt like he had a real friend for the first time. But then, something unexpected happened. They lost all their work because of a computer problem. Frank felt so sad and frustrated (沮丧的). He thought they would never finish the project on time. Betty, however, stayed calm and said, “It’s okay. We can start over. We can make it.” Frank was amazed by her strong will and felt encouraged.

With Betty’s support, Frank felt hopeful again. They worked even harder and finally finished the project. When they showed it to the class, everyone clapped and praised their work. Frank felt proud and happy. He realized that friendship could turn even the hardest time into something beautiful. As he walked home that day, Frank couldn’t stop thinking about how much he had changed. He felt warmth in his heart, knowing that he had found a friend who believed in him.

qs.stem: How does the writer start the text?

ex.ev: Do you believe that friendship sometimes has a magic power?
ex.why: 开头用一个问题引出故事。

qs.stem: Which is the correct order according to the text? a. Frank and Betty got praise when they showed their work to the classmates. b. Frank was paired with a girl named Betty in a group project. c. Frank and Betty worked even harder and finally finished the project. d. As they worked on the project, Frank felt happy to find a real friend. e. Frank and Betty lost all their work because of a computer problem.

ex.why: 顺序：和 Betty 分到一组（b）→ 做项目时找到真朋友（d）→ 电脑出问题作品全丢了（e）→ 更努力完成（c）→ 展示时得到表扬（a）。

qs.stem: Which of the following can best describe Betty?

ex.ev: But Betty was kind and friendly. She smiled at him and said, “Don’t worry. We can do this together.”
ex.why: Betty 亲切地安慰、鼓励 Frank——善良、会关心人。

qs.stem: According to the end of the text, what might happen afterwards (以后)?
opts: Frank and Betty will live in the town together.
Frank will know how good his teacher is.
Frank will work together with Betty again.
Frank will change and be good friends with Betty.

ex.ev: As he walked home that day, Frank couldn’t stop thinking about how much he had changed.
ex.why: 他发现自己变了很多，找到了相信他的朋友——他会改变，和 Betty 成为好朋友。

qs.stem: What is the text?

ex.ev: Once upon a time, in a quiet small town, there lived a boy named Frank.
ex.why: 「从前……」开头，有人物和情节，是一个故事。

cand: adj. 真实的；实际存在的

articles.title: Hainan, an island in Southern China, is not only known for i
body: Hainan, an island in Southern China, is not only known for its blue beaches and sunny weather.     16

Qiong Opera started more than 300 years ago, during the Ming Dynasty.     17     Over time, it has developed its own style and become a way for the people of Hainan to share their stories and traditions.

18     The music is a mixture of traditional Hainan songs. Qiong Opera sounds gentle and soothing (让人感到安慰的). The actors and actresses also use their voices in a smooth and relaxed way, which matches the peaceful life in Hainan. When actors and actresses perform in Qiong Opera, they wear bright clothes and use colorful make-ups to show different characters.     19     They are Sheng, Dan, Jing, Mo and Chou. Each role has its own way of moving and speaking, which makes the performances very interesting to watch.
The stories in Qiong Opera often come from Hainan’s history, myths (神话), and local stories. They talk about Hainan’s past and present. They also show the local culture and lifestyle.     20
Qiong Opera is a treasure of Hainan’s culture. It helps to spread the island’s language, customs and values to the young visitors.

opts: There are five main types of roles in Qiong Opera.
These stories help to keep Hainan’s traditions and beliefs alive.
Qiong Opera is special because of its music and actions.
It accepted several other operas in the Qing Dynasty.
It’s also home to a special form of art called Qiong Opera.

16.ev: Hainan, an island in Southern China, is not only known for its blue beaches and sunny weather.
16.why: not only…，后面 E「它还是一种特别艺术——琼剧的家乡」，also 和 not only 对应。

17.ev: Qiong Opera started more than 300 years ago, during the Ming Dynasty.
17.why: 明朝开始，D「清朝时吸收了几种别的戏曲」，按时间往下讲。

18.ev: The music is a mixture of traditional Hainan songs.
18.why: 这一段讲琼剧的音乐和表演，开头 C「琼剧的特别在于它的音乐和动作」。

articles.src: 2025年南阳市中考二模
articles.title: After breakfast on Saturday morning, Omer sat in his bedroom
body: [图:reading/564e4a23/image3.png]

After breakfast on Saturday morning, Omer sat in his bedroom looking at a map and thinking about his homework for the weekend—to follow the map of the community and to find the treasures at the places marked with an X on the map. He didn’t want to do homework at the weekend, but the treasure hunt (搜寻) sounded like good fun.
Just then, his friend Azra came to play with him. Omer told Azra about his homework and Azra was very pleased to do it with him.
Having seen the first X marked on the park on the map, the two boys went to the park right away with the map. They looked everywhere in the park but couldn’t find any treasure.

“Where are the treasures?” they shook their heads. When they looked around, they saw Mr. Polat., the ice-cream man was there under a tree selling his delicious ice-creams! As always, there was a line of people, but it was worth the wait.
“That’s four dollars for two, boys.”
“Oh dear,” said Omer. “We’ve only got three. Sorry, Mr. Polat!”
“Don’t worry, and take them. It’s raining fire, isn’t it?”
“Thank you, Mr. Polat.”
For the rest of the morning, the two boys spent time visiting all the places marked with an X on the map. They went to the library to see the librarian.
“Do you have any treasures hidden in your library, Mrs. S?”
“Oh, I have lots of treasures, boys. This is one of them,” she said, holding up a book. “Would you like to read it together in the reading corner? There are some homemade cakes on the table too.”
On the way home, they met the local police officer who helped them cross the road.
“Have you seen any hidden treasures?” asked Omer. The police officer shook his head and laughed his big, deep laugh that always made the children laugh.

Omer arrived home with no treasures, but he had really enjoyed looking for them. He thought about the great afternoon he’d had: playing with Azra in the park, the delicious ice-cream from Mr. Polat, the great story the librarian offered them to read and the police officer’s really funny laugh. Suddenly, Omer knew what were the treasures the teacher had told them to look for!
“The people in my community are the treasures!” smiled Omer. “The treasures were there all along!”

qs.stem: Why was Omer interested in the homework for that weekend?
opts: Because he did it with his good friend.
Because many people helped him with it.
Because it took him only one morning.
Because it is different from the usual.

ex.ev: He didn’t want to do homework at the weekend, but the treasure hunt (搜寻) sounded like good fun.
ex.why: 他本来不想周末写作业，但这次是寻宝，听起来很好玩——和平常的作业不一样。

qs.stem: What was the weather like that Saturday morning?

ex.ev: “Don’t worry, and take them. It’s raining fire, isn’t it?”
ex.why: 「天上下火了」是夸张的说法，形容天气很热。

qs.stem: How many people did Omer and Azra turn to for Omer’s homework?

ex.ev: Omer arrived home with no treasures, but he had really enjoyed looking for them.
ex.why: 他们一路找了冰淇淋店主、图书管理员、警察三个人。

qs.stem: What do Azra, the ice-cream man, the librarian and the police officer have in common?

ex.ev: “Don’t worry, and take them.
ex.why: Azra 陪他做作业，冰淇淋店主少收钱，图书管理员请看书吃蛋糕，警察帮他们过马路——都很善良。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?

ex.ev: “The people in my community are the treasures!” smiled Omer.
ex.why: 最后 Omer 明白：社区里的人就是宝藏——「社区里的宝藏」。

articles.src: 2025年南阳市中考二模
articles.title: In our busy lives, it’s sometimes hard to take care of our p
body: [图:reading/564e4a23/image4.png]

In our busy lives, it’s sometimes hard to take care of our pets properly. Whether we’re at work or on vacation, it can be difficult to make sure they’re looked after. To solve the problem, a new pet caring technology comes in.
The pet caring technology helps us take care of our pets even when we’re not around. It has many advantages.

One of the advantages of the pet caring technology is that feeding pets without people’s help. We can set the device (设备) to give our pets food and water at certain times, so they’re never hungry or overfed, or thirsty.

Another good thing about the pet caring technology is that it lets us monitor (监控) our pets’ activity levels. The device has a camera and sensors (传感器) that can tell us if there’s any unusual activity or if our pets are feeling sad or upset.

The pet caring technology also keeps our pets safe. For example, some devices have alarms (警报器) that will sound if there’s a break-in or a fire. This way, we know our pets are protected, even when we’re far away.

And the best thing about the pet caring technology is that it’s very convenient. With just a few touches on our phone, we can see what our pets are doing, when they’re eating, and how they’ re feeling. This makes it easy for us to take good care of them, even when we’re not at home.

qs.stem: What does the writer mainly want to tell us in Paragraph 1?
opts: What our daily lives are like.
How we should look after our pets.
Why we have the pet sitting technology.
Where the pet caring technology comes from.

ex.ev: To solve the problem, a new pet caring technology comes in.
ex.why: 第一段说忙的时候照顾宠物难，为了解决这个问题才有了宠物照顾技术。

qs.stem: What can we do with the help of the pet caring technology? ① Feed our pets properly.             ② Give our pets a bath on time. ③ Know the conditions of our pets.       ④ Make our pets happy. ⑤ Keep our pets safe.             ⑥ Play games with our pets.

ex.ev: We can set the device (设备) to give our pets food and water at certain times,
ex.why: 能定时喂食（①）、监测宠物状况（③）、保护宠物安全（⑤）；没提洗澡、陪玩。

qs.stem: How does the writer explain his point in Paragraph 5?

ex.ev: For example, some devices have alarms (警报器) that will sound if there’s a break-in or a fire.
ex.why: 第五段用报警器的例子说明它能保护宠物安全。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “convenient” mean in Chinese?

ex.ev: With just a few touches on our phone, we can see what our pets are doing,
ex.why: 手机上点几下就能看宠物在做什么——convenient 是「方便的、便利的」。

qs.stem: In which part of a magazine can the text most probably be found?

ex.why: 介绍一种照顾宠物的新技术，最可能在「科学与技术」栏目。

cand: adj. 不寻常的；与众不同的

articles.src: 周口市西华县2026年普通高中招生第一次模拟考试试卷
articles.title: In a small village, there were two brothers named Jamie and Jack.
body: In a small village, there were two brothers named Jamie and Jack. They lived next door to each other on their farms for 20 years. They worked together and happily helped one another.

One day, the two brothers had a fight over a small misunderstanding, which quickly turned into a bigger problem. They stopped working together and began using malicious words towards each other. This led to complete silence between them, and neither spoke to the other again.
A week later, a man with a carpenter’s (木匠的) toolbox knocked on Jamie’s door and asked if he had any small jobs for him to do.

Jamie replied, “Yes, I have a job for you.” He pointed to a wide ditch (沟渠) on the farm and said, “My brother and I used to work together, but last week, he dug this ditch to separate our farms. I want you to build a tall fence there, so I needn’t see my brother anymore.”
The carpenter agreed. Jamie then left for town to do some shopping. Instead of the fence he had requested, he was surprised to see a beautiful bridge across the ditch when he returned.

Just as he was about to ask the carpenter, Jack walked across the bridge in tears. “I’m so sorry, Jamie. After all I’ve said, you still built this bridge to mend our relationship,” Jack said. “You’re the best brother ever.” He then hugged Jamie warmly.
They realized how important they were to each other. The bridge had become more than just a way to cross the ditch—it was a symbol of their renewed relationship and understanding.

qs.stem: Why did the two brothers have a fight?
opts: Jack refused to speak to his brother.
Jamie built a fence to separate their farms.
They didn’t help each other with farm work.

ex.ev: One day, the two brothers had a fight over a small misunderstanding,
ex.why: 吵架起因是一个小误会，就是没有好好理解对方。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “malicious” in paragraph 2 probably mean?

ex.ev: This led to complete silence between them, and neither spoke to the other again.
ex.why: 他们开始说……的话，导致彼此再也不说话——malicious 是「恶意的、不友善的」。

qs.stem: What do we know about the carpenter?
opts: He left without finishing the job.
He didn’t do the job as requested.
He wasn’t actually skilled at repairing things

ex.ev: Instead of the fence he had requested, he was surprised to see a beautiful bridge across the ditch when he returned.
ex.why: 木匠没建篱笆，而是建了一座桥——没按要求做。

qs.stem: How might Jack feel when he saw the bridge?

ex.ev: Just as he was about to ask the carpenter, Jack walked across the bridge in tears.
ex.why: Jack 流着泪走过桥，道歉、拥抱哥哥——被感动、很感激。

qs.stem: What does the author want to tell us through the story?
opts: Understanding can bridge the deepest divide.

ex.ev: it was a symbol of their renewed relationship and understanding.
ex.why: 这座桥成了兄弟和好、互相理解的象征——理解能跨越最深的隔阂。

articles.src: 周口市西华县2026年普通高中招生第一次模拟考试试卷
articles.title: Do you find it hard to concentrate on (专注于) reading books?
body: Do you find it hard to concentrate on (专注于) reading books? That’s probably because you spend a lot of time on the phone and your attention becomes weak. Here are some ways to help you put your phone down and get back into reading.
●Keep your phone as far away as possible.
16     When the phone is not by your side, it’s much easier to keep on reading. If you need to look things up or check your messages, go to where the phone is.
●Read physical books and make notes.
Some experts advise buying actual copies of books instead of reading online. Making notes is also part of the pleasure of reading.     17     It can give you more fun than looking at a screen.

Wake up in the morning, pick up a book first, not the phone and read some lines. Your mind will be given some thoughts. Or after a day’s study, get yourself into reading. It can slow you down and provide relaxation. When to read is up to you to decide.
●Turn to childhood favourite books.
When your brain is attracted (吸引) by a smartphone, return to the books you enjoyed as a child.     19     This will start your love for reading again.
Give these simple ways a try.     20     Let reading become a daily habit. Then, you’ll soon get back your attention and find endless joy in the wonderful world of books.

opts: It means your phone can’t be seen in the same room.
Work out your best time to read.
Open a book and write down something.
Those familiar stories can warm your heart.

16.ev: When the phone is not by your side, it’s much easier to keep on reading.
16.why: 手机放得越远越好，B「也就是说在同一个房间里看不到手机」。

17.ev: Making notes is also part of the pleasure of reading.
17.why: 做笔记是读书的乐趣，D「翻开书写点东西」。

18.ev: When to read is up to you to decide.
18.why: 这一条讲早上读或学习后读，什么时候读你自己定——小标题 C「找出你最好的读书时间」。

19.ev: return to the books you enjoyed as a child.
19.why: 重读小时候喜欢的书，E「那些熟悉的故事能温暖你的心」。

20.ev: Let reading become a daily habit.
20.why: 试试这些方法，A「放下手机」，让读书成为每天的习惯。

cand: adj. 无尽的；没完没了的

articles.src: 2026年南阳市油田中招第一次模拟考试试卷
articles.title: Leonardo da Vinci was both a highly talented artist and a gr
body: Leonardo da Vinci was both a highly talented artist and a great thinker.     36     He created world-famous works, like the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper. However, Leonardo was more than an artist. He was also very curious (好奇的) about science and nature. He studied how birds fly and then designed flying machines.     37

Albert Einstein was also a highly talented scientist and inventor. When Albert Einstein was young, he was quiet and slow to speak. At school, he showed great talent in math and science. As he grew up, he kept thinking about the universe. Finally, he developed the theory of relativity (相对论).     38     Einstein was not only smart but also kind. He often took time to reply to people who wrote to him.     39     He said the child should not worry because he also struggled with difficult math problems!

Both Leonardo da Vinci and Albert Einstein were curious and hard-working.     40     Their ideas and works are still important and inspiring today. They teach us that if we stay curious and keep working hard, we can also achieve great things. We should learn from them and never give up.

opts: He also drew plans for many other inventions.
He was born in Italy in 1452 and became one of the most famous painters in history.
They never stopped learning and asking questions.
Even when a child wrote to him about math problems, he replied kindly.
This important theory completely changed our traditional understanding of space, time, and gravity.

36.ev: He created world-famous works, like the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.
36.why: 后面说他创作了《蒙娜丽莎》等名作，前面应是 B「他 1452 年生于意大利，成了历史上最著名的画家之一」。

37.ev: He studied how birds fly and then designed flying machines.
37.why: 他设计了飞行器，A「他还为很多别的发明画了设计图」，also 是提示。

38.ev: Finally, he developed the theory of relativity (相对论).
38.why: 他提出了相对论，E「这个重要理论彻底改变了人们对时间、空间和重力的传统认识」。

39.ev: He often took time to reply to people who wrote to him.
39.why: 他常给写信的人回信，D「就连一个孩子写信问数学题，他也亲切地回了」，后面接他对孩子说的话。

40.ev: Both Leonardo da Vinci and Albert Einstein were curious and hard-working.
40.why: 两人都好奇又勤奋，C「他们从没停止学习和提问」。

cand: v. 艰难地做；努力争取

articles.src: 许昌市襄城县2025-26学年下期第一次中考九年级
articles.title: My father died when I was five.
body: My father died when I was five. It was hard on us all. My brother, who is eight years older than me, began to take care of my mother and me.
He took on more responsibilities than expected. I remember he made sure the rubbish was taken out, and the yard was cleaned. He did on his own, without being told to do so.

Because of my father’s death, Mom had to get a full-time job. Brother would get me up for school and make me breakfast. While I was eating, he would lay out my clothes, make my bed, and gather my school books up.

Hand in hand we would walk to the bus stop. As we waited, he would play games my father used to play with me. When we returned home from school, we were alone for about half an hour, until Mom was home from work. Before I did my homework, he would prepare something for Mom to cook dinner.
Mom would greet us with a hug and kiss. This was our time to have some fun outside. This was my brother’s time to be a kid.

One Saturday in June several years later, my mother and I were at a store where the Father’s Day cards were sold. I stared at the cards. Mom said, “Cindy, I know this is hard time for you.” “No, Mom. That’s not it. Why don’t they have Brother’s Day cards?” She smiled, “You’re right, your brother has exactly been a father to you. Go ahead to choose a card.” I did so, and on Father’s Day, my mother and I sat my brother down and gave him the card.
As he read it, I saw the tears in his eyes. Mom said, “Son, your father is proud of you, seeing that he raised a good man, and that you do your best to fill his shoes. We love you and thank you.”

qs.stem: Who asked the brother to take on more responsibilities?

ex.ev: He did on his own, without being told to do so.
ex.why: 没人让他做，是他自己主动承担的。

qs.stem: What did the brother do for the whole family? ① He got the writer up for school. ② He prepared for dinner. ③ He did the dishes every day. ④ He gathered up the writer’s books. ⑤ He played games with the writer. ⑥ He got a full-time job.

ex.ev: Brother would get me up for school and make me breakfast. While I was eating, he would lay out my clothes, make my bed, and gather my school books up.
ex.why: 叫她起床①、收拾书本④、在车站陪她玩游戏⑤、帮妈妈准备做晚饭②。洗碗③文中没有；找全职工作⑥的是妈妈。

qs.stem: When did the writer’s brother return to be a kid?
opts: When he played games with the writer at the bus stop. e
When he received a card from the writer.
When he served delicious cookies and milk.
When he had fun outside after Mom came back.

ex.ev: This was our time to have some fun outside. This was my brother’s time to be a kid.
ex.why: 妈妈下班回来后，他们去外面玩，这时哥哥才能做回一个孩子。

qs.stem: How did the writer’s brother feel while reading the card?

ex.ev: As he read it, I saw the tears in his eyes.
ex.why: 读贺卡时眼里有泪，是被感动了。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?

ex.ev: “You’re right, your brother has exactly been a father to you.
ex.why: 哥哥像父亲一样照顾她，她还在父亲节送哥哥贺卡——「我的第二个父亲」。

articles.title: It’s a hot time for Chinese language learning across the wor
body: It’s a hot time for Chinese language learning across the world, not only because of China’s higher position in the world but also because of the increasing economic and cultural connections between China and other countries.
For example the United Arab Emirates(UAE) plans to open Chinese language courses in 200 public primary and middle schools, so experienced Chinese teachers are needed.

Other Chinese courses opened across the world show the increasing need for Chinese speaking talent. Mandarin(普通话) became an elective(选修的) foreign language in Russia’s college entrance exam. Following English, German, French and Spanish, Mandarin has become the fifth elective test subject for the exam.

Spain has more than 40,000 people learning Chinese. Last year about 8,000 people took the Chinese Proficiency Test (HSK) exam. The number of people who took the test was the biggest, according to Xinhua News Agency.

In the US, learning Chinese has been thriving for many years and is now a popular choice for American children, especially those who were born in good families. The children begin to learn Chinese at an early age because their parents believe that learning Chinese will help them build successful international careers.

qs.stem: Why is Chinese language learning so hot?
opts: Because many foreigners like China’s culture.
Because China has the highest position in the world.
Because China helps a lot of countries to develop.
Because China has more international influence around the world.

ex.ev: not only because of China’s higher position in the world but also because of the increasing economic and cultural connections between China and other countries.
ex.why: 因为中国国际地位更高、和各国经济文化联系越来越多——中国的国际影响力更大了。不是「最高」。

qs.stem: The following languages are elective test subjects in Russia EXCEPT ________.

ex.ev: Following English, German, French and Spanish, Mandarin has become the fifth elective test subject for the exam.
ex.why: 俄罗斯的选考科目有英语、德语、法语、西班牙语和汉语，没有日语。

qs.stem: What is the Chinese meaning of the underlined word “thriving”?

ex.ev: is now a popular choice for American children,
ex.why: 在美国学中文多年来一直……，现在很受欢迎——thriving 是「兴盛的」。

qs.stem: What can we know about Chinese learning around the world?
opts: The UAE needs experienced English teachers.
All American children learn Chinese from an early age.
About one fifth of the Spanish learning Chinese took the HSK in 2018.
The Mandarin exam must be taken before going to Russia’s colleges.

ex.ev: Spain has more than 40,000 people learning Chinese. Last year about 8,000 people took the Chinese Proficiency Test (HSK) exam.
ex.why: 4 万人学中文，8000 人考了 HSK，大约五分之一。阿联酋需要的是中文老师；也不是所有美国孩子都学。

qs.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
opts: More people in the UAE begin to learn Chinese.
Chinese language learning is popular around the world.
Some foreign countries want more Chinese teachers.
Many American children are learning Chinese now.

ex.ev: It’s a hot time for Chinese language learning across the world,
ex.why: 第一句点题：全世界都在掀起学中文热。

articles.src: 鹤壁市2026年初中学业水平调研暨中考模拟测试
articles.title: One day, Andy was on his trip to business.
body: [图:reading/a664b5c1/image4.png]

One day, Andy was on his trip to business. While walking past a village, he saw many people busy with their work in a large field. At that moment, a young man who sat by the road caught his attention.
Andy wondered why the young man was free in such a busy season. Then he went up and asked, “Have you grown your vegetables?”

The young man shook his head and sighed, “Not yet! I’m afraid of the weather. If there is a storm, my vegetables may be destroyed. If it is too cold, the seeds (种子) may not come out from the ground at all. If it is too hot, the seeds may even go bad in the soil.”

Andy nodded his head and asked again, “Then, have you grown rice?” The young man thought for a while, and answered, “Not yet. I’m worried about the birds. They may eat the rice.  ▲ ” Andy was very surprised, “So, what have you grown then?”
The farmer replied, “I haven’t grown anything. I am waiting for the best time! I must make sure that nothing is going to destroy my plants.”
Of course, the best time never came. And the young man didn’t get anything from the field at last.

In our life, many people may have the same problem. They have dreams, but they don’t take action because they worry too much about the difficulties in the future. However, if they don’t do anything, how can they achieve their dreams?

qs.stem: Where did the story happen?

ex.ev: While walking past a village, he saw many people busy with their work in a large field.
ex.why: Andy 路过一个村庄时遇到了这个年轻人。

qs.stem: How did the young man feel when Andy talked to him?

ex.ev: “Not yet! I’m afraid of the weather.
ex.why: 他怕风暴、怕冷、怕热、怕鸟，一直在担心。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be put in “ ▲ ” in Paragraph 4?
opts: The field is not big enough either.
I’m sure birds will never come.
I don’t know how to grow rice.

ex.ev: I’m worried about the birds. They may eat the rice.
ex.why: 他担心鸟会吃稻子，所以不敢冒这个险——B「我不能冒这个险」。

qs.stem: What can we know about the young man?
opts: He grew lots of vegetables and rice.
He knew he would get nothing at first.
He worked hard in the field every day.
He waited for perfect conditions to farm.

ex.ev: I am waiting for the best time! I must make sure that nothing is going to destroy my plants.
ex.why: 他在等最好的时机，要确保什么都不会毁掉庄稼——等完美的条件才种。

qs.stem: What does the story want to tell us?
opts: A good beginning is half done.
He who risks nothing gets nothing.

ex.ev: However, if they don’t do anything, how can they achieve their dreams?
ex.why: 什么都不敢冒险，就什么也得不到——不入虎穴，焉得虎子。
