articles.title: “Look at this,” I said to my friend Lily, holding up the col
body: “Look at this,” I said to my friend Lily, holding up the colorful paper. “There’s a three-day art camp at Greenfield this summer!”

Lily looked at the paper, “Emma, it’s during the last week of July,” she said. “That’s the same time as my family’s trip to the beach.” Lily handed the paper back to me. “You’re the artist, not me,” she smiled. “My little brother thought the flowers I painted were spaghetti.”
“But you can learn to draw,” I said in my most encouraging voice. I really didn’t want to go alone.
Later, I called two other friends, but they both had their own summer plans. I folded the paper into a ball and threw it on my desk.

To relax myself, I went outside to draw the maple tree (枫树) at my neighbor Weston’s. As I sat on the stone, I thought about the art camp and wished I could be a little braver. Lily could make friends with other kids in 10 minutes, but I always felt nervous when I didn’t know anyone around me. I was about to give up the camp when Mr. Weston came by to look at my sketch (草图).
“Nice work,” he said. “  ▲ , you know. Their roots (根) don’t grow straight down—they spread out, even when it’s hard. That’s how they get stronger.”

His words hit me. It reminded me of the art camp and my own roots. I wasn’t reaching them out at all. Instead, I was planting myself into one deep place because I felt safer. I suddenly realized that if I wanted to grow, I had to start reaching out too.
That night, I took a deep breath and made a new decision.
[图:reading/12873d07/image3.png]

qs.stem: When may the art camp be held?

ex.ev: “Emma, it’s during the last week of July,” she said.
ex.why: 艺术营在七月最后一周，只有 7 月 26–28 日符合。

qs.stem: What does the underlined sentence probably mean?
opts: Lily was not good at drawing.
Lily could cook spaghetti very well.
Lily could draw better than her brother.

ex.ev: “You’re the artist, not me,” she smiled.
ex.why: Lily 画的花被弟弟看成意大利面，说明她不擅长画画。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be put in  ▲ ?
opts: We can not climb the tree
You are so brave and patient

ex.ev: Their roots (根) don’t grow straight down—they spread out, even when it’s hard. That’s how they get stronger.
ex.why: 后面讲树根向外伸展才会更强壮，前面应是 C「树能教给我们一些道理」。

qs.stem: What is the possible ending to the story?
opts: Emma went to the camp alone.
Emma invited Mr. Weston to the camp.
Emma cut off the roots of the maple tree.

ex.ev: I suddenly realized that if I wanted to grow, I had to start reaching out too.
ex.why: 她明白了要成长就得走出去，当晚做了新决定——一个人去艺术营。

qs.stem: Which saying can best match the story?
opts: East or west, home is best.

ex.ev: Instead, I was planting myself into one deep place because I felt safer.
ex.why: Emma 明白不能把自己封闭起来，要向外伸展、和别人建立联系——没有人是一座孤岛。

articles.src: 2026年焦作市沁阳市初中学业水平模拟测试
articles.title: Everyone enjoys the rain.
body: Everyone enjoys the rain. Rain is a wonderful treasure from nature! Rain lowers the high temperature! Rain is vital to the growth of plants!

Have you ever asked yourself how rain is formed? It’s like boiling water. If you haven’t seen this process yet, try this simple science experiment. Heat some water in a pot. As the water boils, the heat turns the water into hot water vapor (蒸汽). The change of water into water vapor is called evaporation (蒸发). When you put a cover on the boiling pot, the vapor hits the cover and turns into water drops. This is what we call condensation (凝结). Condensation happens when the water vapor changes into liquid (液体) when touching any surface. The higher the temperature of the air is, the more water vapor it can hold.

Water from lakes, rivers and oceans turns into water vapor because of the hot sun. The water vapor rises into the air through evaporation and is kept in the same form but unseen until condensation happens. Since the vapor can’t rise more than a certain height, it remains at the same height above sea.

When the wind blows, whether it is warm or cold, it carries the vapor and raises it. In the sky, a huge amount of water vapor created by evaporation gets together to form clouds. When these clouds meet cold surfaces like mountains or cold air as they rise up, condensation happens. Then, the clouds turn into tiny water drops and fall to the ground. These small water drops falling from the sky are what we call rain.
[图:reading/12873d07/image4.png]

qs.stem: Which of the following can take the place of “is vital to” in the text?

ex.ev: Rain is vital to the growth of plants!
ex.why: 雨对植物生长非常重要——is vital to 可以换成 plays a key role in（起关键作用）。

qs.stem: What do you know from Paragraph 2?
opts: Boiling water is different from making rain.
Boiling water can hardly make water become vapor.
Evaporation is the process of turning vapour into water.
The process of vapour changing into water is called condensation.

ex.ev: This is what we call condensation (凝结).
ex.why: 水蒸气遇到锅盖变成水滴，叫凝结。水变成水蒸气才叫蒸发。

qs.stem: Which shows the relation between temperature change and the water vapor air can hold? [x: temperature (℃); y: water vapor air can hold (g/m3)]

ex.ev: The higher the temperature of the air is, the more water vapor it can hold.
ex.why: 气温越高，空气能容纳的水汽越多，B 图是上升的直线。

qs.stem: How does the writer organize Paragraph 3 and Paragraph 4?
opts: Para. 3 is the first step, and Para. 4 continues the whole process.
Para. 3 shows a fact, and Para. 4 expresses the writer’s opinions.
Para. 3 lists reasons, and Para. 4 draws a conclusion (结论).
Para. 3 offers advice, and Para. 4 gives an example.

ex.ev: When the wind blows, whether it is warm or cold, it carries the vapor and raises it.
ex.why: 第三段讲水变成水汽升空（第一步），第四段接着讲水汽成云、变成雨（后续过程）。

qs.stem: What’s the text mainly about?

ex.ev: Have you ever asked yourself how rain is formed?
ex.why: 全文讲雨是怎样形成的。

cand: adj. 至关重要的；必不可少的

articles.src: 2026年焦作市沁阳市初中学业水平模拟测试
articles.title: In today’s world, it’s easy to spend too much time in front
body: In today’s world, it’s easy to spend too much time in front of phones, computers, and other screens.     36     While they can be useful for study and fun, overuse harms your eyes and health. Here are four simple ways to help you cut your screen time.

Without limits (限制), it’s easy to spend hours on screens.     37     Decide how much time you want to spend on certain apps or screens each day, and stick to that limit. You can even use apps that allow you to set how long you can use them each day, which can help you lower screen time.

You can also create screen-free spaces at home. Think about where you use your phones the most, like your bedroom.     38     And put your phone far away in your bedroom, so you will not pick it up too often. This helps you cut down screen time.

We usually check our phones whenever we receive notifications (通知), even if they’re not important.     39     Doing this small thing will stop you from checking your phone for no good reason all day long.
40     Nature makes you feel fresh. A slow walk in the park, a fun game with friends, or quiet time sitting outside will pull you away from screens easily and make you feel happy.

opts: They are part of daily life.
You can start by setting clear goals.
Use a normal alarm clock to wake you up every day.

36.ev: While they can be useful for study and fun, overuse harms your eyes and health.
36.why: 手机电脑……，虽然有用但用多了伤身，前面应是 A「它们是日常生活的一部分」。

37.ev: Decide how much time you want to spend on certain apps or screens each day, and stick to that limit.
37.why: 后面讲决定每天用多长时间，前面 D「可以从定清楚目标开始」。

38.ev: And put your phone far away in your bedroom, so you will not pick it up too often.
38.why: 卧室里别放手机，E「用普通闹钟叫你起床」，And 后面接着说把手机放远。

39.ev: We usually check our phones whenever we receive notifications (通知), even if they’re not important.
39.why: 一来通知就看手机，B「把通知关掉很简单」。

40.ev: Nature makes you feel fresh.
40.why: 这一段讲去公园散步、在户外坐坐，开头 C「多花时间在户外」。

articles.src: 商丘市睢阳区2026年中招模拟试卷
articles.title: It was a rainy Sunday afternoon.
body: It was a rainy Sunday afternoon. I was sitting in my room, feeling bored. I had planned to go out and meet my friends, but the bad weather had ruined my plans. I decided to look through some old photo albums. As I turned the pages, I saw pictures of my family’s past vacations, birthday parties, and other happy moments. There was one photo that caught my eye. It was a picture of me and my grandfather standing in a beautiful garden. The sun was shining, and we were both smiling brightly.

My grandfather had passed away a few years ago, and I really missed him. I remembered how he used to take me to that garden every weekend. He would show me all the different kinds of flowers and teach me about their names and characteristics. He told me that there was beauty everywhere if we just took the time to look for it.

Suddenly, I heard a knock on my door. It was my dad. He said, “Hey, why don’t we go for a walk in the rain? It can be fun.” I was a bit surprised and didn’t really want to go, but I didn’t want to disappoint him either. So I went out with him.

As we walked along the street, I noticed the raindrops falling on the leaves of the trees, making them look shiny and fresh. As we walked deeper into the park, I saw something amazing. The raindrops had formed little waterfalls on the branches of a willow tree. The drops were falling one by one, creating a beautiful and peaceful scene.

I realized that my grandfather was right. Even on a rainy day, there was beauty all around us. By the time we got home, I was no longer feeling bored. I was actually glad that the rain had stopped me from going out with my friends because I had discovered a new kind of beauty.

qs.stem: Why was the writer feeling bored at the beginning of the story?
opts: Because it was a sunny day and he had nothing to do.
Because he couldn’t go out to meet his friends because of the rain.
Because he was looking through some old photo albums.
Because he missed his grandfather very much.

ex.ev: I had planned to go out and meet my friends, but the bad weather had ruined my plans.
ex.why: 本来要出去见朋友，下雨打乱了计划，所以很无聊。

qs.stem: What did the writer’s grandfather use to do with him?
opts: Take him to the park to play football every weekend.
Teach him how to take photos in the garden.
Show him different flowers and teach him about them.

articles.title: “Ava, why don’t you read this paragraph for us?
body: “Ava, why don’t you read this paragraph for us?” Miss Margaret asked. Ava was nervous, but she stood up and began reading.   She was nervous because she stammered.“Em...Emma was stand...ing...” Hearing this, some of the students started laughing. After class, Ava made her way to the library, hoping to avoid those students and practice reading. She sat in a far corner of the library and started practicing. However, after a number of tries, she realized that reading fluently was still too hard for her. She clearly needed a great deal of practice and help.

Aliza, one of her classmates who had been watching her for some time, went over to Ava and offered to help. From then on, every day whenever they had free time, Aliza would go to help Ava with her reading. A few weeks later, Ava began to read better and her confidence grew.

At the end of the semester, Miss Margaret held a reading test. When it was Ava’s turn, to everyone’s surprise, Ava read the paragraph fluently. Miss Margaret praised Ava for her improved reading ability. Aliza felt proud of Ava as well. Ava and Aliza became good friends after that. Ava was very thankful to Aliza for everything she did. She also came to realize that there are always two types of people in the world: those who make fun of you and those who help you overcome your weaknesses (弱点). The point is that we shouldn’t allow others’ words to hold us back. Instead, we can use their laughter to push us to improve ourselves. But for those who help and support us, we should show how much we appreciate them. Even a simple thank you can go a long way in showing our appreciation. Most importantly, we should also work to be the same kind of helpful person for others in need.

articles.title: A Taste of Potato Stuffing Potato stuffing is a popular dish.
body: A Taste of Potato Stuffing Potato stuffing is a popular dish. Let’s explore how to make it.   [图:reading/699757fd/image1.png]
Let’s Get Ready!
•1½ pounds of white potatoes   •1 spoon of butter
•1 medium-sized onion   •¼ spoon of black pepper
•1½ bell peppers (甜椒)   •¼ cup of raisins (葡萄干)
•3 spoons of cooking oil   •½ cup of milk
•2 spoons of tomato sauce (番茄酱)   •1 egg
•2 spoons of sugar   •hot sauce
Let’s Cook!

Step 1: Wash, peel, and cut the potatoes and then boil them for 6 minutes. Step 2: Heat the oil in a pan over a low heat. Add the onion and bell peppers. Then, cook the tomato sauce, black pepper, sugar, and raisins for 5 minutes. Step 3: Mash (捣碎) the potatoes. Mix them with butter and milk. Then add the cooked mixture to the potatoes. Step 4: Beat the egg and add it to the potatoes. Step 5: Put a little butter on a baking dish (烤盘) . Use a spoon to spread the mixture on the dish. Step 6: Bake the dish at 325°F for 20 minutes or until the mixture is golden brown. After cooling for a while, cut it into pieces before serving.

articles.title: My family had a long history of growing up poor.
body: My family had a long history of growing up poor. Both my mom and dad came from large families with little more than the clothes on their backs. Their parents had also grown up with very little.

When I was five, I showed interest in computers. Before long, I was trying to take apart (拆卸) an old computer in my school’s classroom. By Grade 3, I had learned to program. Then, one day in high school, my computer science teacher suggested I take part in a computer training activity. He gave me a brochure (宣传手册) and I excitedly took it home. However, that excitement quickly disappeared as my mom saw the price of the activity. That evening, I went into my room and cried my eyes out.

But a few weeks later, I got a phone call. It was the head of the training activity telling me I’d be taking part in it. I could hardly believe my ears. During the activity, I met many like-minded kids and learned many skills.

Then, two years after that life-changing summer, one day, I received another call from the head. “I’ve found something I think you’ll want to see,” he said. He suggested we meet. When we met, he took out a long, handwritten letter my mom had sent when I was 15. She wrote I was the smartest kid. She talked a lot about my early love for computers. She ended by saying she couldn’t pay for the cost of the activity and hoped that they would still accept me. I broke down in tears right then and there.

Over the years, I went on to learn as much as I could. I got a job where I could use all my skills. Now, I’m proud to say that I’ve changed my family’s history of living poorly. And all I want to do now is sit down with my mom and thank her for everything she has done for me. Without her, I would never have the bright life I have today.

articles.title: A smile shows that a person is happy.
body: A smile shows that a person is happy. For example, a person may smile when he or she is pleased with the grade on a test. Or a person might smile if a friend told a funny joke.     36     But smiles are more than just a way for people to show that they are happy. There are other good reasons to smile often.
37     In fact, it only takes 17 muscles (肌肉) to smile. On the other hand, it takes 43 muscles to show unhappiness. So give the muscles in your face a rest and smile!

38     People may try to look nice on the outside by exercising or wearing nice clothes. However, there is a famous saying: a smile is the best thing a person can wear. That is because it is easy to be around someone who is smiling and happy. Almost no one wants to be around someone who is unhappy all the time.

Smiles have power. Both smiling and laughing can easily and quickly spread from one person to another. If one person smiles, people around him or her want to smile, too. Similarly, when a person laughs, people tend (倾向于) to laugh with them. If a person is sad, the best thing to do is share a smile or laugh.     39
Smiling and laughing are very good for the body.     40     You’ll find that it will be hard to stay mad or sad for very long!

articles.title: When Jude was twelve, he had a stammer (口吃).
body: When Jude was twelve, he had a stammer (口吃). This made it hard for him to speak. At school, he often wanted to tell the lunch lady what he would like to eat, but the words would not come out right. Once, when he tried to order his meal, he kept repeating sounds. The students around him began to laugh at him. He felt very embarrassed. After that day, he tried to avoid the canteen (食堂). He felt that other students did not understand him.

One day, his teacher gave him a chance to speak in front of the class. It was a short talk at the class meeting, but it was a chance for Jude to express himself. He knew that if he worked hard, he could show his true self to the students.

Jude began to prepare. He spoke slowly and clearly. He practiced in front of a mirror every day. He asked his parents to listen and give suggestions. He learned to breathe slowly and take his time when a word was hard to say. He also practiced the whole speech many times.

On the day of the speech, Jude felt very nervous. The whole class was quiet. He began to speak. His voice was not perfect, but he kept going. He told the students about the time in the canteen and how he had felt. He told them that people with a stammer had many hopes and ideas. He asked his classmates to be patient and give them time to express themselves.

The students clapped (鼓掌) after his speech. Some said sorry for laughing at him before. They said they did not know how hard it was. Jude felt proud. The speech not only helped him a lot but also helped others know the true feelings of people who stammer.
After that, Jude wrote a book about his life with a stammer. He wanted more people to know how people with a stammer felt and hoped everyone would have time to speak.

articles.title: When you’re lost in something and forget the things around y
body: When you’re lost in something and forget the things around you, you get into the flow (心流).

What does it mean?     36     Maybe you’re in a race and all you hear is your heart beating, or you’re so busy writing an article that you forget where you are. A psychologist (心理学家) named Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi described this as being in the flow.

37     Csikszentmihalyi described flow as the secret to happiness. Putting all your energy into something makes you proud of your achievements. It helps you think more clearly because you almost forget everything around you. If you’re focusing (集中) on a game of chess, for example, you’re not worrying about your schoolwork.     38     Being in the flow also helps you feel good because you’re doing something for yourself, not for a prize or to please other people.

How can you find the flow?     39     It can take 10 to 15 minutes to focus your attention on something before you get fully into it. Flow often happens when you’re doing something you enjoy, so pick a challenge that’s fun but you know you can do it. Find a quiet space without any things that may stop you paying attention to what you are doing. It also helps if you’re doing something because you want to, not because you have to.     40     And then you can try other things. Getting into the flow can make activities more enjoyable too.

articles.title: Sue and Johnsy were two young artists living in a small room.
body: Sue and Johnsy were two young artists living in a small room. One cold November, Johnsy became very sick.
The doctor told Sue, “Johnsy doesn’t want to live. You must give her hope.”
But Johnsy had given up. She looked out of the window at an old vine (葡萄藤). “Look,” she said to Sue. “The leaves are falling. When the last leaf falls, I will die.”
“That’s silly!” Sue said. But Johnsy would not listen.

Sue was worried. She went to see their neighbor, old Mr. Behrman, who was a painter and had never been successful. When Sue told him what Johnsy thought about the leaf, he became very angry. “How can someone die because of a leaf?” he cried.
That night, it stormed outside.
The next morning, Johnsy asked to see the vine. She was sure the last leaf would be gone. But to her surprise, one leaf was still there, holding on bravely in the wind and rain.
The following day, the leaf was still there. Johnsy looked at it for a long time. “I’ve been silly, Sue,” she said finally. “________” Then she asked for some food and began to feel hopeful again.
In the afternoon, the doctor visited. “You will be fine, Johnsy,” he said. “But I must see Mr. Behrman downstairs. He is very sick. I’m afraid he won’t make it through the night.”

The next day, Sue came to Johnsy’s bed. “Mr. Behrman died this morning,” she said. Then she led Johnsy to the window. “Look at the last leaf. Have you ever wondered why it never moved in the wind?” Sue explained, “Mr. Behrman was found lying in bed helplessly with pain yesterday morning. His shoes and clothes were wet and cold. That stormy night, when the last real leaf fell, he went outside and painted a new leaf on the wall. It’s his greatest painting.”

body: Have you ever heard someone being described as conscientious (尽心尽责的)?     36     Studies have found that people with this quality (品质) usually do well in their work and have good relationships with other people.

Being conscientious means you want to do your work well and try your best. You don’t give up easily and you do things without waiting to be told.     37     They follow rules, finish their homework early and well, and keep trying especially when tasks are hard. They are responsible and often help others.

Carrying on with tasks and staying active when things get hard is a key part of being conscientious. It can be difficult, but there are ways to make it easier.     38     It means finding ways to keep moving forward, even if it’s a small step at a time. When something gets difficult, it’s important for you to fight against the strong wish to give up.     39     Trying hard is as important as the result. This helps you understand that mistakes and difficulties are a normal part of learning. Each time you finish something difficult, you feel proud, and that builds confidence.

40     If you plan to join a club or do homework after school, do it and don’t let anything easily get in your way. Following through on your plans shows people that you are a person they can trust. This is a very useful skill as you grow up.

articles.title: August Pullman was born with a very rare (罕见的) condition.
body: August Pullman was born with a very rare (罕见的) condition. It made his face look different from other kids. For years his parents taught him at home to keep him away from strange looks and hurtful words.

When August was ten, his parents thought it was time for him to go to school. But August had a fear of unkind eyes, so he always sat at the back of the class quietly and never took part in class activities. A boy named Jack chose the seat next to him. Jack’s friendly chatter (喋喋不休) about everyday things slowly drew August out. August began sharing his love of planets. Jack enjoyed being with August.

However, at a festival party, August heard a painful truth. Jack told another boy Julian that he made friends with August only because their teacher had asked him to. August’s heart was broken. For weeks the two boys did not speak. One day Julian said mean words about August. Standing nearby, Jack suddenly realized something. He had done the same to August. He fought with Julian. After that, Jack went to find August.
“I’m really sorry, August,” Jack said sincerely (真诚地). “I want to be your friend because of you. You’re smart, kind, and the bravest person I know.”

August saw the honesty in Jack’s eyes and gave a small nod. From that moment they became true friends. Jack stood up for August, and August helped Jack with his schoolwork patiently. Gradually, other students got used to August’s face and found that he was humorous and kind. They were willing to talk and play games with him. August even joined a class trip to the mountains, no longer hiding at the back. He became more outgoing, and finally enjoyed his warm and happy school life.

articles.title: 素材改编自Highlights “Ow,” Caroline cried on a hot summer morning.
body: 素材改编自Highlights
“Ow,” Caroline cried on a hot summer morning.

“I’m sorry,” her mother said. She brushed Caroline’s long, thick hair as softly as she could, but the brush got stuck (卡住的) again. Her mom looked at the clock and told her, “Your aunt Kiki should be here any minute. She will help cut your hair.”

When Aunt Kiki came, she greeted Caroline with a hug and a wide smile. After a moment’s consideration, she suggested that short hair should be better for Caroline. “It will be simple to care for, and you’ll feel cooler too,” she said.
Caroline liked the idea. She hoped the new look would make her appear like a star in a movie.
However, when Aunt Kiki finished cutting her hair and held out a mirror, Caroline gasped (倒抽气) and covered her face with her hands.
“What’s wrong, dear?” Aunt Kiki asked.
“It’s—it’s too short!” Caroline said, her voice shaking.
“Caroline, it will be easy to take care of,” she said softly. “And now we can see more of your beautiful face.”
But these words couldn’t make Caroline feel any better. Her grandfather’s look of surprise even brought tears to her eyes.

A few days later, the weather was even hotter. The family went on a trip to the seaside. Caroline jumped into the sea to cool off. Soon she noticed something amazing. Without her long hair, she felt light and free when moving in the water. Nothing covered her face or slowed her down.

That evening, after cleaning up at home, Caroline looked at herself in the mirror. She looked for a long time. Then, she picked up her brush. It moved through her hair smoothly. She felt good and free. She put a small butterfly barrette (小发夹) in her hair, and a smile appeared on her face. She realized that a change could be a good thing, often bringing unexpected advantages. If you’ re willing to see it from a fresh perspective (视角), you can surely discover the bright side it offers.
[图:reading/0ea3b781/image1.png]

articles.title: Do you often play ball?
body: Do you often play ball? Have you ever wondered which of your balls can bounce（反弹）the highest? You can find out by trying this simple test.

To begin with, you will need a few different balls, such as a basketball, a soccer ball, and a tennis ball. Use what you have on hand. Do this test inside a room, but before you start, ask your parents where you can do this to make sure you won’t break anything or get hurt.

The next thing to do is to prepare a piece of paper to write down what you see. Draw a table with three columns（列）. In the first column, write the name of the ball. In the second column, you will later record how high it bounces. In the third column, you will record how many times it bounces.

Now, find an empty wall. Stick a note on it at a certain height. This will be your starting line. Release each ball, one at a time, from this line. When each ball bounces up, stick a note on the wall where it reaches the highest point. Write the ball’s name on that note.

After that, use a ruler to measure（测量）how high each note is. Write that number in the second column on your paper. Then, drop each ball one more time. This time, count how many times it jumps up and down before it stops. Write that number in the third column.
Now look at your paper. Which ball bounces the highest? Which one jumps the most times? Is it the same ball? This fun test helps you learn by doing.

opts: To get more kinds of balls.

To have them record the results.

opts: How to get the balls ready.

body: In modern life, phones and computers are everywhere. They help us with schoolwork and are fun to use, but too much screen time can be harmful.     36     We all need to find a good balance (平衡) in our daily lives.

Once we know our habits, it’s time to make some rules. A simple rule is not to use our phones during meals.     38     A second good rule is to avoid screens before bedtime so that we can get better sleep. Following these rules will make our lives healthier.

39     Why not try reading books, drawing pictures, or playing outside with friends? We can also help with cooking at home. These activities are fun and give our minds a break from screens. They also help us learn new things.
Remember that phones and computers should work for us, not control us.     40     Let’s use technology wisely so it helps rather than harms our daily lives.

36     If I have a problem and cannot think of an answer, I can “sleep on it”. Often an answer comes to me the next day.

Let’s say some co-workers are working on a project together, and they run into a difficult problem.     37     One person might say, “Look, we’re not getting anywhere. So, let’s sleep on it. Tomorrow we can try to figure this out.”

To “sleep on” something means you give yourself time to think about a problem overnight.     38     For example, if I am writing a story and run into a problem, I often sleep on it. I think about the problem before I go to sleep and hope that my sleeping self comes to the rescue (救援)!

Sometimes we use this expression when we just want more time to pass. We also use it when we want to look at a problem with a rested mind.     39     Sometimes a problem doesn’t look so bad the next day after a good night’s sleep.

40     Some problems are not a big deal——they are not important. You can describe them as “nothing to lose sleep over”. And if you want to say you are not going to worry about something, you can say you’re “not going to lose sleep over it”.
So, next time, if you run into a problem with English, try sleeping on it! Maybe the answer will come to you with the morning sun.

opts: No one can think of a way to solve it.
But “to sleep on” has another meaning.
We know that sleep is necessary to be healthy.
And you plan to make a decision about it later.

36.why: 前面讲睡在床上、地上，这里 C「但 sleep on 还有另一个意思」，后面解释。

38.ev: To “sleep on” something means you give yourself time to think about a problem overnight.
38.why: 给自己一晚上时间想问题，E「打算以后再做决定」。

39.ev: We also use it when we want to look at a problem with a rested mind.

articles.title: At the school writing club, Penny and I were paired up as cr
body: At the school writing club, Penny and I were paired up as critique (评论) partners-friends who read each other’s writing and gave helpful advice. She could write perfect sentences, while my ideas were great but my grammar was messy.

Just after we handed our stories to each other, something felt strange. Then it hit me: she had copied the idea from a story I had read! I couldn’t believe it. How could she do that? My mind was racing. After a deep breath, I forced myself to tell her the truth.

A long, silent moment passed before she finally spoke,“ Jenny...I knew I shouldn’t have done this...but I never had a single idea for a story...” With that, she rushed off, a few tears rolling down her face.
Suddenly, I remembered what my job as her critique partner was to help. But how?

The question stayed in my mind until I saw my mom and brother building a tall tower in the living room. Mom stacked (垒) the blocks colorfully but some fell quickly, while my brother made the base safe but not so colorful. Then they decided to work together: her eye for color and his care for strength made the tower taller, stronger, and more colorful—much better than either could do alone.
Suddenly it clicked!

The next morning, I found Penny and made a suggestion. I said, “What if we worked on a story together?” “Can we?” she asked with doubt mixed with hope. “I do have one new idea. Maybe we can write about two friends,” I said. “And one has a big problem and they shared their own strengths.” “And everything ends up perfectly,” she added.
I smiled, “Just like us!”

qs.stem: What was Penny good at as a good critique partner?

ex.ev: She could write perfect sentences, while my ideas were great but my grammar was messy.
ex.why: Penny 能写出完美的句子——擅长语法；作者是点子好、语法乱。

qs.stem: How did the writer feel when she found Penny used another story’s idea?

ex.ev: I couldn’t believe it. How could she do that?
ex.why: 发现 Penny 抄了别人故事的点子，作者不敢相信——很吃惊。

qs.stem: Why does the writer describe her mom and brother building a tower?
opts: To show a new problem came.
To show how she got the solution.

ex.ev: Suddenly it clicked!
ex.why: 看到妈妈和弟弟合作搭出更好的塔，她一下子想到了办法——说明她怎样找到解决办法。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “strengths” refer to?
opts: The things that make you better.

ex.ev: her eye for color and his care for strength made the tower taller, stronger, and more colorful
ex.why: 妈妈会配色、弟弟会搭稳——strengths 指各自的长处、能让事情更好的东西。

qs.stem: Which words can best describe the writer?

ex.ev: Suddenly, I remembered what my job as her critique partner was to help.
ex.why: 她没有揭发 Penny，而是想办法帮她，提议一起写故事——体贴、乐于助人。

articles.title: Jenny loved painting.
body: Jenny loved painting. One day, she was excited to take her first art class. The art teacher Mrs. Minton told the children to paint the flowers in a vase (花瓶). “Don’t worry if your painting is different from others’.” she said. “The important thing is to paint what you see.”

Jenny worked very hard. After painting for a long time, she rested and looked at the painting next to hers. “That’s really good, she said to Carrie, Every flower in Carrie’s painting was like the real flowers in the vase.”
“Thanks.” Carrie said, looking over at Jenny’s painting. “Oh! What happened to yours?”
“What do you mean?” asked Jenny. She looked at her own painting. It was very different from Carrie’s. It covered the whole page and the colors were brighter than the real flowers.
“It looks like a big mess.” said Carrie. “Did you spill (泼出) the paints?”
“No.” said Jenny, upset. “I painted what I saw just like Mrs. Minton said.”
“It’s OK, you know,” said Carrie. “Not everyone is good at art.”
Jenny felt as though she might cry. She loved painting so much and now it seemed she wasn’t very good at it. “Is it really bad?” she asked Mrs. Minton.
“Bad?” said Mrs. Minton. “Oh no! It’s wonderful, Jenny. It’s so full of color and happiness.”
Jenny was very surprised.
“But Mrs. Minton, it doesn’t look anything like the flowers you told us to paint,” Carrie said.

“Maybe not to you, Carrie. Everyone sees different things when they look at the world.” Mrs. Minton answered softly. She showed them a picture in a book. “This is a picture an artist painted of his own face. This is how he saw himself.”
“But...it’s just a few lines.” said Carrie. “It doesn’t look anything like a real person.”

Mrs. Minton turned to Jenny. “Everyone sees the world differently. Art isn’t about copying—it’s about showing what’s in your heart.” Jenny looked at her painting again, with a confident smile on her face.

ex.why: 艺术不是照搬，而是表达内心——「画出你心里的东西」。

body: Finding your goal in life is far more than a common saying. It gives you confidence, satisfaction and happiness, and acts as the key to living a happy life.     16     Also, they can face difficulties more bravely and live a happier life. However, it is not easy for everyone to find their own life goals. Here are some helpful ways for you.

articles.title: Hector was about to compete in the school geography bee.
body: [图:reading/bc4a147a/image6.png]
Hector was about to compete in the school geography bee. He studied hard in the library, wishing to win and show he was a “smart kid.”
One lunchtime, Hector and his friend Abby found an envelope (信封) dropped by Mr. Adler, the bee’s organizer.
They picked it up, and Hector’s eyes widened at the red words on it: Geography Bee Questions and Answers.
“What’s up?” Abby asked. “I hope you’re not thinking this envelope is your ticket to winning tomorrow, because cheating (作弊) is never the right way to win,” she said seriously.
“I’ll return it soon,” Hector lied nervously, pushing it into his backpack.

On the way to Mr. Adler’s room, Hector’s desire (渴望) to win took over. He hid in the boys’ bathroom, opened the envelope and looked through the answers. His face turned bright red and he knew he’d made a mistake. Filled with regret, he stayed away from everyone.
Later, he met his geography teacher. She hugged him and said, “Winning isn’t everything. Working hard is what matters.” Her words gave him courage.
Hector went to Mr. Adler’s room at once.
“Oh, Hector! I was just looking for...” Mr. Adler said.
“This?” Hector held out the open envelope.
“No, actually, I was looking for...” Mr. Adler noticed the envelope. “Where did you get that? And why is it open?”

“I... Uh... I... I just...” Then in a flood of words he told Mr. Adler about finding the envelope, opening the envelope, and spending hours arguing with himself. Finally, he ended up saying, “You might not believe me, but I didn’t memorize the answers or use them.”
“I know.” He didn’t punish (惩罚) him, saying, “I don’t punish people for correcting their mistakes. I’ll write new questions.”
The next day at the bee, Hector was out in round three. He felt no sadness but smiled. He finally understood:  ▲

opts: Show it to the other students.

ex.ev: “I hope you’re not thinking this envelope is your ticket to winning tomorrow, because cheating (作弊) is never the right way to win,”
ex.why: Abby 担心他想用信封里的答案作弊来赢。

opts: Because he knew he was wrong.
Because the bathroom was very hot.

ex.why: 看了答案他满脸通红，知道自己做错了。

qs.stem: What was the main reason why Mr. Adler chose not to punish Hector?
opts: Hector returned the envelope before the bee.
Mr. Adler felt sorry for dropping the envelope.

ex.ev: “I don’t punish people for correcting their mistakes.
ex.why: Adler 老师说：改正错误的人他不惩罚——Hector 说了实话、改正了错误。

qs.stem: How did Hector feel after the competition?

ex.ev: He felt no sadness but smiled.
ex.why: 第三轮就被淘汰，他却不难过还笑了——很轻松。

qs.stem: Which of the following can be put in  ▲ ?
opts: Friends can help us make good decisions.

ex.why: 他靠诚实参赛，输了也坦然——诚实比赢重要得多。

articles.title: Today AI has become a very useful tool.
body: Today AI has become a very useful tool. It can help you with homework, answer your questions, and create new things.     16     It is important for you to learn how to use AI safely. Here are four key tips (提示) to keep you safe while using AI.

One key rule is to be careful with what you share with AI. AI learns from your words, so never share personal or private information. This includes your address, phone number, or secret information. Here’s a good rule:     17

Another important thing to remember is that AI isn’t always perfect and it can make mistakes.   It may give wrong answers to your homework,   wrong facts or wrong explanations.     18     You need to think on your own, check your textbooks, or ask teachers and parents to make sure the information is true.

You also need to watch out for deepfake (深度伪造) information created by AI.     19     They can use AI to create fake voices or photos that sound or look like people you trust.They may be used to steal your money. If you see these videos or get such calls, please call the real person to check if it is true.

20     AI is a helpful tool, but it can never take the place of your own knowledge and skills. You should use AI to support your learning, not to do all your work for you. By developing your own abilities and thinking carefully about things made by AI, you can use it wisely without losing your own skills.

opts: Someone may use AI to fool or cheat you.
However, AI also brings some hidden risks.
And please remember not to depend too much on AI.
So you can’t just believe or copy everything AI provides.
Don’t share anything with AI that you wouldn’t post on social media.

16.why: 前面讲 AI 很有用，B「然而 AI 也有隐藏的风险」，所以要学会安全使用。

17.why: 不要把个人信息告诉 AI，好办法是 E「不会发到网上的东西，也别告诉 AI」。

18.why: AI 会出错，D「所以不能完全相信、照抄 AI 给的东西」。

19.ev: They can use AI to create fake voices or photos that sound or look like people you trust.

articles.title: Have you ever heard of the saying “Don’t judge a book by its cover”?
body: Have you ever heard of the saying “Don’t judge a book by its cover”? Well, in Chinese, we often say “Don’t judge people by their looks”.
Imagine you meet someone new at school. They might look different from you in hair, clothes or looks.     16
Sometimes, people make a mistake by judging others by their looks. They might think someone is mean (刻薄的) or unfriendly just because they have a serious face or wear unusual clothes.     17
In real life, people are like books with many pages.     18     That means talking with them, learning about their interests and personalities and getting to know them.
Think about your best friends. When you met them for the first time, you might not have known they would become your best friends.     19

Don’t judge people by their looks, and open our hearts to new people in our lives. We start to understand and treasure the differences between us, like different cultures, different backgrounds and different ways of thinking.

So, let’s keep an open mind and be nice to everyone we meet.     20     When we do so, we make a big difference to the world, and we make a world where everyone feels important and accepted. After all, the most amazing things are hidden. They are in each one of us!

articles.title: When Leo was in primary school, he didn’t think he was good
body: When Leo was in primary school, he didn’t think he was good at anything. In class, other children read and answered fast. Leo often stayed quiet. He felt a little sad.

But Leo had one special hobby: maps. He liked looking at roads, rivers, and bridges. At home, he sat with his grandpa and looked at an old city map.          “Why do you always look at maps?” his mum said one day. “It’s boring.”
“It’s not boring,” Leo answered. “Maps help people find the right way.”
One Friday, Leo’s class took a trip to a science museum. He woke up early and ran to the school bus. On the bus, some students sang, while others talked about snacks.

After half an hour, the bus suddenly stopped. The driver stood up and said, “Children, the road ahead is closed. My phone map can’t work here. I don’t know which way to go. I may need to call someone.”        The students began to worry. “Will we be late?” one girl asked.
Leo looked out of the window. He saw a big road sign and a small bridge. He took a deep breath and said, “Sir, can I try to help?”

The driver looked at him. “Do you know the way?” Leo opened the paper map in his bag.“Grandpa gave it to me,” he said. He pointed to the sign. “If we turn left at this crossing, go over the bridge, and then turn right at the next traffic light, we can go to the museum from the back road.”

The driver nodded. “Let’s try.” The bus turned left. Soon, they were moving again. Ten minutes later, they could see the museum gate.“You did it,” a boy shouted. “Leo is amazing,” another student said.
Leo smiled. His face felt warm. At that moment, he understood something important—he really could do something well: he could help people find the way.

opts: Because he couldn’t read or answer questions quickly.

ex.why: 别的孩子读得快、答得快，他总不说话，所以有点难过。

opts: He learned it from his mother.

ex.why: 他喜欢看地图上的道路、河流和桥梁。觉得无聊的是妈妈。

opts: Leo would give up looking at maps.

ex.why: 他发现自己真的能做好一件事，变得更自信了。

articles.title: When I was young, all I wanted to be was an artist.
body: When I was young, all I wanted to be was an artist. When I got to high school and could choose what classes to take, I took every art class that was open to me. Painting, drawing, photography — I took every class available.

Then I took a chemistry class. I LOVED it. It was fun, and I was good at it. I started thinking: Maybe I can get a better job in science? Maybe it’s hard to make money as an artist? So, I threw away the art school applications and went to study chemistry in college, not art.

College was fun, and when I graduated with my chemistry degree, I went to a graduate school in Washington D. C. to do a PhD program in chemistry. It was OK to start with, but after the first year, I was terribly sad. I hated the program. It was dry and boring. But I didn’t know what to do about it. So I quit.

I spent the next month feeling bad about my failure, unsure what to do next. Finally, I went to a job center to find work — any work that would pay money. I got a temporary (临时的) job filling envelopes at an NGO (非政府组织). One day, they needed some graphic design (平面设计), and I volunteered. This was the most important turning point in my career.

Over the next few months, they gave me more and more design work. What began as a temporary (临时的) job turned into a permanent (长期的) one. I was finally doing something I loved, and I was making money doing it. It’s been difficult at times, but I really love my job.
Believe me, it is FAR more important that you are happy and get to do what you enjoy every day and get paid less for it, than to get up unwillingly in the morning because you dislike what you do.

articles.title: Mind maps are visual (可视的) tools that help organize informat
body: Mind maps are visual (可视的) tools that help organize information by using a central topic and branches (分支). Mind mapping creates something clear and useful by connecting a main idea with details, pictures, and colors.    16     There are two main kinds of mind maps. Study-based maps help with learning, like understanding a history lesson.     17     Study maps are often made during learning, while life maps are usually made before an activity.

18     Just remember these basics: write the main idea in the middle, use thick lines for key points, and thin lines for details. Simple drawings like a book or a sun can be added, but what matters is the structure (结构), not how beautiful it looks.
19     Any paper will do — even a small piece is good for beginners. Colored pens help separate ideas and make the map more lively and clear.

Mind mapping has many benefits. It helps you focus on important points, organize notes clearly, and remember information longer. It also makes learning more fun and improves your thinking skills.     20     Why not try making one today? You can find free courses online to help you get started.

opts: All you need to start is paper and colored pens.
What’s more, it’s easy to share your mind map with others.
You don’t need to be good at drawing to make a mind map.
Life-based maps are used for planning daily activities, such as a family trip.
They work together to help you understand and remember information better.

16.why: 把主题和细节、图画、颜色连起来，E「它们一起帮你更好地理解和记忆」。

17.ev: Study-based maps help with learning, like understanding a history lesson.
17.why: 两种思维导图：学习类帮助学习，D「生活类用来计划日常活动，比如家庭旅行」。

18.why: 这一段说重要的是结构，不是画得美，开头 C「画思维导图不需要会画画」。

19.ev: Any paper will do — even a small piece is good for beginners. Colored pens help separate ideas
19.why: 后面讲纸和彩笔，前面应是 A「开始只需要纸和彩笔」。

20.ev: It also makes learning more fun and improves your thinking skills.
20.why: 列举好处，B「另外，思维导图很容易分享给别人」，What’s more 继续补充。
