articles.title: Asking for advice can be scary?
body: Asking for advice can be scary? In a recent study, 74 percent said they were afraid to ask for advice. But people who ask for advice are easier to succeed at a task.     16     Here are a few tips.

Look for the best person to give you advice. It might be easy to ask all people around you for advice at once, but will you value all of their advice? Probably not. It might be better to choose one or two people whose opinions you value the most.     17
Think about when to ask.     18     If what you are asking needs a lot of thought, you should ask people when they are free and clear-headed.

Be specific (具体的) in your questioning.       19     Do you ask a business owner, “What advice do you have for me?” No, because it’s not specific enough. Instead, try asking, “What college classes did you find helpful for starting a business?”
20     If you can’t solve your problem by following the first person’s advice, why not ask someone else who may have a different opinion?
Remember, the key is: Don’t be afraid to ask for advice.

opts: Ask somebody for a second opinion.
Finding the right time to ask for advice is important.
So how do you ask for advice?
Imagine you want to own a business someday.
You can ask for advice from people who have experience in the topic.

body: Summary writing (摘要写作) is a really valuable skill, but it can be difficult to learn. If you are ESL learners (第二语言学习者), you may not understand the purpose of writing summaries, or have difficulty in expressing yourself in a short way.     36
Understand what a summary is.
It gives only main points, not the details (细节).     37     And you can’t express your own opinions.
Read a short story or an essay (散文).
Choose a short passage that won’t take a long time to read.     38     Make sure the short passage is easy to understand so that you won’t get confused (困惑的) when you write your summary.

As you read, it is a good way to underline any important information that helps describe the passage as a whole. Look for the key information that can answer the questions of who, what, when, where, why and how.
Try to write a summary in your own words.
40     Write the main point of each part using the key information you just underlined. Your summary should include the basic information without unnecessary details.

articles.title: There was a boy who had a great collection of marbles (弹珠) a
body: There was a boy who had a great collection of marbles (弹珠) and a girl with a big collection of sweets. They were friends for many years and always shared many good things and secrets together.
On a sunny day, they played together outdoors. The girl wanted to play with the marbles. And because the boy wouldn’t share the marbles, the girl didn’t share her sweets with the boy.
After thinking for a long time, they finally agreed to make a deal: The boy would give the girl all his marbles, and the girl would give him all her sweets.

On the night before they were to make the exchange (交换), the boy went through his marbles to put them in a bag. He found a marble which was so beautiful that he decided to hide it under his bed. He packed the rest of his marbles into a bag to give them to the girl. The girl also went through her sweets and put them all into a bag for the next day.
Finally, the day of the exchange came. The girl gave the boy the bag with all of her sweets and the boy gave the girl his bag of marbles without the one he had hidden under his bed.

That night, the girl went to sleep, happy and peaceful, as she now had a beautiful collection of marbles. But the boy looked at his collection of sweets and wondered if the girl had given him all her sweets or if she hid the very best sweet under her bed just as he had done.
Thinking of it, the boy could not get to sleep, as he was troubled by the thought of his deception.

qs.stem: What happened when the girl and the boy played together outdoors?
opts: The boy stole some candies from the girl.
The boy didn’t want to play with the girl anymore.

ex.ev: And because the boy wouldn’t share the marbles, the girl didn’t share her sweets with the boy.
ex.why: 男孩不肯分享弹珠，女孩也不分享糖——他们的友谊出了点小问题。

qs.stem: What deal did the boy and the girl make?
opts: The boy gave up playing marbles.
The boy used the most beautiful marble to exchange the girl’s candies.
The girl could keep her favorite sweet.

ex.ev: The boy would give the girl all his marbles, and the girl would give him all her sweets.
ex.why: 约定：男孩把弹珠全给女孩，女孩把糖全给男孩——互相交换。

qs.stem: Why couldn’t the boy get to sleep in the end?
opts: He regretted giving his marbles to the girl.
He didn’t like sweets at all.
He doubted the girl didn’t give him all the sweets.
He was too excited to sleep.

ex.ev: But the boy looked at his collection of sweets and wondered if the girl had given him all her sweets
ex.why: 他怀疑女孩也像他一样藏了一块最好的糖，所以睡不着。

qs.stem: Which one has the similar meaning with the underlined word “deception”?

ex.ev: He found a marble which was so beautiful that he decided to hide it under his bed.
ex.why: 他偷偷藏了一颗弹珠骗了女孩——deception 是「欺骗」，和说谎意思相近。

qs.stem: What can we know from the text?
opts: No man can do two things at once.
He is wise that is honest.
Nothing is difficult to the man who will try.

ex.ev: That night, the girl went to sleep, happy and peaceful,
ex.why: 诚实的女孩睡得安稳，不诚实的男孩睡不着——诚实的人才是聪明的。

articles.src: 2025年洛阳市第三次中招模拟考试
articles.title: Have you ever thought that you were not good at studying?
body: Have you ever thought that you were not good at studying? In fact, this is usually because you don’t know some useful learning methods well, nor can you put them to use. The following might be of some help to you.

*The Feynman Learning Method* The Feynman learning method was developed by Richard Feynman, a Nobel Prize winner. It’s very good for both learning something new and helping you study for an exam. It has four steps. First, you pretend (假装) to teach a kid about the topic you want to learn, writing down what you know simply. Second, find the parts you don’t understand and go back to study. Third, simplify your notes. Fourth, if possible, teach others. Once you can explain an idea in simple language, you have deeply understood it and will remember it for a long time.

*The Pomodoro Method* The Pomodoro method can help you produce work of higher grade in a shorter amount of time. If you often have trouble getting something done on time or making good use of your time, try it. Here’s how to practice the Pomodoro method:  ●Choose your task. ●Set a 25-minute timer. ●Work on the task until the timer goes off. ●Take a 5-minute break. ●Repeat. ●Take a longer 15-30-minute break every 4 Pomodoro periods.

*The Simon Learning Method* The Simon learning method was created by Herbert Simon, a Nobel Prize winner. It says if you can focus on your studies for six months and manage to study 40 hours a week, you can master almost any field of knowledge. Yes, you heard it right. Any field of knowledge. Its steps are as follows. First, pick a subject. Then, break it into small parts. Next, focus on studying these parts all the time for six months. This way, you can finally master the whole subject.

qs.stem: Which group of people is most likely to be interested in this text?

ex.ev: Have you ever thought that you were not good at studying?
ex.why: 讲学习方法，是写给学生的。

ex.why: 只有费曼学习法明确说分四步；西蒙学习法是三步，番茄法列了更多步骤。

qs.stem: Which of the following is needed in the Pomodoro Method?

ex.ev: ●Set a 25-minute timer.
ex.why: 番茄工作法要定 25 分钟的计时器，D 图是计时器（秒表）。

qs.stem: Which method can you use if you have a nearly half-year-long vacation?

ex.ev: It says if you can focus on your studies for six months and manage to study 40 hours a week,
ex.why: 西蒙学习法要专心学六个月，正适合近半年的假期。

ex.ev: The following might be of some help to you.
ex.why: 介绍学习方法，属于杂志的「学习」栏目。

articles.title: Tiegan always liked to sing loudly.
body: [图:reading/8773bfa9/image5.png]

Tiegan always liked to sing loudly. Sometimes, though, Tiegan’s family liked the house to be quiet. Mom liked to go through some newspapers and magazines, and Dad liked to watch the news on TV each night, “It’s quiet time, Tiegan,” they would say. Then Tiegan had to find something else to do. She had plenty of board games, but she didn’t like them as much as singing,

One summer day, Tiegan was singing her favorite songs in the living room. Dad came downstairs and said, “Tiegan, I have a headache. Can you go outside and play? I really need it to be quiet so I can sleep.”

Tiegan breathed out heavily and went outside. It was a sunny day, and many people were outside. She sat on the sidewalk and looked around. Then she started to sing softly. She was careful to be quiet at first, but soon she began to sing loudly.
The sun was very warm, and Tiegan took off her baseball cap. Now she could feel a cool soft wind across her forehead (前额), which felt nice. She dropped her hat on the sidewalk and kept singing.
Just as Tiegan finished one of her favorite songs, a man with a small dog stopped in front of her, “That was a beautiful song,” he said. And he dropped a dollar into her hat.
Before Tiegan could say anything, the man walked away with his dogs.

Tiegan wasn’t sure what to do with the dollar, but she did want to keep singing. As she started her next song, Mrs. Maudslay—Tiegan’s neighbor came out of her house. “Are you starting a new job, Tiegan?”
“What do you mean?” asked Tiegan. “I’m just playing and singing.”
“Oh,” said Mrs. Maudslay. “I thought maybe you were busking, since you have your hat out.”
“What’s busking?” asked Tiegan.
Mrs. Maudslay laughed quietly. “______ People like to drop in a dollar or two to show that they liked the show.”

Tiegan hadn’t meant to start a new job, but since her hat was already out, she decided to keep singing. Soon enough, people walked past and stopped to listen. When they were ready to move on, they dropped some money into her hat.
By the end of the afternoon, Tiegan’s hat was full. Singing didn’t feel like working, but she surprisingly had made enough money from it.

ex.ev: Tiegan always liked to sing loudly.
ex.why: 她最喜欢大声唱歌，比玩桌游还喜欢。

qs.stem: How did Tiegan feel when her dad asked her to go outside?

ex.ev: Tiegan breathed out heavily and went outside.
ex.why: 爸爸让她出去，她重重地叹了口气——不高兴。

qs.stem: What’s the correct order according to the text? a．Tiegan dropped her hat on the sidewalk. b．Tiegan sat on the sidewalk and looked around. c．Mrs. Maudslay had a conversation with Tiegan. d．A man walked away with his dog after dropping a dollar.

ex.ev: She sat on the sidewalk and looked around.
ex.why: 顺序：坐在人行道上看看四周（b）→ 把帽子放在地上（a）→ 男人放下一美元后走开（d）→ 邻居和她说话（c）。

opts: Busking is when someone sing for fun with neighbors.
Busking is when a street performer collects hats as a hobby.
Busking is when someone is so surprised and has nothing to say.
Busking is when a street performer puts out a hat to collect money.

opts: Hobbies can sometimes bring pleasant surprises.
Street performing is the easiest way to make money.

Singing is the best way to make both yourself and others happy.

ex.why: 她只是在唱自己喜欢的歌，却意外赚了一帽子钱——爱好有时会带来惊喜。

articles.title: There must be such people in our life who want to do importa
body: There must be such people in our life who want to do important work or make meaningful achievements, but they aren’t that smart and don’t have any talent. How should they go about doing things?     16
◆Do the boring things.

There will always be boring work to do.     17     This is an especially good area to work if you aren’t so smart or talented because people will show you more patience to help you get up to a certain skill level, because they don’t want to do it themselves.
◆Learn new skills.

18     A really good example of this is learning to code (编程) with AI. For example, most people don’t exactly know how to use AI to solve real problems, especially if they don’t know how to code. So it’s a great chance for you to shine.
◆Figure out the first step.

Most people can achieve more than they think they can do, but they are often afraid of ideas and just “don’t know where to start”.     19     Learn how to work out the opening step of any idea and get the ball rolling.
◆Ask your stupid questions.

If you aren’t that smart or talented, you will find that you will have a lot of “stupid” questions, that’s okay.     20     More importantly, sometimes, you will bring some questions that other people have but are too afraid to ask because of the fear of being seen as not smart or talented. Sometimes the emperor has no clothes, so don’t be afraid to say something! Ask them!

articles.title: Charlotte dreams of becoming a dancer.
body: Charlotte dreams of becoming a dancer. She studies dance at a private dance school. The dance classroom is big and bright, but these days, Charlotte is really worried.

In every class, she can’t keep her mind on her dance. Some classmates do the dance moves wrong, and the teacher has to correct them often. Others talk loudly during breaks and always complain (抱怨) that the training is too hard. This makes Charlotte so upset that her dancing stops improving.

One day, she works up the courage to tell her teacher, “I don’t want to dance anymore.” The teacher looks very surprised. She stops what she is doing and asks kindly, “Charlotte, can you tell me why?” Charlotte tells the teacher all her problems. She says, “During the class, some students do the movements wrong and some are always chatting. I just can’t focus, and I feel like I can’t dance well either.”

The teacher thinks for a while. Then she gives Charlotte a balance pole (平衡杆) and asks her to dance the dance they learned last week, keeping the pole from falling. Charlotte takes a deep breath, holds the pole in her hand, and starts dancing. She focuses on every step, turn, and jump. When she finishes, the pole is still in her hand.

The teacher walks up and asks with a smile, “When you were dancing, did you notice that some classmates had wrong movements? Did you hear anyone chatting?” Charlotte shakes her head and says, “I was only thinking about keeping this pole balanced and didn’t notice anything else at all.”

The teacher says seriously, “Charlotte, practicing dance is like dancing with a balance pole. You need to focus on your own movements and how you show your feelings. As long as you put your whole heart into it, you won’t be troubled by other people’s mistakes or laziness. When you are following your dream, focus and perseverance (毅力) can help you get through all the difficulties.”

Charlotte seems to understand. From then on, during every class, she focuses on her own dance. She is no longer worried, and her dancing gets better day by day. The light in her eyes comes back again.

opts: She was too tired at the dancing class.
She couldn’t focus because of others’ mistakes and chatting.
The training was too hard and expensive.

Discussing with the classmates during the dance class.

ex.why: 故事讲专注了就会进步——Focus and improve。

articles.title: In this fast-paced life, it’s hard to find the time to cook.
body: In this fast-paced life, it’s hard to find the time to cook. But cooking for other people can be fun and beneficial because it comes with some positive psychological (心理的) benefits.
Performing an act for another human being, like cooking for them, is a form of selflessness. And it can make people feel happy and connected to others.
Cooking is a form of nurturing (养育).
When it comes to cooking, you are feeding someone, which is necessary for survival. Cooking for others is nurturing.     37    .
Cooking can create bonds (联系).

If you’re cooking for someone, even if they’re not present during the act, it can bring a sense of closeness because you’re expressing your love and care for someone.     38    . And cooking for others helps us build and strengthen those connections
Not only does cooking for yourself help you eat more healthily but it also sends yourself a message that you are important. Cooking can also help raise your confidence.
Cooking is a practice of mindfulness.
Cooking can encourage us to really focus.     40    : walk away for a minute and you can burn the onions; check in with your phone and your water can overflow.

Cooking brings us together, and it continues to create communities—and with community come feelings of connection and happiness. Now all you have to do is find the time to add cooking into your busy life.

articles.title: “Why did she spill the beans?
body: “Why did she spill the beans?” I thought regretfully (惋惜地). I’ll always remember that day, when I was so surprised by all the strange looks people gave me. I couldn’t believe I had lost the friendship of the person I trusted the most.

Five years back, Sally was the new kid in class. I don’t know what it was, but something unique about her drew me to her. After a few months, we were best friends. I never expected her to hurt me so much.

Sally was the most friendly person I knew. Maybe that’s why I told her about my personal life. She then told everyone at school, exaggerating (夸大) the matter and adding her own spin (倾向性描述) on it. It was like someone had stabbed (刺) me in the back. After she gave away my secrets, people started laughing at me. They looked at me and giggled (咯咯地笑) whenever I passed by. To avoid embarrassment, I changed schools. Sally called me many times, but I didn’t want to talk to her.

I tried hard to heal from the scars (伤疤) she left on my heart. After five years, my life went back to the way it was, with new friends. Then one day, I ran into Anna at the market. She was my classmate from Grade 3. She told me that Sally wasn’t the one who brought my secrets to light. Mary was. Mary was our school’s big mouth who always wanted to stick her nose into other people’s business.

I was all at sea (不知所措). I wished I could have asked Sally about this. I wished I could go back in time and fix my mistakes. From that, I learned a life lesson—we should be open to honest communication before jumping to conclusions, because even one little mistake could really damage (破坏) our friendships.

opts: Sally saw something special in her.
She liked Sally’s sense of humor.
She wanted to help Sally fit in.

ex.why: Sally 是她认识的最友好的人，所以她才说了自己的私事。

ex.why: spill the beans 就是后文的 gave away my secrets——泄露秘密。

qs.stem: What did the author do after her secrets were given away?
opts: She called Sally to ask why.
She told Sally’s secrets to others.
She dropped out to work at a market.

ex.ev: To avoid embarrassment, I changed schools.
ex.why: 为了避免尴尬，她转学了。

qs.stem: How did the author feel after she found out the truth?

ex.ev: I wished I could go back in time and fix my mistakes.
ex.why: 知道真相后希望能回到过去弥补错误——后悔。

qs.stem: What life lesson did the author learn from the experience?
opts: Keeping others’ secrets is not easy.
It’s better to make decisions quickly.

ex.why: 下结论前要坦诚沟通——友谊里沟通很重要。

articles.src: 2025年许昌市中招二模
articles.title: William used to be a kid who never dared to express his true
body: William used to be a kid who never dared to express his true thoughts. He always agreed with everything his friends said.

One day, he and his friends were discussing whether middle school students should bring their phones to school. His friends all thought they should, but William didn’t agree. However, because he didn’t have the courage to speak out his mind, he chose to agree with them. But he knew that always going against his own will to agree with others made him feel very uncomfortable. So he told his mom about this.
“I just can’t tell people what I really think or want. It’s too difficult for me,” said William.
“You can’t or you don’t want to?” Mom asked patiently.
“I guess I don’t want to. I’m afraid to be different,” answered William.

His mom smiled and handed him a famous book, The Analects of Confucius (《论语》). William knew the book but he didn’t know what his mom meant. However, he started reading the book every night before bed. One day, he read the phrase, “Gentlemen have peace but disagree; flunkies (小人) agree but have no peace.” He didn’t understand it, so he asked his mom.

“It means gentlemen achieve harmony (和谐), but they don’t just blindly agree with others. They have their own ideas, and they can tell the truth bravely. Flunkies agree easily, but they don’t really work together,” his mom explained.

Suddenly, William was inspired and realized that having different ideas was not a bad thing at all. He was very thankful for the book. He decided to be brave enough to express his own thoughts. He did as he said. From then on, he was no longer afraid to speak out his mind. To his surprise, he found that the friendship had become even stronger!

qs.stem: What did William use to be like?
opts: He always expressed his true thoughts bravely.
He was afraid to express his own ideas and always agreed with others.
He often argued with his friends about different ideas.
He didn’t care about others’ opinions at all.

ex.ev: He always agreed with everything his friends said.
ex.why: 他以前不敢说真实想法，朋友说什么都同意。

qs.stem: Why did William feel uncomfortable?
opts: Because his friends didn’t listen to him.
Because he had a fight with his friends.
Because he always went against his own will to agree with others.

ex.ev: But he knew that always going against his own will to agree with others made him feel very uncomfortable.
ex.why: 总是违背自己的意愿去附和别人，让他很难受。

qs.stem: Which of the following can best describe William’s mom?

ex.ev: Mom asked patiently.
ex.why: 妈妈耐心地问，又用《论语》引导他自己想明白——耐心又有智慧。

qs.stem: What is the meaning of the underlined sentence in the passage?
opts: 君子坦荡荡，小人长戚戚。
君子周而不比，小人比而不周。
君子和而不同，小人同而不和。
君子喻于义，小人喻于利。

ex.ev: It means gentlemen achieve harmony (和谐), but they don’t just blindly agree with others.
ex.why: 君子和谐相处但不盲目附和——君子和而不同，小人同而不和。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the story?
opts: Having different ideas is bad for friendship.

ex.ev: He decided to be brave enough to express his own thoughts.
ex.why: 他学会勇敢说出想法，友谊反而更好——表达真实想法很有必要。

cand: adj. 身体不舒服的；不舒适的

articles.src: 2025年许昌市中招二模
articles.title: Words to Describe Your School There must be something that y
body: Words to Describe Your School
There must be something that you love about your school, whether it is the environment, culture, daily life, or the teachers.
When you are talking about your school, the words to describe it will send a message about how you feel.     36
Here is the list of the words you can choose to describe your school.
Clean

In a clean school environment, the walls are free of graffiti (涂鸦). The floors are cleaned daily.     37     Even the bathroom smells fresh because it is cleaned so well. This is a good word to use when the school is clean because cleanliness helps students to live and study better.
Modern

A modern school environment is one with the latest equipment (最新设备). It helps students to learn through activities in clubs such as science clubs, robot clubs and computer clubs.     38     All these help students learn about new science and technology.
Safe

39     The school always has a team to protect students from dangers. This is a good word to describe your school. With a safe environment, students can focus on their studies without worrying about getting hurt, and they feel comfortable and relaxed every day at school.
Hardworking

A hardworking school is a place in which students are encouraged to give their best in whatever they do and never give up.     40     You have no choice but to try and keep up with others. This is a good word to use when you always have something to do.
This list will help you to pick the right word for your situation.

opts: There is no rubbish under the desks.
Teachers never allow you to be lazy.
For this reason, you have to choose them carefully.
It provides students with modern classrooms and laboratories.
Such a school environment means a danger-free (无危险的) area.

articles.title: Li Qingzhao was one of the best-known women writers in Chine
body: [图:reading/6b6b0cb9/image9.png]
Li Qingzhao was one of the best-known women writers in Chinese history.     16     However, her life was hard but sweet.

Li was born into a literary (文学的) family in 1084. Her father collected a lot of books.     17     Her early poems showed her innocence (单纯), good mind and love of nature. Li was someone who always wanted to destroy old customs from the start. Many people like her writing style.     18

She was lucky in her marriage. In 1101, Li married Zhao Mingcheng, and she shared interests in many ways with him.     19     They shared a love of poetry and often wrote poems for each other. They collected many books. They even sold clothes and went hungry to build up a big library.

This happy life ended because of war.     20     The couple took many of their books and ran away to Nanjing, where they lived for a year. Zhao Mingcheng died in 1129, leaving her alone. Later, he arrived at Hangzhou in 1132, where she died in 1155.
Li Qingzhao’s life was tough, but she left many valuable poems to the world. 请你

opts: They were not rich, but they lived happily together.
She was a very famous poet just at the age of seventeen.
The fight took place in Shandong and their house was burned.
And she was able to receive a good education in her childhood.
She showed great love for writing and was known as a special woman then.

16.ev: Li Qingzhao was one of the best-known women writers in Chinese history.
16.why: 介绍她是著名女作家，E「她热爱写作，在当时就被认为是一位特别的女子」。

17.ev: Her father collected a lot of books.
17.why: 出身文学家庭、父亲藏书多，D「所以她小时候能受到良好教育」。

18.ev: Many people like her writing style.
18.why: 讲她早年的诗，B「她十七岁就是很有名的诗人了」。

19.ev: They shared a love of poetry and often wrote poems for each other.
19.why: 婚姻幸福，A「他们不富有，但生活得很幸福」，后面还卖衣服、挨饿买书。

20.ev: This happy life ended because of war.
20.why: 因为战争幸福生活结束，C「战争在山东发生，他们的房子被烧」。

articles.src: 2025年濮阳市中招第二次模拟
articles.title: Little George lived in a poor village.
body: Little George lived in a poor village. One summer day George’s mother sent him to the field to pick up some dry wood for the fire.

George looked very hard. By the time the sun was high, he was very hot and wished for a cool place to rest and have some food. As he walked along, he found some shade, and by it were some fine, wild strawberries.

“How good these will be with my bread and butter,” thought George. He picked up all of the strawberries. As he was lifting the first strawberry to his mouth, he remembered his sick mother, alone in her dark, cold room in the village.
With this in mind, he put the strawberry back again. “Shall I save them for her?” he asked himself. He thought how refreshing they would be for her, yet was still looking at them with a longing eye.

“I will eat half, and take the other half to her,” he said. He divided them into two heaps (堆), but each heap looked so small. He put them together again. “I will only eat one,” he thought. But, as he again lifted it to his mouth, he saw that he had taken the best, and he put it back. When the sun was beginning to sink (下沉), George set out for home. How happy he felt that he had all his strawberries for his sick mother.

He heard his mother’s weak voice calling him. “Is that you, George? I am glad you have come back. I am thirsty, and am longing for some tea.” George ran to her and joyfully offered his wild strawberries. “And you saved them for me, didn’t you?” said she, laying her hand fondly (怜爱地) on his head, with tears in her eyes. Is the joy of eating strawberries half as much as the happiness George felt at this moment?

qs.stem: Why did George go to the field?
opts: To look for some wood for the fire.
To eat his bread and butter.
To find some fruits to eat.

ex.ev: George’s mother sent him to the field to pick up some dry wood for the fire.
ex.why: 妈妈让他去田里捡柴火。

qs.stem: What does the underlined phrase “with a longing eye” in Paragraph 4 show about George?
opts: He wanted to find more strawberries.
He felt that the sunlight was too strong.
He thought the strawberries were good for his mom.
He wanted to eat the strawberries very much.

ex.ev: He thought how refreshing they would be for her, yet was still looking at them with a longing eye.
ex.why: 想留给妈妈，却还是眼巴巴地看着——他很想吃。

qs.stem: Why did George put down the strawberry the second time he lifted it to his mouth?
opts: Because he wanted to eat other strawberries.
Because it was the best one.

ex.ev: he saw that he had taken the best, and he put it back.
ex.why: 他发现拿的是最好的那颗，就放回去了。

qs.stem: How did George’s mom feel after seeing the strawberries?

ex.ev: with tears in her eyes
ex.why: 妈妈含着泪摸他的头——被感动了。

qs.stem: What lesson can be learned from George’s actions in the story?
opts: It’s better to put yourself first.
Keep all the good things for your mom.

ex.ev: How happy he felt that he had all his strawberries for his sick mother.
ex.why: 把草莓全留给生病的妈妈，他觉得很幸福——分享就是关爱。

cand: v. 使恢复精神；使清爽
adj. 喜悦的；令人高兴的

articles.src: 2025年濮阳市中招第二次模拟
articles.title: What’s your dream in the near future?
body: What’s your dream in the near future? How do you plan to achieve it?

We all have dreams, each special in its own way. Sometimes, they feel like gentle nudges (唠叨).     36     It may sound sad, but many people mix up wishing, wanting and dreaming with actually working towards their goals. This mix-up often stops them from achieving what they really want in life.
37     Write them down.

You might think, “Can writing down my goals really make them happen?” The truth is that it won’t actually make them real, but it’s a powerful first step.     38     This practice sets you on the path to progress and success.

Also, writing down your goals comes with many other benefits (好处). To start with, when you write down what you want to achieve, it helps you keep going in the right direction and take responsibility for your goals. It’s like giving yourself a mission that encourages you to work towards your dreams.     39     It’s simpler to recall what you’ve written compared to just thinking about it. Believe it or not, writing down your goals can even help you stay focused on what you want to achieve. The more focused you are, the better your chances of reaching your goal.

Every great journey begins with a single step—and your pen is the compass for this adventure. When dreams take shape on paper, they transform from fleeting (短暂的) thoughts into living promises to yourself.     40     And your future self will thank you.

opts: Writing your goals down also helps you remember them better.
While other times, they completely take over our mind.
It turns your vague (模糊的) dreams into real aims.
So, grab a pen and start writing down your dreams.
There’s a simple way to make your goals come true.

36.ev: Sometimes, they feel like gentle nudges (唠叨).
36.why: Sometimes 对应 B 里的 other times：「而有时它们会完全占据我们的头脑」。

37.ev: Write them down.
37.why: E「有一个简单的方法让目标成真」，接着说：写下来。

38.ev: This practice sets you on the path to progress and success.
38.why: 写下来不能让目标直接实现，但 C「它把模糊的梦想变成真正的目标」。

39.ev: It’s simpler to recall what you’ve written compared to just thinking about it.
39.why: 后面说写下来的更容易回想，A「写下目标也能帮你记得更牢」。

40.ev: And your future self will thank you.
40.why: 结尾号召 D「所以拿起笔，写下你的梦想吧」。

cand: adj. 真实的；实际存在的

articles.src: 2025年南阳市重点初中联考中考二模
articles.title: As a child, I was very shy.
body: As a child, I was very shy. Almost everyone around me except my parents made me nervous. But then one day, it changed.

On that day, we took the school bus to school in the morning. The school bus was very crowded and hot. But we couldn’t open the windows. It was simply raining too hard. I sat alone as usual, speaking to no one. Over and over, I carefully cleaned a small circle on my window so that I could see the rain outside.

The bus stopped, waiting for the traffic light. I saw a small dog cross the street. He was all wet and didn’t seem to know where to go. Passing cars would kill him. I wanted to help the dog, but I knew the bus driver Mr Smith wouldn’t let me get off the bus. I thought that if I pointed out the poor dog, the other children would probably laugh at me.

I felt very sad. The bus began to move forward. I still couldn’t take my eyes off this little dog. He was begging for help. I looked around, but nobody else seemed to have noticed it. Suddenly, I stood up and cried, “Mr. Smith! A poor dog outside! If we don’t help him, he’ll die! ”
To my surprise, Mr. Smith wasn’t angry and didn’t shout at me. The other children didn’t laugh at me. The bus slowly stopped. Mr. Smith said, “Children don’t leave this bus.”...

qs.stem: Why didn’t the children open the windows of the school bus?

ex.ev: It was simply raining too hard.
ex.why: 雨下得太大，没法开窗。

qs.stem: What made the little dog in danger?

ex.ev: Passing cars would kill him.
ex.why: 过往的汽车会撞死它。

qs.stem: How did the author feel about Mr. Smith’s actions?

ex.ev: To my surprise, Mr. Smith wasn’t angry and didn’t shout at me.
ex.why: To my surprise——司机没生气，作者很惊讶。

qs.stem: The author writes the text in the order of ________.

ex.why: 按时间顺序写：早上坐校车 → 等红灯时看见小狗 → 车开动后喊出来 → 车停下。

qs.stem: What would happen next in the text?
opts: The author got off and saved the little dog.
The little dog was killed at last.
Mr. Smith saved the little dog.

ex.ev: The bus slowly stopped.
ex.why: 司机停车，又让孩子们别下车——接下来应该是他自己下去救小狗。

articles.title: How to Be More Interesting No one is really boring, and no o
body: How to Be More Interesting

No one is really boring, and no one has to be perfect to be welcome among friends. But sometimes you may feel you are so boring and need to be more interesting.     36     If you want to make a change, you have come to the right place.

Many people want to leave a good impression on others, but they care too much about small things and forget how to be themselves. They are worrying about whether they are good enough, so they look nervous and unnatural.     37     Enjoy the present moment and don’t worry too much about the future.

Interesting people are usually kind and positive. This is one of the reasons why we find them so interesting. If you often look at the good side of life, you will bring warmth to people around you. They will love to share happiness and hope with you.     38

Some people are quiet and shy, so they seldom show their true feelings in front of others.     39     However, if you close your heart to the world, you will lose the chance to know more wonderful people and wonderful things. Being a little more open can make you more lively and interesting.

40     You can take up a new hobby, learn a new skill, or talk to someone you don’t know very well. People who never step out of their usual life may easily feel bored. By trying more new things, you will have more to share with others and become a more interesting person.

opts: It’s important to broaden your comfort zone.
After all, no one really wants to be around a negative, unhappy person.
Being an interesting person is something that can be learned and practiced.
Try to stay relaxed and flexible.
Many people feel they need to hold back to protect themselves.

36.why: 想变得有趣，C「有趣是可以学、可以练的」，接着说你来对地方了。

37.why: 前面说太在意小事显得紧张，D「尽量放松、灵活一些」。

38.ev: They will love to share happiness and hope with you.
38.why: 讲积极乐观，B「毕竟没人真想和消极、不开心的人在一起」。

39.ev: However, if you close your heart to the world, you will lose the chance to know more wonderful people and wonderful things.

articles.title: Schools are supposed to be safe places for children all the time.
body: Schools are supposed to be safe places for children all the time. Sadly, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (国际红十字委员会) has seen accidents happen in schools from time to time. For this reason, the ICRC began its education program in 2017. First-aid training in schools around the world is one of its plans.

Kate is a 16-year-old student who wants to become a doctor when she grows up. She lives in New York. In the spring of 2021, she took part in the ICRC’s first-aid training. During the process, one important lesson she learned was that in dangerous situations, everyone must take care of themselves first before helping others.

Since joining in the training, Kate has learned a lot of first-aid skills. She has been able to use them to stop the bleeding (流血) and deal with the wound herself. She once helped her friend who hurt his hand with broken glass. She even taught other students who could not take part in the training as well as her younger cousins some first-aid skills she learned.
“The training is important,” Kate said. “The teachers and students in our school used to know little about first aid. Now we can carry out some of the skills correctly in different situations.”
Thanks to the ICRC’s first-aid training, many students and teachers, like Kate, have become professional (专业的) first aiders. Their ability of protecting themselves has improved.

qs.stem: When did the ICRC begin its education program?

ex.ev: the ICRC began its education program in 2017.
ex.why: 2017 年开始教育项目。

qs.stem: What does Kate want to be when she grows up?

ex.ev: Kate is a 16-year-old student who wants to become a doctor when she grows up.
ex.why: Kate 长大想当医生。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “them” refer to in Paragraph 3?

ex.ev: Since joining in the training, Kate has learned a lot of first-aid skills.
ex.why: them 指前一句学到的急救技能。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the text?
opts: The ICRC hasn’t seen accidents in schools from time to time.
In 2020, Kate took part in the ICRC’s first-aid training.
Kate taught other students the first-aid skills she learned.
Kate’s family and friends thought the first-aid training wasn’t important.

ex.ev: She even taught other students who could not take part in the training as well as her younger cousins some first-aid skills she learned.
ex.why: 她还把学到的急救技能教给其他同学；B 错，她是 2021 年参加的。

qs.stem: What’s the best title for the text?
opts: The Experience of Learning First Aid

ex.why: 全文讲 Kate 参加急救培训、学会急救的经历。

articles.title: Many students always worry about their English learning.
body: Many students always worry about their English learning. Learning English well is not an easy task, but it is important for all the students.     16

Improve your listening skills by exposing (暴露) yourself to English every day. You should listen to English songs, watch English movies or English programs, or listen to English news.     17     They can also help improve your listening and speaking skills.

Practice speaking English as much as possible. It can help you become more confident.     18     Mistakes are part of the learning process. You can talk with your classmates, join an English corner or even practice by speaking to yourself in English. Don’t be afraid of losing face or being laughed at. You needn’t care about those who laugh at your mistakes.     19     It helps you increase your vocabulary and understand sentence structures. When you read, you can learn new words and grammar structures naturally. You can start with simple storybooks, and then move on to English magazines or newspapers.
Don’t forget to practice your writing skills.     20     You can write about your daily life and your feelings. Writing regularly will help you organize your thoughts and improve your writing skills.
Remember, consistency (持续性) is the key. If you keep practicing every day, you will become a good English learner soon!

articles.src: 2026年新乡市九年级中考一模
articles.title: The summer before the ninth grade, my father took me on a sp
body: The summer before the ninth grade, my father took me on a special trip to a small village in Qinghai. After a long tiring day of traveling, we arrived at the quiet place. The air was fresh but thin, and there were no city lights — just wide and open fields.

That night, something amazing happened. As it grew dark, countless stars appeared, filling the sky. The Milky Way (银河) shone brightly, and I even saw a shooting star! I asked, “Dad, why does the sky look so different here? The stars seem much brighter.”

My father pushed up his glasses, which were shining with the starlight. “The stars are the same,” he explained. “It’s just that in the city, the lights and buildings block our view. Here, we can finally see how big the universe is.”

Lying on the soft grass, I suddenly felt very small. All my pride about getting good grades at school, all the times I had a fight with others, even when I refused to say sorry to my best friend last week — none of them seemed important under the huge sky. Some of these stars’ light has been traveling for hundreds of years just to reach us tonight. Compared with that, the problems I have are so small!

The next morning, I watched our hostess carefully. Though she walked slowly, she did everything with care and purpose. When I had trouble making a fire for breakfast, she didn’t get angry but showed me how to do it carefully until I got it right. Her patience taught me another lesson about being humble (谦逊的).

Now, whenever I start feeling too proud or disappointed about something, I remember that night under the stars. I think about how small I am in this huge universe, and how much there is to learn. The stars have been shining for billions of years, and I’m just beginning to understand things. This experience helps me stay humble and keeps me wanting to learn more every day.

opts: In a city with tall buildings.
In a small village in Qinghai.

ex.why: 爸爸带他去了青海的一个小村子。

qs.stem: What did the writer think of his past problems under the huge sky?
opts: They were still very important to him.
He was proud of getting good grades at school.
He felt sorry for refusing to say sorry to his friend.
None of them seemed important compared to the universe.

ex.ev: none of them seemed important under the huge sky.
ex.why: 在广阔的星空下，这些事都不重要了。

qs.stem: Which words can best describe the hostess?

ex.ev: she didn’t get angry but showed me how to do it carefully until I got it right.
ex.why: 她不生气，一遍遍耐心教他生火——善良又耐心。

qs.stem: What does the underlined sentence in the last paragraph mean?
opts: Stars are older than the Earth.

ex.ev: The stars have been shining for billions of years, and I’m just beginning to understand things.
ex.why: 星星照耀了几十亿年，我才刚开始懂事——宇宙之大远超我们的认识。

articles.src: 2026年平顶山市中招学科第一次调研试卷 九年级
articles.title: Tom was known as the “forgetful boy” in his class.
body: [图:reading/8e926d67/image5.png]
Tom was known as the “forgetful boy” in his class. He often forgot his homework, his lunch, and sometimes even his own pencil case. His desk was always a mess, with papers everywhere.
One Tuesday morning, Mrs. Chen said with a smile, “Class, tomorrow we’re having a special guest-a scientist from the city museum. Please bring one interesting rock for a science activity.”
That night, Tom thought, “I must remember to find a rock!” He even wrote a note on his hand. But then his favorite TV show came on, and he forgot all about it.

The next morning, Tom walked into the classroom happily. Then he saw his classmates showing their rocks. Billy had a shiny white rock. Mary had one with stripes (条纹). Carol had a smooth gray stone from her garden. Tom’s heart sank. “Oh no! I forgot again!” He sat quietly at his desk, feeling terrible.
Just then, his best friend Mike came over.“Tom, do you have a rock?” Mike asked softly.
Tom shook his head sadly. He couldn’t look up.
Mike smiled warmly. He reached into his bag and pulled out a small, shiny rock. He placed it on Tom’s desk. “Here, take this one. I brought two—just in case.”
Tom’s eyes lit up. “Really? But it’s your rock!”
“We’re friends, right?” Mike said. “Friends help each other.”
During the activity, the scientist looked at Tom’s rock.“What an interesting rock!”she said.“This has some special minerals(矿物) inside.”
Tom smiled at Mike, and Mike smiled back. Tom didn’t say where the rock came from. He just enjoyed the moment.

From that day on, Tom tried harder to remember things. He put notes on his desk and asked his mom to remind him. But he never forgot what a true friend is like. Every time he saw a rock, he thought of Mike.

qs.stem: What problem did Tom have at the beginning?

ex.ev: He often forgot his homework, his lunch, and sometimes even his own pencil case.
ex.why: 他经常忘东西。

qs.stem: How did Tom feel when he saw his classmates’ rocks?

ex.ev: Tom’s heart sank.
ex.why: 心一沉，觉得很难受——情绪低落。

qs.stem: Why did Mike bring two rocks?
opts: He forgot he already had one.
He thought Tom might need one.

ex.ev: I brought two—just in case.
ex.why: 以防万一带了两块——想到 Tom 可能会需要。

qs.stem: Which part of the story is the climax (高潮)?
opts: Tom forgot to bring a rock.
Mike gave a rock to Tom.

ex.ev: He placed it on Tom’s desk.
ex.why: 高潮是故事最关键的转折：Tom 最难过时，Mike 递来一块石头。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the story?

articles.title: Have you ever wondered why your voice sounds different on a
body: [图:reading/8e926d67/image6.png]
Have you ever wondered why your voice sounds different on a recording? This common experience has a science fact behind it. It’s all about how sound moves to your ears.

When you speak, sound moves in two ways. First, it moves through the air to your ears. This is how other people hear your voice. Second, it moves through the bones in your head to your inner ears. This is called bone conduction (骨传导). The bones in your head shake as you speak. This makes your voice sound deeper and fuller to yourself.

But when you hear your voice on a recording, you’re only hearing the sound that moved through the air. The bone-conducted sound is not there. So your recorded voice sounds higher and, to you, a little strange.
This is why singers sometimes put one hand on their ear when they sing. They are trying to hear both the air sound and the bone sound. This helps them sing better.

This doesn’t just happen with voices. Think about when you eat hard foods like apples. You hear the crunching (咬碎) sound through your bones too. That’s why your own chewing (咀嚼) sounds much louder to you than to people sitting next to you. They only hear the sound through the air, while you get both air and bone sounds.

Scientists find that people usually don’t like their recorded voices at first. Why? Because they’ re not used to them. Your brain likes familiar sounds. The voice you hear through your bones is what you’ve heard your whole life. But after listening a few times, most people get used to it.
So next time you hear your recorded voice and think “That doesn’t sound like me!”, remember – it’s not a problem with your phone. It’s just science explaining how your body works!

body: The bestseller Steal Like an Artist by Austin Kleon is a fantastic guide for readers who want to get better at learning, creating, and finding their own voice. Its biggest message is powerful yet simple. You don’t have to invent something totally new to be creative.     36

This doesn’t mean copying others’ work. It means learning from people you admire.     37     You can take their best ideas and mix them into something that feels like yours. This idea is perfect for teenagers because it takes away the fear to be “perfectly original (原创的)”. Every great creator builds on what came before, and so can you. Actively learn from the best around you.

38     Start by keeping a notebook. You can take down cool sentences from books, clever problem-solving steps, or even ideas you love. Then, practice by imitating (模仿) first, and then create. Try using a model text’s mind map but fill it with your own experiences.     39     Learn from each other’s strengths, and don’t forget to share how you learned something, not just the final result. Small daily habits matter, too. Memorize one great sentence a day. Try one new study tip each week.     40
Steal Like an Artist reminds us that creativity isn’t about being unique (独特的). It’s about staying curious, learning bravely, and bringing out the best in you.

body: During the summer break, 14-year-old Wang Lin from Zhengzhou took part in a special activity — he became a volunteer guide at the Henan Museum. “I’ve always loved history, especially stories about the Bronze Age,” he said.

Every weekend, Wang Lin would stand in the museum’s “Treasures of Henan” hall, sharing stories about ancient artifacts (文物) with visitors. “My favorite is the ’Lotus and Crane Square Pot’,” he said. “It’s over 2,500 years old, and the shape is so beautiful. I tell people how it shows the creativity of ancient Chinese workers.”

One day, a visitor asked him, “You’re so young. How do you know all this?” Wang Lin replied, “I’ve been reading about Henan’s history since I was eight.” He then explained how a family trip to the Longmen Grottoes raised his interest. “I saw the huge statues and asked my dad a thousand questions. He bought me a book about Henan’s history, and I just couldn’t put it down.”
Now, Wang Lin hopes to study archaeology (考古学) in the future. “There’s still so much we don’t know about our past,” he said. “I want to help discover new stories.”
His mother said, “He used to be a shy boy. But now, he speaks confidently in front of strangers. I’m proud of him.”
When asked if he ever gets nervous, Wang Lin smiled. “Sometimes, but when I see people’s eyes light up because of what I’m saying, I feel really happy. Sharing history brings me joy.”

body: Recently in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, a video of a young girl performing the Pangu dance, an ancient dance dating back to the Han Dynasty, caught the attention of tens of thousands of netizens. According to the girl’s mother, Ms. Wang, her daughter Tongtong is now 10 years old. Tongtong began learning Chinese dance at the age of three and a half because of her born passion for dancing.

According to Ms. Wang, the Pangu dance dates back to the Han Dynasty and is an important part of Han culture. Dancers use drums as props (道具) placed on the ground, dressed in beautiful costumes. They leap (跳跃) and dance on the surface, showing their skillful movements.

“Because of her love for dancing, Tongtong has developed friendships with many dance lovers. They enjoy learning and sharing short dance videos on Douyin to document their growth. Inspired by this, Tongtong began learning and uploading (上传) dance videos on Douyin since November of last year,” Ms. Wang explained.

Ms. Wang mentioned that her daughter takes about half an hour each day to learn dance on Douyin after completing her homework. Besides, Tongtong attends three-hour dance classes twice a week. “She makes good use of her time in order to improve her performance. She also has excellent grades in her class,” Ms. Wang proudly added.

Tongtong expressed great joy after learning that many people like her dance video. “She is glad that her dance is being loved by everyone,” said Ms. Wang. “She wants to make more people know about the Pangu dance. She aims to further continue learning the ancient dances.”

articles.title: One noon, in the summer when I was five, my sister and I wer
body: One noon, in the summer when I was five, my sister and I were busy building a sand palace when two brightly colored lollipops（棒棒糖）suddenly appeared before us. We looked up in surprise and saw our elder cousin Michael smiling at us. “If you can do me a favor, these two will be yours”, he said. “Okay! Okay!” We couldn’t wait to eat them and agreed at once. As for what exactly he wanted us to do, we hardly paid attention. We only heard the words, “Just carry a black pot for me once”.

My sister and I sat under a tree, tasted the lollipops, and discussed where to find a “black pot” to carry on our backs. Suddenly, my sister said, “The kitchen! Mom’s cooking pot! They are black!” So I rushed into the kitchen, took a cooking pot, and put it onto my back. My sister copied me, threw another pot over her shoulder and carried it. Just like that, we walked out, ready to report our success to our elder cousin.

Suddenly, Mom’s sharp（尖锐的）voice rang out from inside: “How did the tea cup end up on the floor?” We shook our heads at the same time and met Mom’s angry eyes. Then, she looked at us and asked, “What are you two doing?” I said, “Cousin Michael gave us lollipops and told us to carry the black pots for him.” Mom’s eyes first became wide in confusion（困惑）. Then she laughed loudly, so hard that tears（眼泪）came down from her eyes. My sister and I looked at each other, having no idea what was going on. That evening, Mom described our carrying-black-pot action to the whole family, leaving everyone laughing loudly.
Now, many years have passed, but once my family get together, Mom never fails to retell this classic story of the “black pot”.

To prove the writer and his sister didn’t want to help.

He just wanted to find a reason to share his lollipops.
He made a mistake and was afraid to be punished.

ex.why: 「背黑锅」就是替人顶罪：Michael 打碎了茶杯，怕挨罚，想让两个小孩替他背锅。

ex.ev: Then she laughed loudly
ex.why: 妈妈先是生气（angry eyes），然后困惑（eyes became wide in confusion），最后大笑——C 图。

body: AI is already used for many things. It can help our lives in many ways, but people also have worries about it.
Recently, a famous band was found to be made by AI. Their music was made by AI.     16     This has caused heated discussion: does it matter if music is made by AI?

Some people think it should carry a warning. Music is more than just a tune (曲调) and words. It is connected to people’s life experiences and feelings, and often carries powerful messages.    17     So listeners have a right to know if they are listening to AI-made music.
Also, many artists are worried that their music is used to train AI without their permission. A number of famous musicians have spoken out about this.     18

While other people have different opinions, they believe that it doesn’t matter how music is made. As long as people like the music, do they really need to know how it was created? The final result is what counts.
19     Not everyone can use a recording studio (录音室) or buy expensive tools, but AI can fix this problem. People who use AI to make music shouldn’t be treated differently from other artists.

Also, using technology to make music isn’t new.     20     AI-made music is just the next step. If we put warnings on AI music, should we also put warnings on other music like new versions (版本) of old songs?
In a word, we’re supposed to find a balance. AI can be a helpful tool in music, but we must use it in a way that is honest and fair to everyone.

articles.title: Dorsa Yavarivafa, a 16-year-old badminton player, once had d
body: Dorsa Yavarivafa, a 16-year-old badminton player, once had dreams just like any other child. What made her different was that she never gave up her dream, even when life turned difficult.

Dorsa’s badminton journey started in a small park in Tehran. Every weekend, her father would take her there, patiently teaching her how to hold the racket and hit the shuttlecock. She was only six at that time. The sound of the shuttlecock flying across the park, along with her father’s encouraging smiles, became the happiest part of her life. As she grew older, she began to take part in local competitions. At ten, she won a medal in a junior match and kept it carefully in her badminton bag—as a reminder of her dream.

But two years later, her father died in an accident. Life became difficult. She had to leave her hometown with her mother. They traveled across several countries, sometimes sleeping in small houses and eating food from kind people.

Through those difficult times, Dorsa always carried her badminton bag with her. She didn’t have proper sports clothes, but that didn’t stop her. She ran on dusty roads and across quiet fields. “I didn’t have much, but I had my legs and my will,” she said. Her hard work finally paid off. Last year, she took part in the Paris Olympics. “It felt like a dream come true,” she smiled.

Now living in London, Dorsa continues to train and hopes to take part in more international games. She also serves as a volunteer for a charity that helps children. Last month, she visited a school for kids in need and taught them how to hold a racket and hit a shuttlecock. “I want to tell every child who feels lost,” she said, “never stop dreaming, and never give up.”

articles.title: Last month, something happened that changed how I think about myself.
body: Last month, something happened that changed how I think about myself.

It was the 800-meter race in PE class. I’m not a fast runner, but I wanted to look strong in front of my classmates. By the last round, my legs felt like noodles. But I kept telling myself, “Don’t stop. Don’t look weak.”
Then I fell-hard. About ten meters from the finish line, my foot caught on something. My knees hit the ground. My hands were bleeding. I heard some kids gasp (倒抽气).
My face burned red. I wanted to disappear.
For a moment, I thought about getting up quickly and pretending (假装) it didn’t hurt. But I couldn’t. It hurt too much. So I just sat on the ground, tears in my eyes.

Then my best friend Mia ran back. She didn’t ask if I was OK-she already knew I wasn’t. She just sat down right next to me. Other classmates came together. Some brought water. One girl said, “I fell here last year too. It really hurts.”
When I got to the nurse’s office, I sat thinking. I had spent so much energy trying to look strong. I was afraid to seem weak. But when I showed my real self-hurt, crying, falling-they helped me.
The next day at lunch, I told Mia, “I felt so embarrassed (尴尬的).”
She laughed-not at me, but with me. “You’re human” she said. “Remember the last time when I fell down in front of everyone?”
We laughed together. Then she added, “You know what? I actually like you more now. Before, you always seemed so perfect. Now I feel like I know the real you.”
For the first time, I didn’t pretend to be fine. I talked about my fears and embarrassing moments. She shared hers too. We felt closer than ever.
Now I understand something important. Trying to be perfect all the time is tiring. But when I show my real self, I feel free.

opts: To ask what happened to her.
To show she understood her feelings.

ex.why: 她不问，只是坐在旁边陪着——她懂作者的感受。

ex.why: 顺序：800 米比赛开始（b）→ 摔倒受伤（a）→ 想爬起来假装没事（e）→ Mia 跑回来坐在旁边（c）→ 其他同学送水（d）。

opts: She felt they became even closer.

ex.ev: We felt closer than ever.
ex.why: 聊完后两人比以前更亲近了。

qs.stem: What is the lesson the writer learned from this experience?
opts: Friends should never laugh at each other.
It’s better to hide your feelings from others.
Friendship is more important than winning races.
Being real brings more happiness than being perfect.

ex.why: 一直装完美很累，做真实的自己反而轻松——真实比完美更让人快乐。

articles.title: Taking a great photo isn’t easy and there are lots of things
body: Taking a great photo isn’t easy and there are lots of things to consider. How do you choose and organize your subjects within your photo?     16     Here is some advice from experts.

First, find a focus. When shooting, ask yourself, “What’s the focus?” If you’re taking a picture of a crowded street, choose a subject that catches your eye.     17     In a field landscape, the focus could be a big tree.

18     Avoid placing the subject in the middle. Position it on the left or right. Divide your photo into a three-by-three grid (网格), and place the focus at one of the central square’s corners for a better composition.
Create colorful contrasts (对比). Colors stand out more with contrast.     19     They will stand out more if they are taken beside a gray stone wall, or photographed against a bright blue sky.

Try different ways. Move around and try taking it from different directions, above, or below. For example, if you photograph a building from a plane, it looks tiny. But a photo of the same building looking up from the street makes it look huge.     20
Practice makes perfect. Try everything for the perfect photo.

opts: It can tell a different story.
Think about the focus, colors, light and more.
It can be a person in bright colors
When shooting yellow flowers, don’t fill your picture with them.

articles.title: Zhang Xue was born in a poor village in Hunan in 1987.
body: Zhang Xue was born in a poor village in Hunan in 1987. His family did not have much money. When he was 14, he left school and began to work in a small motorcycle (摩托车) repair shop. He loved motorcycles and dreamed of becoming a famous rider one day.

In 2006, Zhang Xue was 19 years old. He heard that a TV team was filming near his town. He wanted to appear on TV, so he rode his motorcycle over 100 kilometres in heavy rain to follow them. He showed some difficult riding skills along the way. Finally, he appeared on TV. After that, more people began to know this young man.

Later, Zhang Xue moved to Chongqing for better chances. In 2017, he started a motorcycle company with friends. However, Zhang Xue left the company because he wanted to make better and faster motorcycles with his own ideas.

In 2024, Zhang Xue started his own company, ZXMOTO. He worked day and night with his team. In just four months, they sold over 10,000 motorcycles. In March 2026, something amazing happened. His motorcycle won first place at a world race in Portugal (葡萄牙). It beat top companies like Yamaha and Ducati by nearly 4 seconds. This was the first time a Chinese motorcycle won such an important world race. Chinese people felt proud.

Today, people call Zhang Xue the “Lei Jun of Motorcycles”. He still talks with his customers online every week. He often says, “I don’t like business. I just love making motorcycles.” His story tells us that dreams can come true if we work hard and never give up.

articles.title: Grandma Kay was in the kitchen.
body: Grandma Kay was in the kitchen. She had just taken apple pies out of the oven.
Carrie, a ten-year-old girl, and her mom came in. Carrie said, “Wow, those smell good, Grandma! May I have one, please?”
Carrie and her mom shared a pie. Some crumbs (食物碎屑) fell on the floor. As Carrie swept them up, she said, “If we had a little cat, it would eat the crumbs.  ▲ ”
“Well! Raising a cat means a lot of work! I have to say that there’s nothing cuter than a cat, though,” said Grandma Kay.
“I love cat stories. I guess I just love cats. It’s my dream to keep a cat at home. Can we get one, please?” Carrie looked hopefully at her mother and said.
Carrie’s mother smiled and didn’t say anything.
The girl continued, “Mom, tell me about the cat you used to have. How did you get it?”

“We went to the animal shelter (收容所) in our town. While we were sitting and waiting, a little white cat picked us out, not the other way round. She crawled up the chair and then lay on my leg, looking at me with her shining eyes. She won our hearts right away,” said Carrie’s mother, laughing.
“We can agree that we all like cats, right?” said Carrie.
“Yes!” Carrie’s mother and grandma said.
“Would we all like to have a cat?” Carrie asked.
“Yes,” replied Mom.
“No. A little cat needs more attention than I could give it,” said Grandma.
“I know why Grandma doesn’t want a cat: she knows she’ll end up taking care of it when I’m at school or you’re at work,” Carrie said to her mother.
Then Carrie turned to Grandma. “I’ll feed the cat, clean up the room, and play with it after school and at weekends. I’ll be responsible for the cat.”
“I believe that you will help. Now let’s look forward to our new life with a cat,” Grandma nodded and smiled.
Carrie jumped excitedly. She hugged Grandma and her mother.

qs.stem: Which of the following can be put in  ▲ ?
opts: A cat is lying on the kitchen floor.
Is it a silly idea to keep a cat at home?
A little cat might make a mess here.
Wouldn’t it be great to have a little cat?

ex.ev: If we had a little cat, it would eat the crumbs.
ex.why: 接着说 D「有只小猫多好啊？」——她想养猫。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “crawled” mean?
opts: Dropped down from a higher level.

ex.ev: She crawled up the chair and then lay on my leg
ex.why: 小猫爬上椅子——crawl 是用腿慢慢往前爬。

qs.stem: Why did Grandma refuse to keep a cat at first?
opts: Because they couldn’t make room for it.
Because she didn’t like any kinds of cats.
Because they already had a pet at home.
Because she knew she had to take care of it.

ex.ev: she knows she’ll end up taking care of it when I’m at school or you’re at work
ex.why: 奶奶知道最后得由她来照顾猫。

qs.stem: What will probably be written in the next paragraph?
opts: Carrie helped at the animal shelter.
There was a pet cat in Carrie’s family.
Carrie decided to raise a dog instead.
Carrie worked hard to be an animal doctor.

ex.ev: Now let’s look forward to our new life with a cat,
ex.why: 奶奶同意了，接下来家里应该有了一只猫。

qs.stem: What is the best title for the text?

ex.ev: It’s my dream to keep a cat at home.
ex.why: 全文讲 Carrie 想养猫的愿望。

articles.title: A lot of kids dream of becoming Internet stars.
body: A lot of kids dream of becoming Internet stars. Every day, they post videos online and hope to become new Internet stars.
16     Lia Marie Johnson once posted a funny video of herself eating something. More than a million people watched it! Should you try to become an Internet star? Read on to help you decide.
Bethany Mota is one of YouTube’s biggest stars.     17     Today, she’s 31, and she has over 9 million fans.

People who post the most popular video on YouTube can make thousands of dollars. Experts have guessed that Bethany makes about $40,000 a month. She also has her own clothing line. Bethany won a Teen Choice Award, and she appeared on the TV show Dancing with the Stars.     18     “I’m my own boss,” Bethany says.

On the other hand, putting videos of yourself on the Internet can be risky.     19     A few years ago, a girl named Rebecca Black posted a music video called Friday. Many people hated it. Rebecca was bullied (欺凌) so badly that she left school without finishing her studies.

20     In fact, few people make any money on the Internet. And making videos takes a lot of time and hard work. Bethany says that even a five-minute video takes days to create. That doesn’t leave much time for schoolwork, friends... or just being a kid.

opts: Becoming an Internet star isn’t easy, either.
There’s another benefit of being an Internet star.
In fact, some have already become famous online.
Being bullied online is one of the biggest risks.
She was 14 when she started posting videos about clothes and more.

16.ev: Lia Marie Johnson once posted a funny video of herself eating something.
16.why: C「事实上有些人已经在网上出名了」，后面举例。

17.ev: Today, she’s 31, and she has over 9 million fans.
17.why: E「她 14 岁开始发服装视频」，和后面的 Today 形成对比。

18.ev: I’m my own boss
18.why: 前面讲赚钱，B「当网红还有另一个好处」：自己给自己当老板。

19.ev: Rebecca was bullied (欺凌) so badly that she left school without finishing her studies.
19.why: 举了被欺凌的例子，D「网络欺凌是最大的风险之一」。

20.ev: In fact, few people make any money on the Internet.
20.why: 很少有人赚到钱、做视频很辛苦，A「当网红也不容易」。

articles.title: One day, a young king went out to hunt deer when he accident
body: One day, a young king went out to hunt deer when he accidentally became separated from his companions. Wandering (漫步) around, the king saw a hut (小屋) surrounded (围绕) by a garden, and a young woman was tending the garden.

The king spoke to her, saying, “Tell me, what plants are you growing here?” “I am raising pumpkins as you can see,” the woman replied. She had a quick glance at the pile of pumpkins behind her and gave a quick smile to the king. He couldn’t help but smile back.
As the king returned toward the city, an idea began to grow in him. He thought, “Perhaps I might think up a test to see just how smart this young woman might be.”

The king then ordered a soldier to carry a new jar (罐子) without handles (把手) to the young woman’s house. The soldier’s orders were to tell the young woman that the jar was from the king, and that she was to put a whole pumpkin inside the jar with a small opening at the top, and that both the jar and the pumpkin must remain whole.

The young woman returned a message to the king that such a task might take some time. Indeed, it was several months before the young woman arrived at the palace. In her hands, she held the same jar, and sure enough, an entire pumpkin sat inside it. The king had completely no idea how she could have brought this about!

This was her answer to the riddle: She had placed a pumpkin bud (花蕾), which was still connected to a vine (藤蔓) in the ground, inside the jar through its small opening. Over time, the pumpkin bud grew into a full-sized pumpkin.

qs.stem: Which one has a similar meaning to the underlined word “tending”?

ex.ev: a young woman was tending the garden.
ex.why: 年轻女子在照料园子——tend 就是 take care of。

qs.stem: What was the woman planting in Paragraph 2?

ex.ev: I am raising pumpkins as you can see,
ex.why: 她在种南瓜。

qs.stem: What task did the king’s soldier give to the young woman?
opts: To grow the biggest pumpkin in the land.
To bring a pumpkin bud to the palace.
To put a whole pumpkin into a jar with a small opening without breaking.
To fix a jar without handles.

ex.ev: she was to put a whole pumpkin inside the jar with a small opening at the top, and that both the jar and the pumpkin must remain whole.
ex.why: 把整个南瓜放进小口罐子，罐子和南瓜都不能破。

qs.stem: Why did the young woman say the task might take some time?
opts: Because she wanted to refuse the king’s request.
Because she needed to find a special jar.
Because she was afraid to see the king again.
Because she had to wait for the pumpkin inside the jar to grow.

ex.ev: Over time, the pumpkin bud grew into a full-sized pumpkin.
ex.why: 她把花苞放进罐子，要等它长成大南瓜，所以需要时间。

qs.stem: What is the main lesson of the story?
opts: True wisdom often lies in creative thinking and patience.
It is important to listen to the king’s orders.
Gardening needs a lot of skills.
Kings should not test ordinary people.

ex.ev: This was her answer to the riddle
ex.why: 巧妙的想法加上几个月的耐心等待——真正的智慧在于创造性思维和耐心。

articles.title: February brings long and cold days, and it also gives us a s
body: February brings long and cold days, and it also gives us a small amount of hope. It means that we have survived (幸存) the cold temperatures of December and January and are waiting for March to welcome spring. What’s more, February doesn’t last too long. It’s two to three days shorter than every other month. But why does February only have 28 and sometimes 29 days?

February’s 28 days dated back to (追溯到) the second king of Ancient Rome, Numa Pompilius. Before he became king, Rome’s calendar had just 10 months. It began in March and ended in December. The Romans didn’t give names to what is now January and February. This period was not important to them because it had nothing to do with the harvest. After Numa became king, he decided to make the calendar more accurate (精确的). His new calendar contained (包含) 355 days in a year. Two more months were also added to the end of the calendar: January and February.

As the Romans thought even numbers were unlucky, Numa wanted to avoid having them in his calendar. As such, each month had either 29 or 31 days. But to reach 355 days, one month had to be an even number. February was chosen to be that unlucky month with 28 days.

In 45 BCE, Julius Caesar asked an expert to create a new sun-based calendar. Ten days were added to each year: before seven months had 29 days; now, four of them had 30, and the other three had 31. However, the 28-day February stuck and never changed, except for a leap year (闰年)   once every four years.

qs.stem: How do people feel about February from Paragraph 1?
opts: It is the coldest and longest month.
It gives people hope because spring is coming and it is short.
It is an unlucky month without any festivals.
It is not important because it has nothing to do with farming.

ex.ev: It means that we have survived (幸存) the cold temperatures of December and January and are waiting for March to welcome spring.
ex.why: 二月意味着春天快来了，而且它比别的月份短——给人希望。

qs.stem: What was the main change King Numa Pompilius made to the Roman calendar?
opts: He made the calendar begin in January.
He created a new sun-based calendar with 365 days.
He changed all months to have either 30 or 31 days.
He added the months of January and February to a 10-month calendar.

ex.ev: Two more months were also added to the end of the calendar: January and February.
ex.why: 他在原来 10 个月的历法后面加了一月和二月。

qs.stem: Which is “an even number” according to Paragraph 3?

ex.ev: As the Romans thought even numbers were unlucky, Numa wanted to avoid having them in his calendar.
ex.why: even number 是偶数：每月 29 或 31 天（奇数），只有二月是 28 天（偶数）。2 是偶数。

qs.stem: What can we know about Julius Caesar’s new calendar from the text?
opts: It changed the names of the months.
It made February have 29 days every year.
It kept February as a 28-day month except for leap years.
It completely changed the lengths of all months.

ex.ev: However, the 28-day February stuck and never changed, except for a leap year (闰年)
ex.why: 二月一直是 28 天，只有闰年例外。

qs.stem: Which is the best title for the text?
opts: The story of the Roman holidays.
Old beliefs and the Roman calendar.

ex.ev: But why does February only have 28 and sometimes 29 days?
ex.why: 第一段提出问题，全文回答为什么二月这么短。

articles.title: I felt nervous when getting home from school.
body: I felt nervous when getting home from school. Every day, my room was something different.

As I entered the house, Mom greeted me with a smile. It seemed as if nothing was wrong. But I was still doubtful about it. Yesterday, around the mouth of my favorite figurine (小雕像) was some chocolate. Clearly, Callie, who had just turned three, had enjoyed the chocolate so much that she wanted to share it with my figurine.

I looked around for Callie. I didn’t see her, but I heard the TV playing in the other room. As I checked the family room, I found it was pretty messy. There were toys all over the floor, but none of them seemed to be mine. “Maybe she didn’t enter my room today.”
I pushed my room door open and was shocked to see the mess! There were a few headless dolls, some broken blocks and a couple of toys with juice. “She did it again!” I shouted in anger.

Mom ran up to me. She promised to put a special lock on my door. Knowing that soon my room would truly belong to me, I felt better. However, I decided to tell my little sister how she had made life unpleasant for me.
“Callie…” I started when I got to the family room.

“Hooray!” she shouted. Callie jumped off the sofa and hugged my knees with such happiness that I could only look down at her and smile. After all, she was only three and learning about the world in her own way. And she always chose to explore and mess up my room because she loved me, her big sister!

qs.stem: Why did the writer feel nervous coming home every day?
opts: Her room might be changed again.

ex.ev: Every day, my room was something different.
ex.why: 每天回家房间都会变个样——怕又被弄乱。

qs.stem: What can we infer from the chocolate around the writer’s figurine?
opts: Callie didn’t like to eat chocolate.
Callie had entered the writer’s room.
Callie took the chocolate from the writer’s room.
Callie wanted to share the chocolate with the writer.

ex.ev: Yesterday, around the mouth of my favorite figurine (小雕像) was some chocolate.
ex.why: 雕像嘴边有巧克力，说明 Callie 进过作者的房间。

qs.stem: What did Mom promise to do to solve the problem?
opts: Put a special lock on her door.

ex.ev: She promised to put a special lock on my door.
ex.why: 妈妈答应给她的房门装一把特别的锁。

qs.stem: What finally stopped the writer from being angry?

ex.ev: Callie jumped off the sofa and hugged my knees with such happiness that I could only look down at her and smile.
ex.why: 妹妹开心地抱住她，她只能笑了。

qs.stem: What does the writer realize at last?
opts: Callie’s mess showed she loved her.
It’s better to stay away from Callie.
Being three is a good excuse for messing up.
Young age is a good excuse for making mistakes.

ex.ev: And she always chose to explore and mess up my room because she loved me, her big sister!
ex.why: 妹妹总弄乱她的房间，是因为爱她这个姐姐。

cand: adj. 令人不快的；难受的
