articles.title: Fifteen-year-old Leo is a lover of the outdoors.
body: Fifteen-year-old Leo is a lover of the outdoors. Every Saturday, he visits his grandparents’ farm and helps them with the farm work.

One Saturday, after finishing planting tomatoes in the vegetable garden, Grandma suggested taking a walk in the nearby forest. The forest was beautiful and full of life. Leo was excited to explore it until he noticed some rubbish.
“Grandma, look! Someone has left their rubbish here,” Leo said.
“That’s not good,” said Grandma. “Rubbish can harm wildlife. Let’s clean it up.”
Together, they picked up all the rubbish and placed it into a bag Grandma carried.
“________ Don’t they care about the environment?” Leo asked.
“Sometimes people just don’t think about the results of their behavior,” Grandma replied. “But every small effort counts. If we all do our part, we can make a big difference.”

Feeling encouraged, Leo decided to raise awareness (意识) in his school about protecting nature. The following week, he shared his idea with his teacher, Mrs. Thompson. With her support, Leo organized a clean-up activity at the local park. All his classmates took part and collected a lot of rubbish, making the park a better place.

After the clean-up, everyone felt a sense of pride. Leo suggested that they do this every month and help protect wildlife. Being excited about the idea, the group discussed future projects like planting flowers for butterflies and building birdhouses. At that moment, Leo fully understood that when people work together, they can make a big difference to nature.
[图:reading/bc059fe8/image2.png]

qs.stem: What does Leo usually spend his Saturdays doing?

ex.ev: Every Saturday, he visits his grandparents’ farm and helps them with the farm work.
ex.why: 每周六去爷爷奶奶的农场帮忙干活。

qs.stem: Which sentence can be put in “________”?
opts: What else can we do to help?
How can animals mistake rubbish for food?
How about putting up a sign to warn people?

ex.ev: Sometimes people just don’t think about the results of their behavior,
ex.why: 奶奶回答人们没想到行为的后果，所以 Leo 问的是 A「人们为什么乱扔垃圾？」

qs.stem: How did Leo and his classmates feel after the clean-up activity?

ex.ev: After the clean-up, everyone felt a sense of pride.
ex.why: 大家都觉得自豪。

qs.stem: What is the correct order of the following events? a. Leo and his grandma cleaned up the rubbish in the forest. b. Leo and his classmates cleaned up the local park. c. Leo planted tomatoes on his grandparents’ farm. d. Leo talked to his teacher about his idea.

ex.why: 顺序：种西红柿（c）→ 和奶奶在森林捡垃圾（a）→ 跟老师说想法（d）→ 和同学清理公园（b）。

qs.stem: What does the story mainly want to tell us?
opts: We should work together to protect nature.
Volunteering is a great way to make a difference.
Animals are our friends and we should protect them.
Our family members and friends are always there to help.

ex.ev: when people work together, they can make a big difference to nature.
ex.why: 原文最后点明：大家一起努力就能保护好自然。

articles.src: 上蔡县塔桥镇第一初级中学2026年九年级中招练习试卷
articles.title: Music can make us feel many different things.
body: Music can make us feel many different things. Some songs make us feel happy, while others make us feel sad or calm. Music can also remind us of special times in our lives. For example, we might remember a song that played on our birthdays, or when we first met a good friend. These songs become special because they are connected to our feelings and memories.

But music doesn’t just help us remember. Scientists now think it might also change how we remember things. In a study, researchers asked people to read some short stories. These stories were not happy or sad—they were just normal. The next day, the people listened to happy music, sad music, or no music while they were asked to think about the stories again. While this happened, a machine called fMRI was used to see how their brains worked.

On the third day, the people were asked to recall the same stories again, but without any music. The scientists wondered if the music had changed what people remembered. And it did. When people listened to happy music, they remembered the stories in a happier way. When they listened to sad music, they remembered the stories as sadder ones. Even without music, their memories stayed changed.

The brain scans (扫描) showed that music made certain parts of the brain more active. These parts help us feel emotions (情感) and remember things. This means music can really change how we feel about our past. It doesn’t just help us remember—it changes the memory itself.

This may explain why music from special times, like a wedding or a holiday, can make us feel strong emotions. Some scientists say music might one day help people who feel sad, such as people with depression (抑郁症).
[图:reading/bc059fe8/image3.png]

qs.stem: Why does the writer mention songs from birthdays or first meeting friends?
opts: To say that people like music at parties.
To show music makes people feel relaxed.
To explain how music connects to memories.
To tell people what songs to play on special days.

ex.ev: These songs become special because they are connected to our feelings and memories.
ex.why: 举生日歌、初遇朋友的歌，是为了说明音乐和记忆连在一起。

qs.stem: What does the underlined word “recall” in Paragraph 3 mean?

ex.ev: On the third day, the people were asked to recall the same stories again, but without any music.
ex.why: 让他们再回想一遍那些故事——recall 是「回想」，即 look back。

qs.stem: What can we learn from the researchers’ study?
opts: Music helps people forget bad things.
Music always brings back old memories.
Music makes normal stories easy to remember.
Music can change how we feel about past events.

ex.ev: This means music can really change how we feel about our past.
ex.why: 研究说明音乐能改变我们对过去事情的感受。

qs.stem: What’s the writer’s purpose of using some scientists’ words at the end of the text?
opts: To tell why music is important in life.
To introduce a possible use of music in the future.
To prove that music is the best treatment for depression.
To encourage people to listen to music when they feel sad.

ex.ev: Some scientists say music might one day help people who feel sad, such as people with depression (抑郁症).
ex.why: might one day——介绍音乐将来可能的用处。

qs.stem: Which is the best title for the text?
opts: Music’s Influence on Teen Mental Health

ex.ev: It doesn’t just help us remember—it changes the memory itself.
ex.why: 全文讲音乐怎样影响情感和记忆——音乐在塑造情感中的作用。

cand: adj. 活跃的；积极参与的

You will have a chance to act in these plays. Our teachers will give you advice on how to improve your acting skills. Cooking Club Cooking Club is about learning new recipes and perfecting cooking skills. You will learn one new recipe every week. You can try it out at home, and then bring the dish you cooked to a club meeting for everyone to try. We also discuss cooking skills and watch cooking shows at the meetings. body: With Children’s Day on its way, it’s time to start thinking about everyone’s favorite topic: gifts!     16     Coming from the US, I have found gift - giving to be quite different in China compared with my home country.

17     In the US, the person who gives the gift will often want to see the person who gets the gift immediately (立刻地) open the present.     18     In China, however, it’s more polite to thank the person for the gift but privately open it later.

19     Although people in the US might give money to their children, it is usually done very secretly with the money put in a card and not discussed out loud. In China, the practice is much opener in a flashy red envelope (红包).

Finally, the monetary (金钱的) value of the gift can play a big role in China in ways that are different from the US.     20     But in China, it can make the person who accepts the gift feel embarrassed due to a sense of having to return the favor (恩惠) in the future to the person who gives the gift.
So, the next time you give a gift to somebody, remember that culture and meaning are part of every action we take.

articles.title: Last summer, I went to visit my cousin in a small mountain village.
body: Last summer, I went to visit my cousin in a small mountain village. The village was quiet and beautiful, with green hills around it. However, something unusual caught my attention.

Behind my cousin’s house, there was a little girl who always sat alone under a big tree. She never played with other children. Day after day, she just sat there, drawing on the ground with a small stick. I asked my cousin about her. He told me her name was Mei, and she couldn’t hear or speak. Most villagers ignored her because they thought she was different.

One sunny afternoon, I saw Mei drawing again. Her pictures were amazing — birds, flowers and a bright sun with long rays (光线). I walked to her quietly and gave her a box of colored pens. She looked up at me, surprised. For a moment, she didn’t move. Then she smiled widely and began to draw a picture for me. We didn’t say a word, but I felt we understood each other.

Day by day, we became good friends. I taught her to write simple words on paper, and she taught me that happiness does not need sound. Her world was silent, but it was full of colors and warmth. She showed me that a person’s value is not in what he doesn’t have, but in what he can give.

When I left the village, Mei gave me her drawing of two hands holding together. I still keep it on my desk. That summer, I learned that kindness can break down any wall. And sometimes, the quietest people have the most colorful hearts.

body: Technology is not just about speed and fun — it can also be about the changes in life. Technology is helping people with disabilities in China.     16     It can be things like special equipment (设施) to help them move or use computers, making websites and apps easier to use, getting help from doctors far away, or making homes easier to live in. The goal is to give people with disabilities more freedom and make things easier for them.     17
The leader of the China Disabled Persons’ Federation said that technology is very important for improving the lives of people with disabilities.     18

China is doing a lot to help people with disabilities find jobs and make sure they can go everywhere easily. There are about 85 million people with disabilities in China.     19     Also, over 100,000 disabled students have gone to college. China is also helping children with disabilities. Over 440,000 children got help in 2024 to get better. The government is making it easier for those people to get the care they need.

What’s more, China is making changes to homes for families that have low incomes.     20     So far, about 1.18 million homes have been changed to make them more accessible (可进入的) for the people who live there.

articles.title: It was very hard to describe how sad and helpless the four men felt.
body: It was very hard to describe how sad and helpless the four men felt. They had come so close to rescuing (拯救) the woman, but still could not stop what was happening. Sir Francis stood quietly, biting (咬) his fingers nervously. Passepartout was full of anger and began shouting. The Indian man had to try to calm him down. Mr. Fogg, however, looked just as calm as ever. He didn’t seem to feel any fear or sadness.
“I think we should go now,” said Sir Francis in a low voice.
The Indian man nodded slowly. “There is nothing more we can do.”
Passepartout did not speak. He kept looking at the fire and the people around it.
“Let us wait a little longer,” said Fogg. “I don’t need to be in Allahabad before tomorrow morning. I still have some time.”
“But what are you hoping for?” asked Sir Francis. “Soon, the sun will rise. And when it does, she will be burned.”
“The chance we are waiting for may come at the last moment,” answered Fogg with the same quiet voice.

Sir Francis could not understand what Fogg was thinking. What kind of plan could this cold Englishman have? Did he want to run into the crowd and take the woman away just as the fire began? That would be very dangerous. But Fogg was not a foolish man, so Sir Francis decided to trust him and wait.
The young Indian led them back to a safer place behind the trees, where they could see everything but not be seen.

Passepartout sat on a low branch and started to think. At first, he thought his idea was silly. “It won’t work,” he told himself. But after a while, he changed his mind. “Maybe it’s our only chance,” he said. Quietly, he began to move along the tree branches, which bent (倾斜) toward the ground.

articles.title: Leo had a music player that he loved more than anything.
body: Leo had a music player that he loved more than anything. It was a gift from his grandfather, filled with hundreds of songs. Every day after school, Leo would put on his earphones and lose himself in a world of melodies (旋律). He dreamed of becoming a musician one day.
However, Leo never let anyone else touch the player. He was afraid it might get broken or lost.
One afternoon, his classmate Sam saw him listening to music during break. “Your player looks so cool! Can I try it for a minute?” Sam asked hopefully.
Leo shook his head quickly. “Sorry, it’s very special to me,” he said, holding it tightly (紧紧地).
Sam nodded in understanding, but Leo could see the disappointment in his eyes. That night, Leo’s father noticed he was quiet. “What’s wrong, Leo?” he asked. Leo explained what happened.
“You know,” his father said gently, “music is a gift that becomes more beautiful when shared.”
“But what if something happens to my music player?” Leo worried.
“_________,” his father replied.
The next day, Leo took a deep breath and walked up to Sam. “Hey, do you still want to try my music player?” he asked nervously.
Sam’s eyes widened. “Really? Thanks, Leo!”
Leo carefully handed him the player and showed him how to use it. Sam’s face broke into a huge smile as he listened. “This is amazing! I’ve never heard such clear sound before!”
A few days later, Sam returned the player. “Thank you for trusting me,” he said. “I made a playlist of my favorite songs—maybe you’ d like to listen sometime.”

Leo felt warm inside. He realized that by sharing, he hadn’t lost anything—instead, he’d gained a friend who loved music as much as he did. From then on, Leo and Sam often listened to music together, discovering new songs and sharing their dreams.

articles.title: Have you noticed the new and cool expressions online?
body: Have you noticed the new and cool expressions online? They are fun ways people talk and share life. These expressions can be about games, feelings, or even food—perfect for chatting (聊天) with your classmates.   Want to learn about some of them? Let’s take a look!

Lanzhou hand-pulled cats Some people make a fun “game” with cats. They pretend (假装)that cats are Lanzhou hand-pulled noodles. First, they softly knead (揉) the cat. Then, they softly pull it. Finally, they pretend to put it in a bowl. The “Lanzhou hand-pulled cat” is ready! Enjoy it to feel happy!

Out of ideas People use this expression when they are having bad luck or facing problems but don’t know how to deal with them. It’s like a joke they tell themselves. It shows they feel OK and just accept the situation instead of getting worried. Some young people have this attitude (态度) towards the challenges in life.

Basic This is a popular idea about life. It started with a piece of advice on dressing: “If your top is basic, your bottom should not be.” After this idea became popular online, people used it in different ways. For example, with the meal: if breakfast is basic, then dinner should not be. Now, this idea shows how young people enjoy life in a fun way.

articles.title: Jennifer was working on her craft (手工艺品) when Mom entered the room.
body: Jennifer was working on her craft (手工艺品) when Mom entered the room.
“Will you take it to your new school tomorrow?” she asked softly.
Jennifer had butterflies in her stomach. She had been trying hard to forget about starting third grade in a new town. Mom noticed her expression of worry.
“New-school nerves (神经紧张), right? But you’ll make all kinds of friends just by being yourself.” Mom comforted (安慰) Jennifer and kissed her good night.

The next morning, Jennifer decided to take Bouncy, her handmade snake, to school. Throughout the first half of the day, it helped knowing that Bounce was nearby. Jennifer found enough confidence to get through greetings without turning bright red. Jennifer was feeling pretty good, until she checked on Bouncy after break. He was missing!
It was now lunchtime. How could she face so many strangers in the dining hall? While lining up, she noticed a colorful poster for several after-school clubs.
Just then, a girl walked over, holding Bouncy. “Hey, this fell out of your schoolbag. I’m Sophia.”
Jennifer took Bouncy back, and said, “Um, thanks. I’m Jennifer.”
“Looks like you made that by yourself,” Sophia said.
“Yes, I love making crafts,” Jennifer replied.
“Could you show me how to make one?” Sophia asked, smiling.
“Sure,” Jennifer smiled back, and then noticed the lunch line started moving. “Guess I have to go. But ... do you want to sit together with me?”
“Yes,” Sophia hissed (发嘶嘶声) like a snake, making them both laugh.

After school, when they sat together, more kids came together, interested in learning. “Maybe we could make crafts this weekend,” Jennifer suggested, but everyone was busy. Sophia sighed (叹息道), “Too bad we can’t do it after school.”
“Of course we can!” Thinking of the poster, Jennifer suddenly had an idea. She would like to talk to her teacher Mrs. Miller the following day.
Two weeks later in the art room, the Craft Club held its first meeting. “What are we going to make today?” Sophia asked.根据材料内容选择最佳答案：

body: The Week Junior
Are you more likely to be kind to others when someone has done something nice for you? This is called “pay it forward”.     36

What does “pay it forward” mean? This means doing a good thing for someone because another person has done something kind for you. So if you spill (洒出) your drink and someone helps you clean it up, you pay their kindness forward by helping someone else.     37     In this way you’re helping to send kindness out into the world, which is called “the butterfly effect (蝴蝶效应)”.

Why does kindness matter? Being kind to others helps everyone feel happier and more connected. When you do something nice, it can make someone’s day better and it also makes you feel good inside.     38     It also makes you feel less stressed (焦虑的) and improves your health condition. Besides, making others feel valued and liked can also start or continue the butterfly effect.

39     Kindness doesn’t have to be a big, great act. It simply means being kind to someone just because you can. So think about small actions that might encourage others to be kind.     40     Praise can really brighten someone’s day. You can also reach out to a friend who might be feeling sad. Even a smile or “hi” helps.

opts: How can you pay it forward?
You can say something nice to a classmate.
It can make your school or community a better place.
This could be helping neighbors carry their shopping bags.
Being kind to others by helping for free makes you happier.
